title: Qualify and version the shared agent lifecycle contract
body:
## Outcome
Define one evidence-backed event and session vocabulary for local Codex Desktop, Codex CLI, and Claude Code that every device integration can consume.

## Scope
This owns shared provider qualification previously planned in Pixoo #29. Pixoo retains consumer adoption in [divoom-app-upgrade#29](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/29). Use the existing Nanoleaf behavior and tests as evidence, without treating its Codex-specific assumptions as universal.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Record accessible installed client versions, primary documentation, event/payload/ordering identifiers, delivery support, and parent/subagent evidence. Distinguish documented, observed, unsupported and inaccessible signals; documentation/fixtures do not establish live compatibility.
- [ ] Define a versioned runtime-validated metadata envelope with provider, host/source, session and available turn identity, event identity or deterministic deduplication fallback, event kind, observation time and evidenced parent relationships.
- [ ] Keep activity, continuing questions, blocked input/approval, turn-ended notices, interruption/runtime end, acknowledgment and freshness distinct. A turn ending proves neither success nor readership.
- [ ] Represent each top-level session separately, including concurrent sessions in one project. Aggregate only attributable children; unknown parentage and unavailable counts stay explicit.
- [ ] Define optional Codex Desktop unread evidence and per-consumer notice policies. Preserve Nanoleaf's existing read behavior during migration; Pixoo dismissal remains monitor-only and never edits agent read state.
- [ ] Allow only lifecycle metadata, identifiers, timestamps and explicit user-chosen labels. Exclude prompts, transcripts, tool arguments/results, auto-copied titles, credentials and unrelated private paths before transmission and persistence.
- [ ] Specify bounded nonblocking fail-open producer delivery, timeout/overflow behavior and silent observational output. Monitoring cannot approve, deny, change permissions or hold an agent action waiting.
- [ ] Provide fixtures for new/old turns, ongoing questions, blocked input, resolution, turn end, interruption, children, duplicates, missing IDs, late events and unsupported evidence. Define required-client stop conditions.
- [ ] Publish vocabulary, schema compatibility rules and source/version evidence in hub documentation and issue-linked OpenSpec artifacts. Mark all live-client gaps for [agent-device-hub#8](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/8) and device acceptance.

## Dependencies
- [agent-device-hub#1](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/1)

## Verification
Schema/fixture validation and a primary-source capability matrix using synthetic metadata. Inspect accessible installed client artifacts read-only; no settings changes or agent launches.

## Delivery target
Source-only, including configuration/installation tooling. Personal setup, agent launches and physical tests need separate explicit authorization.

## Planning and delivery
GitHub owns scope, acceptance, dependencies and status. Follow this repository's AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. The current request authorizes this backlog definition and repository setup; it does not authorize implementing these future features.

Before implementation, prepare the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change at openspec/changes/gh-2-agent-lifecycle-contract/. Verify the identity and applicable design requirements first.

## Codex-first goal alignment, 2026-09-07

Part of [the shared Codex-integration goal](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/32). First deliver automatic Codex task integration and manual frontend controls for that integration. General agent-independent device control is [a later phase](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31). Existing local MCP delivery and independently owned work keep their scope. Shared provider contracts remain extensible; retain existing Claude criteria and report Codex milestone evidence separately rather than falsely closing outstanding provider acceptance.

### Additional acceptance criteria
- [ ] Qualify Codex Desktop and CLI on the supported Windows/WSL paths first, including installed-version gaps. Define shared labels, task/project identity and notice acknowledgment needed by manual integration controls without exporting private Codex metadata.
- [ ] Supply the event semantics and supported path matrix needed to establish cold/warm hook baselines in [performance qualification](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/30); document hard fail-open behavior before runtime implementation.

This update defines backlog work only. It does not start implementation, change an active installation or grant device-test authority. Existing OpenSpec identities, validation and UI/physical acceptance gates remain.

title: Implement the reusable agent-state core and provider emitters
body:
## Outcome
Interpret agent observations once and expose durable, trustworthy session snapshots to multiple device consumers.

## Scope
Implement shared TypeScript packages and bounded provider emitters from [agent-device-hub#2](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/2). The first production host is Pixoo's existing backend in [divoom-app-upgrade#31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/31); this issue does not create a second backend or install hooks.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Implement the qualified provider mappings and deterministic reducer with injectable time. Namespace state by provider/source/session and retain available turn and evidenced child identity.
- [x] Preserve continuing questions, blocked attention, turn-ended notices, interruption and unavailable evidence independently. A new turn or explicit monitor acknowledgment clears only the intended monitor notice.
- [x] Reject stale prior-turn changes, deduplicate retries and make child counts stable under concurrent, missing-ID and reordered observations. Unknown ordering remains visible as uncertainty.
- [x] Expose session observation age separately from collector health. Five minutes without session evidence marks observations uncertain, not failed. Restart restores previously active sessions as uncertain until fresh evidence.
- [x] Persist state, chosen labels and undismissed notices through the host's storage boundary. Bound the diagnostic journal to 24 hours or 10,000 events, whichever comes first, without deleting current state or notices.
- [x] Validate/strip non-allowlisted fields before delivery and persistence. Privacy-canary tests must prove excluded payloads do not appear in transport, storage, diagnostics or errors.
- [x] Export an embedding API for ingest, snapshots/change subscriptions, acknowledgment, shutdown, and migrations. Version the package/contracts and test the TypeScript and Python consumer fixtures; no per-device copy of the reducer.
- [x] Keep provider emitters fail-open with bounded latency, payloads and queues during collector outages. State collection never commands a device, including in Media/Free modes.
- [x] Document immutable snapshot revisions, compatibility, storage ownership, source installation identity and one active state owner. Publish reproducible package artifacts usable by a separate repository without checkout-relative imports.

## Dependencies
- [agent-device-hub#2](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/2)

## Verification
Fake-clock reducer, privacy, deduplication, retention, migration, interrupted-write, restart, concurrent-producer and package-consumer checks without credentials or devices.

## Delivery target
Source-only, including configuration/installation tooling. Personal setup, agent launches and physical tests need separate explicit authorization.

## Planning and delivery
GitHub owns scope, acceptance, dependencies and status. Follow this repository's AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. The current request authorizes this backlog definition and repository setup; it does not authorize implementing these future features.

Before implementation, prepare the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change at openspec/changes/gh-3-agent-state-core/. Verify the identity and applicable design requirements first.

## Codex-first goal alignment, 2026-09-07

Part of [the shared Codex-integration goal](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/32). First deliver automatic Codex task integration and manual frontend controls for that integration. General agent-independent device control is [a later phase](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31). Existing local MCP delivery and independently owned work keep their scope. Shared provider contracts remain extensible; retain existing Claude criteria and report Codex milestone evidence separately rather than falsely closing outstanding provider acceptance.

### Additional acceptance criteria
- [x] Keep the shared source in packages/agent-state and provider integration modules in this repository. Publish immutable artifacts for initial embedding in Pixoo and later standalone reuse; do not move or duplicate the reducer into device repositories.
- [x] Expose one current-state feed to independent registered consumers. Bound each consumer's delivery/history and isolate stalls; recover from snapshots after expired cursors without replaying old effects. Verify two device consumers plus a stalled third fake consumer.
- [x] Use the baseline and frozen numeric budget artifact from [performance qualification](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/30) before implementation. Event collection and hook return remain independent of UI visibility, device availability and selected device mode. This is an early design input, not a dependency on that issue's integrated completion.

This update defines backlog work only. It does not start implementation, change an active installation or grant device-test authority. Existing OpenSpec identities, validation and UI/physical acceptance gates remain.

## Source delivery completed, 2026-09-20

PR #105 merged as `f550bcd6b7d3b7da0f34c90c622b343afe2b25fb`, with the same tree as independently reviewed head `ab6c7f5`. The [agent-state 1.0.0 release](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/releases/tag/agent-state-v1.0.0) contains the archive, checksum and source receipt. A fresh merged-revision build reproduces SHA-256 `ae589d311e282c3356579c85507a3aa973ab7990e06e062143aeb08d8d2dcc99`; isolated imports, declarations, manifests, 96 Node/process tests and 36 Python snapshot fixtures pass.

The separately owned CI task merged PR #108 as `ed5024e94da08009f313b08a0dd0e5a1af687a25`, retaining all product suites under the owner-approved five-job Ubuntu matrix and repairing package-index setup. All five merged-main jobs pass, including Linux hook qualification: [Checks](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/35527760360) and [Work guide](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/35527760350). Product source, package inputs, dependencies and OpenSpec are byte-for-byte unchanged from the released source.

The source acceptance criteria and applicable merged-main CI requirement are met. title: Define versioned controller capabilities and integration APIs
body:
## Outcome
Give shared clients a stable way to inspect and command existing device owners without erasing device-specific behavior.

## Scope
Own schemas and cross-language fixtures for device identity, capabilities, observations, commands and feeds. Device implementations remain in [divoom-app-upgrade#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/37) and [codex-nanoleaf#28](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/28). This contract can be defined independently of provider qualification.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Define a stable configured device ID and controller/source identity. Register only explicitly configured destinations; callers cannot choose raw IPs, URLs, filesystem paths, firmware/reset operations or arbitrary device commands.
- [ ] Describe supported capabilities and typed operations for power/brightness and optional device-specific media, zones, scenes and previews. Unsupported capabilities are explicit; ordinary lights do not implement Pixoo's RGB animation interface.
- [ ] Separate desired configuration, queued/pending work, last successful send, failed/partially applied or uncertain work, external control, and observation age from service health. Transport acknowledgment is never optical proof.
- [ ] Version request/result and snapshot/change-feed envelopes. Include request identity, configuration revision, output generation, typed failure and possible prior effects; define bounded replay, conflicting duplicates, cursor expiry and full resync.
- [ ] Define a machine-client authentication boundary distinct from browser Origin/editing tokens, loopback defaults, credential rotation/revocation and bounded admission. Do not weaken existing browser protections.
- [ ] Keep one designated writer per physical device. Clients delegate through its services/queue; expired generations and reconnects cannot replay stale commands or reclaim ownership.
- [ ] Specify renderer metadata with explicit clock domain, epochs, compatibility and update outcomes. Device payloads may contain Pixoo frames or Nanoleaf zone timelines; no universal animation scheduler is introduced.
- [ ] Define package/API compatibility policy and shared fixtures consumed by Python and TypeScript. Keep databases private to their owners; Windows and WSL must never coordinate by concurrently opening a mounted SQLite file.

## Dependencies
- [agent-device-hub#1](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/1)

## Verification
Schema and contract-consumer fixtures covering unsupported capabilities, replay/conflicts, stale generations/cursors, authentication, unknown telemetry and cross-process clock interpretation.

## Delivery target
Source-only, including configuration/installation tooling. Personal setup, agent launches and physical tests need separate explicit authorization.

## Planning and delivery
GitHub owns scope, acceptance, dependencies and status. Follow this repository's AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. The current request authorizes this backlog definition and repository setup; it does not authorize implementing these future features.

Before implementation, prepare the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change at openspec/changes/gh-4-controller-contract/. Verify the identity and applicable design requirements first.

## Priority and access decision
Local Codex control is the current delivery priority. Phone, mobile browser, ChatGPT web, and another-computer access are future goals. Keep native-client authentication, explicit targets, and one existing device writer. Local client access may use the existing same-machine Windows/WSL route and does not prohibit the owning controller from reaching its configured LAN device. This contract is the shared source prerequisite for the local MCP module in #7 and [Nanoleaf controller #28](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/28). Provider qualification and standalone hosting are independent.

title: Host shared monitoring and route commands to existing controllers
body:
## Outcome
Provide one optional standalone hub host for shared agent state, registered controllers, APIs and future clients.

## Scope
Compose the shared state core and controller clients. Before this migration the state core can remain embedded in Pixoo. Standalone hosting is an explicit source/deployment stage, not a second simultaneously active collector.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Serve authenticated loopback APIs and revisioned snapshot/change feeds using the shared contracts. Keep agent-state health and each device's health independent.
- [x] Connect the Pixoo and Linux/WSL Nanoleaf controller APIs through bounded clients; support simulators and deterministic outages without credentials.
- [x] Route all commands to their existing owner. Isolate queues/failures per device so an offline Pixoo cannot block Nanoleaf; no direct protocol writer is added.
- [x] Implement one authoritative agent-state owner, whether embedded or standalone. Specify a quiesced, versioned export/import that preserves identities and revisions, switches producers and consumer endpoints, and supports rollback without two active owners or duplicate notices/effects. Exercise Pixoo #31's embedded/remote session-source facade: its renderer/browser must receive the new feed, and shared label/acknowledgment writes must reach the selected owner. Resume ingestion only after the selected owner and consumer routes are ready; fail explicitly if readiness or migration fails.
- [x] Preserve private data ownership across host changes; do not mount a shared SQLite database between Windows and WSL. Resolve reachability through explicit supported local endpoints without router/firewall changes or an implicit host switch.
- [x] On restart/reconnect, recover current snapshots and uncertain observations without replaying expired animations, missed pictures or ambiguous sent commands.
- [x] Package a reproducible host with isolated runtime storage, readiness, graceful shutdown and a controller compatibility matrix. Source completion does not install or start it on the user's machine.

## Dependencies
- [agent-device-hub#3](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/3)
- [agent-device-hub#4](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/4)
- [divoom-app-upgrade#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/37)
- [codex-nanoleaf#28](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/28)
- [divoom-app-upgrade#31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/31)

## Verification
Local integration with both fake controller clients, slow/offline isolation, auth, recovery, quiesced migration/rollback and one-owner checks. Verify Pixoo feed and acknowledgment routing through cutover, interrupted cutover and rollback; separately validate the installed Nanoleaf consumer cutover under [agent-device-hub#8](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/8).

## Delivery target
Source-only, including configuration/installation tooling. Personal setup, agent launches and physical tests need separate explicit authorization.

## Planning and delivery
GitHub owns scope, acceptance, dependencies and status. Follow this repository's AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. The current request authorizes this backlog definition and repository setup; it does not authorize implementing these future features.

Before implementation, prepare the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change at openspec/changes/gh-5-hub-host/. Verify the identity and applicable design requirements first.

## Priority and access decision
Planned after the local Codex control path. Shared monitoring, standalone hosting, collector migration, and the unified dashboard remain useful follow-on work; none is a prerequisite for the reusable local MCP module or device-local Codex acceptance. Preserve the existing behavior until any separately authorized migration.

## Codex-first goal alignment, 2026-09-07

Part of [the shared Codex-integration goal](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/32). First deliver automatic Codex task integration and manual frontend controls for that integration. General agent-independent device control is [a later phase](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31). Existing local MCP delivery and independently owned work keep their scope. Shared provider contracts remain extensible; retain existing Claude criteria and report Codex milestone evidence separately rather than falsely closing outstanding provider acceptance.

### Additional acceptance criteria
- [x] Serve a common integration-management API for the shared frontend: source/consumer health, current task state, user labels and monitor acknowledgment, registered device capabilities, integration modes and controller-owned mappings/settings.
- [x] Route Pixoo monitor filters/modes and Nanoleaf supported integration settings through their owning APIs. Specify finite versioned integration extensions and compatibility fixtures; do not silently broaden released device API v1, pass native credentials to the browser or add a second device writer.
- [x] Keep shared source/package ownership in this repository across embedded and standalone hosting. The standalone application composes the same engine; Pixoo's backend remains a device service using its selected session-source facade.
- [x] Validate source/consumer/API responsiveness against the early budget artifact from [performance qualification](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/30) and preserve Linux-owned Nanoleaf state and its designated writer.

### Additional required dependencies
- [Nanoleaf integration-settings API](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/49) for the completed integration-management adapter.
- [Pixoo #33](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/33) for completed monitor settings/mode operations. Host/core work with fakes can proceed independently; do not claim final controller integration until these APIs are delivered.

This update defines backlog work only. It does not start implementation, change an active installation or grant device-test authority. Existing OpenSpec identities, validation and UI/physical acceptance gates remain.

## Owner delivery decision, September 21, 2026

The owner explicitly invoked deliver-work for this issue and selected Linux in WSL as the primary runtime. Native Windows runtime implementation and qualification are outside this delivery. Use configured authenticated local controller endpoints and private Linux storage; do not share controller databases, change a live installation or operate devices. This supersedes the earlier Windows-only wording and planning-only authority for this issue.

Host/core work may proceed while Pixoo #33 remains open. Nanoleaf #49 is now source-delivered through PR #63. Final Pixoo settings integration remains blocked on its owning API; do not invent or silently widen a controller contract.


## Owner memory-budget decision, September 21, 2026

The owner explicitly requested doubling the service RSS budget from 128 MiB to **256 MiB** and deferring budget re-evaluation and memory improvements to [Hub #123](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/123). That follow-up is backlog work and does not block this issue. Preserve all original measurements and their failures against 128 MiB; a budget increase is not evidence of optimization. Other budgets, functional acceptance and integrated qualification remain unchanged.

Pixoo #33 has since closed through [PR #64](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/pull/64). Its delivered API can now be integrated; this does not complete the host adapter or migration acceptance.

## Source acceptance, September 21, 2026

[PR #121](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/121) merged as `2c3bb4117bab0f845a95048b4ce72a49e915cfdc`. Both independent Standards and Specification reviewers approved final head `fdc277392179b7a6a7e7825566faada7cfb624c9`. All five PR jobs and all five merged-main jobs passed. Main evidence: [shared/product checks](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/35653288866), [guide checks](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/35653288926). The merged tree matches the reviewed candidate.

The Linux host provides scoped authenticated monitor/management APIs, independent bounded controller clients, Pixoo and Nanoleaf settings adapters, private durable ownership and supervised migration. The real pinned Pixoo simulator verified producer switching, its selected-source facade, label/acknowledgment routing, renderer revision and fresh-store rollback after accepted writes. Migration recovery tests preserve fences and original producer policy across failures. Readiness is bound to the live supervised Pixoo child and its selected configuration. Nanoleaf's actual owning controller fixture verified queued settings, application and replay.

Local validation includes 29 host tests, shared build/type/contract/state/MCP checks, reproducible offline package installation, seven specifications and six archived changes, 15 workflow tests and guide checks. The final synthetic API receipt retains 9,000 samples, zero failures and peak RSS 165.44 MiB against 256 MiB. It remains `qualified: false` for full integration. Original failed receipts and the earlier CI fixture failure remain recorded; the corrected current-head run passed.

This closes source delivery only. Nothing was installed, no live state was migrated and no device was operated. Installed cutover remains #8; full integrated qualification remains #30; budget reassessment and memory optimization remain nonblocking #123. [Guide companion #125](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/125) merged as `a639e0a8ca79c1651e3acb9190c565af1c9c7fa9` after both independent reviews, local guide checks and verified guide-only CI filtering. Guide-source synchronization is complete; public publication remains pending.

title: Build the shared Codex-integration frontend
body:
## Outcome
Provide one browser interface for agent sessions, attention and supported device controls.

## Scope
Build a React/TypeScript Codex-integration frontend over the hub API, using the delivered Nanoleaf frontend as the visual and interaction starting point. Include manual controls for supported integration behavior. Keep advanced Nanoleaf wall editing and Pixoo playlist editing in their existing interfaces initially; general agent-independent device control is a later phase.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Show provider/source sessions, attributable subagents, continuing versus blocked attention, retained notices, chosen labels, observation age and collector health without inferring success or readership.
- [ ] Show each registered device's capabilities, selected device-specific mode, desired/pending state, last successful update, failures, freshness and external control. Unknown values cannot look confirmed.
- [ ] Use the same protected application commands as MCP with device identity, request IDs and revision checks. Acknowledgment changes only monitor state; observation/selection sends no device mutations.
- [ ] Expose only supported explicit controls and validated links to existing device editors. Preserve Nanoleaf Work/Quiet/Free and Pixoo Monitor/Media meanings; do not introduce a global mode that silently takes over devices.
- [ ] Handle snapshot/change-feed reconnect, stale results, expired cursors and concurrent clients while preserving focus and user edits.
- [ ] Exact frame/timeline previews are deferred for a future scope decision and excluded from this issue. Nanoleaf [codex-nanoleaf#15](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/15)/[codex-nanoleaf#17](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/17) and Pixoo [divoom-app-upgrade#32](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/32) supply device rendering contracts, not committed hub preview integration. Any later hub preview issue must depend on its applicable rendering/parity work; the basic overview remains independent.
- [ ] Meet keyboard, contrast, reduced-motion and responsive-layout checks with synthetic data. Get explicit user approval of the current UI candidate before merge; record live/physical acceptance separately.

## Dependencies
- [agent-device-hub#5](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/5)

## Verification
Browser and fake-controller integration checks for every state/control, reconnect, concurrent edits, accessibility and no-write inspection. No personal sessions or devices required.

## Delivery target
Source-only, including configuration/installation tooling. Personal setup, agent launches and physical tests need separate explicit authorization.

## Planning and delivery
GitHub owns scope, acceptance, dependencies and status. Follow this repository's AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. The current request authorizes this backlog definition and repository setup; it does not authorize implementing these future features.

Before implementation, prepare the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change at openspec/changes/gh-6-unified-dashboard/. Verify the identity and applicable design requirements first.

## Priority and access decision
Planned after the local Codex control path. Shared monitoring, standalone hosting, collector migration, and the unified dashboard remain useful follow-on work; none is a prerequisite for the reusable local MCP module or device-local Codex acceptance. Preserve the existing behavior until any separately authorized migration.

## Codex-first goal alignment, 2026-09-07

Part of [the shared Codex-integration goal](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/32). First deliver automatic Codex task integration and manual frontend controls for that integration. General agent-independent device control is [a later phase](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31). Existing local MCP delivery and independently owned work keep their scope. Shared provider contracts remain extensible; retain existing Claude criteria and report Codex milestone evidence separately rather than falsely closing outstanding provider acceptance.

### Additional acceptance criteria
- [ ] Make the first frontend a Codex-integration application with task/activity, device integration and source/connection views. It must support useful inspection and controls when no current task is active, without implementing a general device-control dashboard.
- [ ] Use the delivered Nanoleaf frontend's visual language and task/selection/pending-state interaction patterns as the design starting point in apps/dashboard. comments.body:
## Push API qualification (2026-09-23)

The official Tidbyt cloud still accepts pushes. One background push to the user's device appeared in rotation without interrupting the current app, and the test installation was deleted afterward.

**Calls** (all against `https://api.tidbyt.com/v0`, behind Cloudflare):

| Call | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /devices/<device>/installations` | 200, 15 existing installations |
| `POST /devices/<device>/push` with `{deviceID, image, installationID: "hubqualtest", background: true}` | 200, body `{}`, 262 ms |
| `GET /devices/<device>/installations` | 200, `hubqualtest` listed with an empty `appID` |
| `DELETE /devices/<device>/installations/hubqualtest` | 200, body `{}`, 281 ms |
| `GET /devices/<device>/installations` | 200, 14 installations, `hubqualtest` absent |

**Authentication.** `Authorization: Bearer <API key>`, with the key and device ID from the Tidbyt app (Settings → General → Get API Key). A script read both from a mode-600 file outside Git; neither appeared in arguments, output or this comment. Unauthenticated and invalid-token requests fail in ways a client must not treat as a normal auth rejection:
- No `Authorization` header: **500**, `{"code":2,"message":"context doesn't have a UID"}`.
- Invalid bearer token: **401**, `{"code":16,"message":"auth error: Post \"https://hydra-admin/oauth2/introspect\": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate has expired ... after 2025-09-12..."}`. The cloud's internal token introspection has an expired certificate. Valid API keys still authenticate, so this path only matters for bad or revoked keys, and the controller should classify it as an authentication failure, not a transient error.

**Image.** A 64×32 lossless WebP (290 bytes), sent base64-encoded in `image`, was accepted. No size or format limit was documented or observed. The docs pages (tidbyt.dev, api.tidbyt.com) now render without content, so the request shape was confirmed from [pixlet's push/list/delete commands](https://github.com/tidbyt/pixlet/tree/c29059778792f1731822098aeb71f9bf5567b38b/cmd) at `c290597` (last commit 2024-09-30).

**Rate limits.** None seen. No `Retry-After` or rate-limit headers were returned, and no 429 occurred. Limits were not probed, because this issue allows only the one test push.

**Rotation.** The user confirmed that the background push joined the rotation and did not interrupt the app on screen. Pushed installations appear in the installation list with an empty `appID`, which separates them from store apps. Delete removes the installation, and the next list read confirms it is gone.

**Not established:** firmware/generation (#24), Tronbyt behavior (#23), foreground (non-background) push behavior, how long an installation persists without refresh, and the display duration within rotation.

title: Qualify direct LIFX LAN control
body:
## Outcome

Identify the LIFX bulbs and choose how the hub talks to them over the LAN, so [#18](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/18) can start.

## Checks, in order

1. **Model and firmware.** The user supplies one or more bulb IPs. Send read-only `GetVersion` (32), `GetHostFirmware` (14) and `LightGet` (101) messages to UDP 56700 at those IPs. Look the returned product ID up in [LIFX/products](https://github.com/LIFX/products) to learn color, temperature range and effect support. "A16" is the user's name for the bulb; do not assume A19.
2. **Network path.** Confirm that replies reach the hub's runtime in WSL. The controller targets configured IPs. Broadcast discovery may not cross WSL's NAT, so it is not needed.
3. **Library or direct.** Compare one maintained Node/TypeScript library with writing the few messages the controller needs (`GetVersion`, `LightGet`/`LightState`, `SetPower`, `SetColor`, `SetWaveform`). If a library wins, record its version and license.

Retries, timeouts, packet fixtures and partial multi-bulb outcomes belong to #18.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Model, product ID, firmware and supported features recorded from check 1. Unknown features stay off.
- [ ] **AC2.** The network path result and the library-or-direct decision recorded, with version and license if a library is used.
- [ ] **AC3.** One closing comment on this issue is the record. Keep bulb IPs and serials out of Git and out of the issue.

## Assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-23, scope trimmed for a personal project.

- **Complexity: low.** A few read-only UDP messages and a dependency choice.
- **Uncertainty: medium.** Exact model, whether WSL receives the replies, and whether a usable maintained library exists.
- **Impact: low.** Read-only against the bulbs.

**Readiness:** ready. #14 is closed. **Review:** none beyond the closing comment; source reviews apply to #18.

Home Assistant and cloud HTTP were already considered and set aside in `controllers/lifx/README.md`. [#11](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/11) stays related, not a prerequisite.

## Sources

- https://lan.developer.lifx.com/docs/communicating-with-device
- https://github.com/LIFX/products

Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. This issue authorizes only read-only `Get` messages to bulb IPs the user supplies. No `Set` messages, broadcast discovery, router or firewall changes, or installation.

- [x] Measure hook process launch through return and event admission through receipt by each real consumer. Include first-call/startup observations separately from warmed calls. Use monotonic durations within a process or harness-observed boundaries; do not subtract unverified cross-process clocks. Detailed internal phase timing and separate Node/Python microbenchmarks are diagnostic work only when a slow result needs explanation. Monitoring-feed measurements do not use manual MCP as a substitute.
- [x] Exercise one task and a realistic concurrent profile, initially 10 active tasks. Use a short 50-task burst only to check bounded queues/memory, explicit overflow or resync, lack of hangs, and recovery. Fifty visible task slots and sustained 50-task throughput are not promised. Choose and document a proportionate sample count; the historical three-by-1,000 calls for every profile is not required.
- [x] Define practical responsiveness targets and sampling in the issue-linked implementation plan before qualification runs, with reasons tied to the standalone setup and everyday use. Record p95 and, only with adequate samples, p99 as diagnostics. Historical legacy-hook percentile ceilings are comparison data, not pass/fail gates for this revised #30. Retain the 3,000 ms hard hook return deadline, the existing 256 MiB service RSS ceiling, and the applicable bounded queue/payload contracts. Do not relabel earlier failures as passes or relax a target after failure without a documented reviewed decision.
- [x] Prove hook return remains fail-open and within its hard deadline when the hub is unavailable. Stall or disconnect one consumer and verify that the healthy consumer continues to receive current state. Exercise a stalled fake consumer alongside Pixoo and Nanoleaf where needed to test subscription isolation. Check bounded resource use and honest loss/resync reporting during the burst; do not grow retries or queues indefinitely.
- [x] Cover a small scenario set: dashboard closed and connected, dashboard reconnect, an ordinary supported integration control during monitoring, one unavailable consumer, and standalone hub stop/restart. Verify recovery to current state without replaying expired effects, retention of labels/notices as required by existing contracts, and one active state owner and designated writer per device. Reuse relevant consumer playback/animation regressions; no exhaustive UI/control/media cross-product or migration/rollback performance matrix is required.
- [x] Confine every run to synthetic input and explicit disposable Linux state, with no private state access, external network/device traffic or Windows executable forwarding. Reap owned descendants on success, timeout and failure. Report consumer receipt/fake transport separately from installed-client and physical evidence. No live installation or physical timing is needed to close this source issue.

## Dependencies and parallel work
- Source inputs remain [Hub #3](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/3), [#5](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/5), [#6](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/6), [#8](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/8), [Pixoo #33](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/33) and [Nanoleaf #29](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/29). Verify delivered revisions before running dependent scenarios; independent fixture/instrumentation work need not wait for unrelated evidence.
- [Pixoo #61](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/61) owns optional embedded-host hardening. Its evidence is not required to implement or close this standalone-only #30. This revision does not change #61's acceptance criteria or historical failed receipts.
- [Hub #9](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/9) may consume this bounded source report. Installed-client and physical acceptance remain [Pixoo #34](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/34) and [Nanoleaf #30](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/30), with their own authority and evidence.

## Exclusions and delivery
Embedded-host qualification, native Windows comparison/forwarding, production deployment, full owner-migration/rollback qualification, physical/optical measurement, language rewrites and unrelated controller optimization are outside this revision. Existing runtime recovery, authentication, privacy, durability and single-owner protections remain intact.

Follow current AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md for implementation, independent Standards and Specification reviews, applicable CI, guarded merge and merged-source verification. Keep the issue open until these source acceptance criteria are evidenced. Personal hook changes, agent launches, installation and device operations require separate authorization. Public guide publication remains separate from source synchronization.

Part of [Hub #32](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/32). The early `gh-30-shared-monitor-performance` change was synchronized and archived in PR #77. Preserve it and its receipts. New executable measurement behavior needs a new issue-linked OpenSpec change; this scope-only revision has no product behavior delta. Historical budget JSON is unchanged by this revision; the new qualification must distinguish diagnostic legacy comparisons from the retained hard deadline/resource checks and its new standalone targets.

## Historical scope and evidence

The following is the pre-revision issue text, retained for provenance. Its broader requirements and statement that #30 consumes #61 evidence are superseded by the current scope above. Prior measurements, failures, source merges and exclusions remain historical facts, not evidence that the new qualification passed.

<details>
<summary>Scope, decisions and evidence before the personal-project revision</summary>

## Outcome
Demonstrate that the shared Node.js/TypeScript service and Python Nanoleaf consumer preserve responsive Codex work and device behavior.

## Scope
Own the cross-repository performance profile, repeatable source fixtures and release evidence. Run baseline and budget definition after #2 before dependent runtime designs freeze; complete integrated qualification after #3/#5/#6/#8 and the device consumers. This does not authorize a language rewrite.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Establish repeatable Linux baselines in Ubuntu WSL under comparable host/load conditions; no native Windows comparison or executable-forwarding measurement is required. Record client/runtime/repository versions, host/load profile, cold and warm startup, sample counts and repeated runs. Separate hook return, event admission/reduction/publication, each consumer's admission, transport submission and later physical observation.
- [ ] Freeze numeric p95/p99 budgets and hard failure timeouts before implementation based on measured baselines and the user's no-performance-regression requirement. Specify clock comparison, sampling, pass/fail tolerance, CPU/memory/queue limits and intentional rendering cadence. Material budget changes require documented review, not post-failure relaxation.
- [ ] Exercise one task, 10 concurrent tasks and a 50-task burst with Pixoo/Nanoleaf consumers and a stalled third fake consumer. Respect device display capacity and verify bounded overflow/coalescing/resync behavior; these profiles do not promise 50 visible task slots.
- [ ] Prove a stalled or disconnected device cannot delay a healthy consumer or agent hook return. Hooks meet their bounded fail-open budget during host failure; sustained overload keeps memory/queue depth bounded and reports data loss or resync honestly.
- [ ] Measure the real Linux hook from process launch through return, including stdin parsing, admission/commit and actual Linux worker-spawn handoff. Measure Node/Python component and process overhead on Linux; report background readiness/cleanup separately. Use synthetic stdin and explicit disposable Linux state, prove confinement against private state, external network, devices and Windows executables, and reap detached descendants on success, timeout and failure. Admission-only/no-op-launch timing is insufficient. Qualify the monitoring feed independently from manual MCP transport; avoid per-event process creation if it exceeds the budget.
- [ ] Include the shared frontend open/closed and reconnecting, concurrent integration controls, Pixoo playback and Nanoleaf animation/scene regressions, embedded hosting, standalone hosting, restart and rollback.
- [ ] Publish reproducible commands and a pinned cross-repository receipt, distinguish fixture/transport/optical measurements and feed results into #9 and device acceptance. Numeric qualification remains required for performance acceptance. The September 20 owner decision below defers Pixoo embedded-host qualification to a hardening story and permits feature source delivery before that qualification.

## Linux replan, September 10, 2026

The user selected Linux-only performance qualification. This replaces the former matched Windows/WSL and Windows forwarding/helper requirements, including the historical interop blocker recorded in earlier comments. WSL is the Linux host environment; it does not require a cross-OS call path.

Use the source-delivered fresh Linux runtime from [Nanoleaf PR #57](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/57), merge `2558df5a2fc543247b0c75898ef0260ba3ea264b`, and ADR 0007. PR #77 now implements and tests that pin and its executed file set for isolated profiling. Installed/client/physical acceptance remains [Nanoleaf #55](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/55), not a prerequisite for isolated source measurements.

[PR #77](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/77) merged the early Linux source baseline and numeric budgets on September 12, 2026 UTC as `1fd353215532a5d0220b99d9b35b6da0436221cc`. It records 9,000 real hook calls across nine repeated 1/10/50-session profiles, actual worker-spawn handoff, bounded cleanup and confinement checks. The measured p95 ceilings are 63/82/377 ms, with a 3,000 ms hard return timeout. The merged [baseline report](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/1fd353215532a5d0220b99d9b35b6da0436221cc/docs/performance-baseline.md) and [budget definitions](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/1fd353215532a5d0220b99d9b35b6da0436221cc/docs/performance/linux-budgets.json) are inputs to dependent runtime designs.

Historical admission/validator receipts remain separate from full-hook measurements. The synthetic profiles do not establish installed-client or physical-device acceptance. Queue/cadence limits for future shared services remain design constraints awaiting integrated tests. This issue stays open for integrated feed/consumer qualification; the broad acceptance criteria above remain unchecked where they include that later work.

The subsequent deliver-work request authorizes scoped measurement implementation, isolated runs, review and eligible source merge. Installation, live clients and devices remain outside this delivery. Repository-wide Windows CI removal and CI cost reduction are separate work. Report remaining Windows elements in shared policy/contracts, CI, legacy source and historical evidence to the user; do not silently retain them as measurement prerequisites. Existing configured CI remains a merge gate until its separately reviewed replacement is delivered. The completed CI story #91 preserved platform coverage and does not implement this new Linux-only policy.

## Dependencies and staging
- Baseline/design begins after [#2](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/2); its budget artifact is required input to #3/#5 and consumer designs, not a dependency on this issue's final completion.
- Integrated completion requires [#3](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/3), [#5](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/5), [#6](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/6), [#8](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/8), [Pixoo #33](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/33) and [Nanoleaf #29](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/29).
- [#9](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/9) consumes final source qualification. Physical observation remains in [Pixoo #34](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/34) and [Nanoleaf #30](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/30).

## Verification and delivery target
Source qualification and documentation, with separately linked physical measurements. Blocked for integrated completion by the listed implementations; baseline work is the first bounded stage. Prepare an issue-linked OpenSpec design for new executable timing/overload behavior, or document when a pure verification change needs no product delta.

## Delivery and authority
The original September 7 planning authority was extended by the user's explicit deliver-work request for #30/#77. The early source baseline and budgets merged in #77; final integrated qualification remains pending its dependencies. Personal setup, agent sessions, installed hook changes and device operations remain outside scope. Source work follows the repository's current AGENTS.md and SDLC, issue-linked OpenSpec planning, applicable checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews, human approval for UI candidates, guarded merge and merged-source readback. Preserve other coordinators' work. Installation and physical acceptance require their separately scoped authorization.

## Goal and planning identity
Part of [Hub #32](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/32). The early-stage OpenSpec change gh-30-shared-monitor-performance was synchronized and archived in #77. Future executable deltas need their own applicable planning artifacts. The early baseline/budget is consumed before runtime implementation; final performance qualification remains after integrated implementations. These are separate stages and must not introduce a dependency cycle.

## Guide synchronization and closeout, September 12, 2026 UTC

PR #77 incorporated the planning inputs and generated guide from [PR #99](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/99). PR #99 is now closed as superseded and needs no separate merge. The current documentation follow-up reconciles the guide narrative and history with the observed #77 merge; its own PR and approval remain separate from the completed source merge. Public publication and live verification are outside this follow-up.

The owner explicitly excluded further #77 CI verification from this reconciliation. This records the observed source merge and does not claim successful merged-main CI. Overall #30 remains open for integrated qualification after the dependencies above. Repository-wide Windows policy and legacy-source cleanup remain separate work.

## Embedded-host hardening decision, September 20, 2026

The owner moved [Pixoo #31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/31) performance measurement and numeric acceptance to [Pixoo hardening #61](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/61). That story follows #31 and does not block it or dependent feature progress. This issue retains integrated qualification and consumes #61 evidence. Frozen limits and failed receipts remain unchanged; feature delivery must not claim qualified performance. Correctness, privacy, authentication, durability, exclusive ownership, bounded resources, failure isolation and hard fail-open deadlines remain required. Other integrated dependencies and acceptance criteria are unchanged.

</details>

title: Define agent-independent device controls after Codex integration acceptance
body:
## Outcome
In a second phase, expand the shared frontend into a general device-control application that works without an agent session.

## Scope and priority
The user selected Codex integration and manual frontend controls for that integration as the first goal. This issue records later planning for general power, brightness, scenes, media and other device-native controls. Preserve controls already delivered in device apps or local MCP work; do not postpone or undo that independent delivery.

## Acceptance criteria for planning
- [x] Begin after the Codex-first goal has its source, shared-frontend and authorized installed acceptance evidence; record any remaining gaps before advancing.
- [x] Inventory existing controller capabilities and choose the supported initial general-control set with the user. Identify missing device API work in the owning repositories instead of assuming every light/display supports every operation.
- [x] Define explicit manual takeover, restoration and interaction with ongoing Codex monitoring and device-specific modes. No global mode may silently overwrite all device intent.
- [x] Define frontend pages and narrow controller extensions using the same protected command owners, identity/replay rules and failure evidence. The frontend must not become another physical writer.
- [x] Reuse delivered visual components and domain editors as appropriate; define any integration or migration work separately. Exact live rendering, phone/remote access and language/repository migrations retain their own scope.
- [x] Create or refine bounded implementation issues in the hub and affected device repos only after the feature set is settled. Define source tests, human UI approval and separately authorized physical acceptance.

## Dependencies and readiness
Deferred until Codex-first shared monitoring and integration controls are accepted. The later feature set remains a user decision. Do not implement this phase or mark it ready as part of the current backlog alignment.

## Delivery target
Deferred planning definition; no new physical controls are implemented by this issue.

## Delivery and authority
Planning/backlog definition only under the user's 2026-09-07 request. Do not start implementation, personal setup, agent sessions, hook changes or device operations from this issue publication. Future source work follows the repository's current AGENTS.md and SDLC, issue-linked OpenSpec planning, applicable checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews, human approval for UI candidates, guarded merge and merged-source readback. Preserve other coordinators' work. Installation and physical acceptance require their separately scoped authorization.

## Blocking goal
[Hub #32](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/32) owns the prior Codex-first goal and its acceptance milestone. Remain deferred until that milestone passes. This planning-only backlog item has no product spec delta yet; define issue-linked implementation changes after the later feature set is accepted.

## Desktop-control consumer

The accepted desk presets and explicitly configured preset bindings are defined in [jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#67](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/67) and [jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#68](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/68). They remain downstream of this general-control definition and the Codex-first milestone. Control profiles map inputs to actions; desk presets apply configured device actions without redefining native modes. Manual device changes remain until the next explicit preset request. Early Codex mouse delivery in [jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub#65](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/65) is independent of this milestone. These links define future consumers and add no implementation scope to the current milestone.

## Central BUNNY UI and future components, 2026-09-21

The user confirmed that general device control should extend the same central BUNNY application established by [Hub #6](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/6). Preserve its Nanoleaf-derived visual language and reusable integration views.

- [x] Plan general controls within the existing shared navigation and component status/settings/control views, including operation without an active agent session. Each later user-facing BUNNY integration must adopt that same view pattern as its supported capabilities are delivered.
- [x] For each selected feature, record the component's capability and permission matrix, owning API/service, required UI work and verification. Unsupported capabilities remain explicit; a new component does not imply support for every lighting or media operation.
- [x] Keep routine supported controls in the central UI and define bounded follow-on issues for specialized editor integration where needed. Preserve existing editor links until their replacements are delivered and accepted.
- [x] Carry the reusable integration-view acceptance criteria from Hub #6 into the later implementation issues, including differing component capabilities, unavailable states, concurrent edits and inspection without writes. Retain the existing manual takeover, restoration and designated-writer boundaries.

This is an authorized planning refinement. The issue remains deferred behind [Hub #32](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/32); choosing and implementing the later control set retains its existing acceptance and authorization requirements.


## Accepted definition, 2026-09-22

The user resolved the planning decisions in a grouped question round on 2026-09-22 and authorized the tracker changes and documentation PR below. The durable record is ADR 0005, `docs/decisions/0005-general-device-controls.md`, delivered with the linked hub PR. This section is the tracker summary; the ADR and the linked issues own the details.

**Codex-first gap record.** Hub #32 closed 2026-09-22. Nanoleaf #30 and Pixoo #34 installed acceptance, and Hub #8, #9 and #30, are closed. No remaining gap blocks this definition. The public guide edition is behind the merged source, which is a separate publication stage.

**Capability inventory at definition time.**

| Device | Native controller v1 capabilities declared | Delivered extension | General-control status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pixoo | Screen power (off pauses, on does not resume), brightness 0–100, media: playlist selection by ID (up to 100 IDs, no names) and pause/resume/stop/next/previous/clear. Scenes, zones, preview and modes unsupported. | Monitor/Media mode, filters, cadence | Supported now; UI in #151, names in Pixoo #67 |
| Nanoleaf | Mode set Work/Quiet/Free only. Power, brightness, media, zones, scenes and preview unsupported. | Layout, coverage, element/task assignment, project colors | Needs Nanoleaf #64 before UI in #153 |
| Tidbyt, LIFX, PC lighting | No controller delivered (#15/#16, #17/#18, #51/#53) | none | Unavailable; join through their existing issues and #56 |

**Initial general-control set.** Pixoo: power, brightness, playlist selection and the six playback actions, one guarded v1 command each; rendition selection stays an editor link. Nanoleaf: power, brightness and saved-scene activation after Nanoleaf #64 declares them. Hub MCP media tools are a separate issue, #152.

**Takeover, restoration and mode rules.**
- Power and brightness are mode-independent. The owning controller keeps its policies: Pixoo screen-off pauses; a Nanoleaf brightness command is an override that persists until the next explicit mode command.
- Content controls (Pixoo playlist and playback, Nanoleaf scenes) are disabled while the device presents agent status, with the reason and a one-click explicit switch to Media or Free through the existing mode control. No user action changes a mode as a side effect of another command, and no compound writes are submitted.
- Nothing restores automatically. Restoration is the existing mode command. The hub stores no baseline and runs no timer. Free-mode restoration baselines for presets remain #67.
- Nanoleaf scene activation is accepted only in Free, as a one-shot worker write with no polling after handoff.

**Pages and permissions.** Controls live only in each component's existing view; navigation is unchanged and no page commands more than one device. Availability is the product of controller-declared capability and the credential's existing control scope and device aliases; every disabled control names the missing capability or scope. The frontend remains a client of the hub route and never a physical writer.

**Vocabulary.** *General control*: an explicit user-issued supported device operation through the owning controller, independent of any agent session (avoid "manual control", "agent-independent control"). *Status presentation*: a device rendering agent status (Pixoo Monitor, Nanoleaf Work or Quiet). *Takeover*: the user selecting the device's content mode (Pixoo Media, Nanoleaf Free) so content controls apply; distinct from the contract's *external control*, a change made outside the controller. *Restoration*: an explicit return to status presentation through the existing mode command.

**Bounded implementation issues.**

| Issue | Scope | Readiness |

title: Deliver Codex-first shared monitoring and integration controls
body:
## Outcome
One qualified Codex lifecycle event reaches one shared state owner and produces consistent task status on Pixoo and Nanoleaf. A common frontend lets the user inspect and manage those Codex integrations. General device control without agent interaction is a later goal.

## Accepted direction
- Keep Node.js/TypeScript shared services and Pixoo, and the Python Windows Nanoleaf worker. Preserve performance through measured release budgets.
- Shared state code belongs in this repo from the start, initially packaged into Pixoo's backend and later run by a standalone host. The frontend belongs here in apps/dashboard, using the delivered Nanoleaf visual language and useful interaction patterns as its starting point.
- Each device integration consumes the shared feed and retains its own rendering policy, private state and designated writer. One stalled device must not delay another or block Codex.
- Preserve existing local MCP delivery and other coordinators' work. This planning goal does not take over their issues or installed state.

## First-phase frontend
Show Codex sessions, attention, retained notices, freshness, collector/consumer health and device integration state. Support explicit user labels, monitor-only notice dismissal, supported per-device participation/modes and task/project mappings. Device modes keep their existing meanings. Existing advanced editors remain usable; full wall-map/playlist-editor migration, custom effects and exact optical previews are not initial gates.

## Delivery stages
1. Qualify Codex Desktop/CLI and Windows/WSL paths in #2; retain provider-neutral contracts and existing Claude source fixtures without making a new Claude installed rollout the Codex milestone.
2. Deliver #3 and Pixoo #29/#31/#37, then Pixoo #32/#33 and Nanoleaf #29/#49 after their prerequisites.
3. Deliver standalone hosting #5 and reversible owned-hook setup/migration #8. Prove one active state owner and no duplicate legacy/shared ingestion.
4. Deliver #6's Codex-integration frontend using the owning controller APIs; deliver #13's shared MCP composition without duplicating existing local tools.
5. Pass the cross-repository source suite #9 and performance qualification. Then use the separately authorized Pixoo #34 and Nanoleaf #30 acceptance stages for real Codex hooks and visible behavior.

## Completion criteria
- [x] Existing issue scope, live prerequisites and ownership are refreshed. Issue bodies/specs/docs are reconciled before implementation; completed or independently active work is preserved.
- [x] All first-phase source features have reviewed merged revisions and applicable validation evidence. UI candidates have explicit human approval.
- [x] The same synthetic task sequence reaches both consumers and the common frontend through embedded and standalone hosts; duplicates/outages/reconnect cannot invent success, repeat expired effects or take over Media/Free behavior.
- [x] Frontend integration controls use protected owning services, preserve identity/revisions and show pending/conflict/uncertain results. Inspection is free of device mutations.
- [x] Performance budgets pass across required source/runtime profiles; a third fake consumer demonstrates extensibility without adding new production hardware.
- [x] Source completion is reported separately from installed acceptance. Full Codex-first acceptance needs the approved real Windows/WSL client and device evidence. Claude-specific outstanding criteria remain tracked and are not falsely closed by the Codex milestone.
- [x] General agent-independent controls remain deferred; no implementation goal or installation is silently started by backlog definition.

## Scope ownership
This is the cross-repository goal and priority record. Child issues retain their own acceptance, OpenSpec identity, review and completion conditions. This record does not waive a child's remaining Claude, physical, UI or prerequisite criteria. No giant cross-repository implementation PR is intended.

## Dependencies and delivery target
Planning is complete only when the bounded source stories and missing API/performance work are linked. Runtime completion depends on their source and separately authorized acceptance evidence. Current action is backlog alignment only.

## Delivery and authority
Planning/backlog definition only under the user's 2026-09-07 request. Do not start implementation, personal setup, agent sessions, hook changes or device operations from this issue publication. Future source work follows the repository's current AGENTS.md and SDLC, issue-linked OpenSpec planning, applicable checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews, human approval for UI candidates, guarded merge and merged-source readback. Preserve other coordinators' work. Installation and physical acceptance require their separately scoped authorization.

## Repository work and required sequence
| Stage | Owning issues |
| --- | --- |
| Lifecycle qualification and shared engine | [Hub #2](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/2), [Hub #3](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/3) |
| Pixoo embedding, renderer and integration controls | [Pixoo #29](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/29), [#31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/31), [#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/37), [#32](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/32), [#33](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/33) |

| Standalone host, frontend, hooks and shared MCP | [Hub #5](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/5), [#6](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/6), [#8](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/8), [#13](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/13) |
| Performance and integrated source acceptance | [Hub #30](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/30), [#9](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/9) |
| Authorized installed Codex milestones | [Pixoo #34](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/34), [Nanoleaf #30](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/30) |
| Later general device-control planning | [Hub #31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31) |

The first dependency-ready source definition is Hub #2 after verified #1; performance baseline design follows #2. Pixoo #30 remains an independently authorized physical cadence qualification prerequisite for final #33 integration. Do not replace that evidence with simulator results.

The Codex-first installed milestone consumes the applicable Codex/UI/device receipts from Pixoo #34 and Nanoleaf #30; it need not falsely close those broader issues while required Claude cases remain. Their remaining criteria stay tracked. Repository consolidation, additional hardware, advanced animation editors and exact optical previews are outside this goal.

## Planning/document alignment and completion reporting
Each implementing issue must reconcile affected architecture/ADR/roadmap/adoption-guide pointers and its OpenSpec scenarios with this priority before implementation. The source stays in its owning repository; source ownership and initial runtime hosting are different concerns. Use the current approved Nanoleaf frontend as design input, preserve independently active UI/device work, and obtain new human UI approval for the shared candidate.

This issue is a GitHub planning/coordination record, not an automatically scheduled Codex goal. Current publication creates no running implementation. Native issue-dependency mutation is unavailable in the current connector; the explicit required-dependency links in child issue bodies are authoritative planning records and the proposed graph has been checked for cycles. title: Defer Windows Apple Music as an optional playback source
body:
## Outcome and priority

Deferred: add the native Windows Apple Music app as an optional later source of the [shared playback and Sony delivery](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175). The initial music delivery uses the Sony HT-A9 through [#175](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175) and requires no Windows helper or program.

Owner decision, September 24, 2026: Linux/Docker-compatible playback service first, Sony first real adapter, Windows integration later only if still wanted. This issue no longer owns the shared service and does not block UI, displays, lighting, Music presets or Sony delivery.

## Boundary to revisit before implementation

- Keep Windows-specific access behind a source adapter and reuse the shared snapshot/command contract. A Linux container cannot directly consume the native Windows media-session API; any later Windows-local helper or remote producer needs an explicit placement decision and installed qualification.
- Do not preselect Python/pywinrt, PowerShell subprocess supervision, login startup, a tray application or a connector push protocol. Qualify the smallest approach from the actual host environment when this deferred work is selected.
- Select Apple Music by `GetSessions()` and its qualified `SourceAppUserModelId`, never the system's current-session heuristic. Test alongside another media app and with Apple Music in the background.
- Report available metadata and controls without requiring duration, progress or artwork. Retain unavailable/stale observations, exact command targeting, unsupported controls, request correlation and no automatic retry of uncertain writes.
- If this becomes the second source, implement the minimum coexistence/selection behavior through the shared service, with an explicit selection that never changes merely because another source updates or the selected source disappears. Coordinate any selection UI with [#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/37); do not duplicate the playback service.

## Acceptance to refine when selected

- [ ] **AC1.** Record the chosen placement, installed Windows/app versions, exact session identity, useful fields and isolated supported-control results in the issue-linked OpenSpec design. Historical probe evidence is not current app qualification.
- [ ] **AC2.** Implement one Windows adapter against the shared service, with fake-source tests for selection, metadata/freshness, unsupported controls, duplicate commands and uncertain results. Preserve the Sony source and explicitly selected target when both are present.
- [ ] **AC3.** Run all applicable hub/shared checks and repository delivery gates. Add only the owning Windows adapter's setup and test instructions.
- [ ] **AC4.** After separate installation/control authorization, record an installed check: real track changes reach the hub and supported commands affect Apple Music only. No installed success is claimed by fake tests.

## Dependencies and status

Required source contract: [shared playback and Sony delivery](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175). Revisit whether Windows integration is needed after the Sony path is useful; this is a preference/readiness decision, not an implementation blocker for the initial music work. Keep status:backlog and deferred until selected and refined. Complexity and uncertainty remain medium until host placement is qualified.

No catalog search, library/queue selection, audio capture, new display/lighting implementation or Docker migration is included. [#178](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/178) separately investigates chosen-item playback.

Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md), and the owning hub/development guides. Use an exact issue-linked OpenSpec change, an isolated delivery worktree, independent Standards and Specification reviews of the same committed base/head, applicable local and current-head CI checks, guarded merge, and merged-revision CI. This tracker revision authorizes no implementation, installation, personal configuration, account connection, or device operation. Installed checks require a named owner and explicit target/sequence authorization; keep credentials, receiver addresses and private listening data out of Git.

## Historical probe context (September 22, 2026)

The recorded host was Windows 11 build 26200 with `AppleInc.AppleMusicWin` 1.1540.23042.0. A read-only PowerShell probe launched from WSL enumerated media sessions. This does not establish the current app's fields or command behavior. The former Python connector, separate qualification document and notification-count requirements are superseded by the deferred scope above. The probe below is retained as a reference; it is not an instruction to run it in this tracker task.

## Read-only probe


PowerShell 5.1, launched from WSL with `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File <\\wsl.localhost path>` or run on Windows. It reads only; it sends no commands.

```powershell
[Windows.Media.Control.GlobalSystemMediaTransportControlsSessionManager, Windows.Media.Control, ContentType = WindowsRuntime] | Out-Null
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Runtime.WindowsRuntime
$asTask = ([System.WindowsRuntimeSystemExtensions].GetMethods() | Where-Object { $_.Name -eq 'AsTask' -and $_.GetParameters().Count -eq 1 -and $_.GetParameters()[0].ParameterType.Name -eq 'IAsyncOperation`1' })[0]
function Await($op, $type) { $t = $asTask.MakeGenericMethod($type).Invoke($null, @($op)); $t.Wait(-1) | Out-Null; $t.Result }
$mgr = Await ([Windows.Media.Control.GlobalSystemMediaTransportControlsSessionManager]::RequestAsync()) ([Windows.Media.Control.GlobalSystemMediaTransportControlsSessionManager])
foreach ($s in $mgr.GetSessions()) {
  "--- source=$($s.SourceAppUserModelId)"
  $pi = $s.GetPlaybackInfo(); "status=$($pi.PlaybackStatus) next=$($pi.Controls.IsNextEnabled) prev=$($pi.Controls.IsPreviousEnabled) pause=$($pi.Controls.IsPauseEnabled)"
  $tl = $s.GetTimelineProperties(); "position=$($tl.Position) end=$($tl.EndTime) updated=$($tl.LastUpdatedTime)"
  $mp = Await ($s.TryGetMediaPropertiesAsync()) ([Windows.Media.Control.GlobalSystemMediaTransportControlsSessionMediaProperties])
  "title=$($mp.Title) | artist=$($mp.Artist) | album=$($mp.AlbumTitle) | albumArtist=$($mp.AlbumArtist) | track=$($mp.TrackNumber) | thumbnail=$($null -ne $mp.Thumbnail)"
  if ($mp.Thumbnail) { $st = Await ($mp.Thumbnail.OpenReadAsync()) ([Windows.Storage.Streams.IRandomAccessStreamWithContentType]); "thumbnailType=$($st.ContentType) size=$($st.Size)" }
}
```

body:

Use the source-independent playback interface delivered in [#175](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175), initially backed by Sony. Expose only controls qualified for that source: Sony pause/next/previous; play/resume remains unavailable until qualified in [the Sony resume follow-up](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/242). That follow-up does not block the supported controls here. Make unsupported controls and unavailable sources clear. Optional artwork acquisition is separately tracked in [playback artwork story](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/229). This issue owns its later UI presentation, while [#38](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/38) owns display resizing/rendering. Artwork is not a completion requirement for the text-only UI and controls. Keep controls bound to the source shown; source-selection UI is only needed when another real source is delivered. ## Required scope when refined

- Extend the existing authorization setup so intended browser-launch sessions and Codex MCP clients can read and, when granted, control their configured playback source. Browser-launch sessions currently have no playback grant. Keep browser sessions and machine credentials within their existing boundaries; grant only the required source-scoped read/control access, without broad device, ingestion or administrative access.
- Bind every command to the displayed/requested source. Show controls only when both source capability and client permission allow them. Cover read-only access, denied source access and unsupported commands with focused tests using the existing authorization model.
- Include separately authorized installed browser and actual Codex MCP checks: read the current snapshot and issue a supported command to the intended source. Record real client behavior separately from fake-service tests and transport acknowledgments. Apply the existing UI approval requirement.
- When artwork is added, acceptance must include visible current-track artwork, updates after track/source changes and a readable fallback when artwork is absent. [#229](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/229) must retain an open UI rendering story if this text-only issue closes first; artwork does not block this initial delivery.

body:
