Make observed song transitions trigger approved lighting effects on participating devices, beginning with Nanoleaf. This is a planned follow-up to [shared playback and Sony delivery](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175), not part of its initial now-playing/transport delivery.

This story already tracked song-change lighting. Owner clarification, September 24, 2026: it also owns the transition-detection work removed from the initial playback feature; the feature remains wanted.

## Scope and acceptance to refine

- [ ] **AC1.** Add source-aware transition detection over the shared normalized playback snapshots. Keep this logic independent of Sony so future sources can use it. Choose a small in-process subscription or polling implementation here; no pre-existing SSE feed is required.
- [ ] **AC2.** Define and test metadata comparison/track identity, duplicate reads, missing metadata and stale/recovered observations. Initial connection, reconnect and an explicit source switch initialize a baseline rather than firing an old effect. Start with title/artist/album comparison; same-song repeats and identical-metadata tracks may remain indistinguishable unless a qualified source supplies better identity. Document the chosen policy before implementation.
- [ ] **AC3.** Let the owner choose participating targets and song-to-effect/scene behavior. Consume the participation/interruption policy from [#40](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/40) and preserve manual ownership, native modes and scene restoration. Refine required policy/scene dependencies before readiness; no automatic behavior is enabled by this issue update.
- [ ] **AC4.** Send effects only through the existing owning controller queue. Use fake playback/controller tests for a changed song, duplicates, stale input, source change and alert/manual interruption; separately authorize a real playback and visible-lighting check.

Separately qualify Nanoleaf Rhythm scenes where selected. Metadata-triggered lighting is decorative; measured audio response remains [#41](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/41). Artwork is not required for basic song transitions. UI, richer scene mapping and exact physical targets need refinement before implementation.

body:

Ordinary bridge networking is a candidate to verify, not an installed guarantee; hub bind address, published ports, Host/Origin checks and credentials must be qualified together. Preserve existing access boundaries. Live receiver checks require explicit target/sequence authorization. ## Outcome and accepted decision

Adopt a fresh Linux installation of the Nanoleaf runtime in Ubuntu WSL on the existing PC. Keep the separate Linux processes, shared Linux SQLite state, and existing single light writer. The accepted fresh-install scope supersedes this issue's earlier placeholder requirement for state preservation and reversible Windows migration.

Existing Nanoleaf data need not be imported or preserved. Preserve unrelated applications, hooks, and Codex data. Retain Windows Desktop/browser clients and read configured Desktop JSON metadata through the mounted filesystem. Native Windows task execution is outside this transition.

This issue is blocked by the installed-acceptance issue, which is blocked by source delivery. Keep this issue open until both linked outcomes and documentation synchronization are complete. Hub documentation may be drafted alongside source implementation. The source issue does not wait for this issue to close.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] C1. Link the Nanoleaf source and installed-acceptance issues as the respective owners. Retain this issue until their required outcomes and documentation synchronization are complete.
- [x] C2. Update canonical architecture guidance and the maintained work guide through a linked Hub companion PR. Clearly distinguish proposed, source-delivered, and installed behavior.
- [x] C3. Show Linux hooks, wall map, and controller coordinating through Linux SQLite; the existing on-demand worker writing to Nanoleaf; and MCP communicating directly with the controller over HTTP.
- [x] C4. Retain Windows Desktop/browser clients and mounted JSON metadata reads in the diagrams. Remove Windows executable forwarding from the proposed Linux runtime.
- [x] C5. Record documentation validation results and linked source/acceptance evidence. Guide synchronization remains pending until its companion PR and required validation are complete.

## Verification and delivery

All checks below are planned, not executed evidence.

| Criteria | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| C1 | Read back both owning issues and native dependencies. Confirm completion evidence separately for reviewed source and installed operation, with no cycle that blocks source delivery on this coordination issue. |
| C2 | Linked Hub companion PR with refreshed owning guide inputs, generated HTML, and a dated updates.md entry. Verify primary issue coverage and source/installed status against GitHub evidence. |
| C3, C4 | Review diagrams and their pinned source receipts against the accepted process, database, HTTP, metadata, and device-writer paths. Inspect desktop, mobile, and print rendering using the guide procedure. |
| C5 | Recorded documentation checks at the reviewed candidate plus source and installed-acceptance links. Never treat the source merge or a diagram as proof of installed behavior. |

Follow AGENTS.md, docs/sdlc.md, and docs/work-guide/README.md. Use the installed archify skill when changing diagrams. Preserve independent Standards and Specification review, applicable hosted CI, and any applicable human UI approval gate. The Nanoleaf issue owns the runtime OpenSpec/design/ADR; reference it rather than defining a competing product contract here.

## Scope boundaries and related work

- The monorepo move at https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/26 is separate. Runtime ownership changes do not relocate repository ownership.
- Shared monitoring, Docker hosting, additional devices, data migration, rollback tooling, a combined daemon, and a new hook API are excluded.
- https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/11 retains its broader persistent-display requirements. The Linux source issue covers only the port and URL behavior needed for this installation.
- Preserve the future-work guide relationship at https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/35 and the local-first direction in [ADR 0004](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/decisions/0004-local-first-personal-assistant.md).

This tracker update does not implement the services, update repository documentation, install anything, modify hooks, or operate lights. Work-guide synchronization is pending the companion PR tracked here.

## Planning assessment

Assessed 2026-09-09 against Nanoleaf main `ea3b95661352f927aceaf92b62d74660978c201f` and Hub main `2564a357ec7d1a72c5525c0f36b98287244a6e89`.

- Impact: low. This issue coordinates tracking and documentation; its children own runtime and operational consequences.

The overall transition is estimated at 2–4 focused engineering days, excluding review and scheduling delays. This is not an additional per-issue estimate.

title: Document PC and desk lighting and initialize the implementation backlog
body:
## Outcome

Record the accepted PC and desk lighting direction in the hub documentation and create lightweight GitHub issues to refine closer to implementation.

## Accepted scope

Target Corsair Dominator Platinum RGB DDR5 memory and supported H150i ELITE LCD XT lighting, plus Lian Li Strimer lighting and the Varmilo VA108M-RGB keyboard where compatible. Preserve iCUE, L-Connect 3 and the existing lighting and keyboard setup. Strimer and keyboard qualification and delivery must not block a verified Corsair release; keyboard support must not block Strimer either. Keep fan speeds, pump settings, cooler LCD content and wider motherboard/GPU lighting outside this feature.

The supplied screenshots identify the Corsair device names and an L-Connect 3 Strimer Plus Controller configured for 24-pin and dual 8-pin cables. They do not prove external API support, connected RGB fan count, exact Strimer cable generation, firmware, wiring or visible effects. Earlier hardware logs are historical evidence only.

Varmilo starts with whole-keyboard automatic agent-status lighting. Qualify existing supported interfaces and defer integration if none exists. A closed qualification issue with an unsupported result does not make implementation ready. Preserve normal typing, mappings, macros, lock indicators and stock firmware. Per-key notification mapping, custom USB protocol research, simulated keypress fallbacks and firmware replacement are outside this accepted path. The official vendor driver listing and generic Windows inventory do not establish a supported automation API.

## Documentation changes

- Add `controllers/pc-lighting/README.md` with the evidence, qualification questions, capability and ownership boundaries, and links to future work.
- Update `docs/architecture.md` with a Windows-local PC lighting adapter, one designated writer per target, preserved vendor applications and reuse of shared state/contracts.
- Update `docs/roadmap.md` with the workstream and required versus conditional dependencies.
- Add a discovery link in the root `README.md`, retaining the documentation-only implementation status.
- Create separate Corsair, Strimer and Varmilo qualification, implementation and physical acceptance placeholders, plus shared automatic-status and UI/MCP-control placeholders. Link them from the existing future-work guide without changing its priorities.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Document accepted scope, evidence limits, preserved applications, restoration requirements and independent Corsair/Strimer delivery with optional keyboard participation.
- [x] Reuse current controller contracts and shared state ownership; record missing RGB/channel contracts as future qualification work, not new wire values.
- [x] Publish linked skeleton issues marked as future backlog work with refinement questions, source prerequisites and separate installation/physical gates.
- [x] Verify native dependency relationships, issue readback and an acyclic prerequisite graph.
- [x] Validate documentation links and the repository workflow checks on Node 24.
- [x] Obtain independent Standards and Specification reviews of the same committed comparison, deliver through a guarded PR merge, and verify all merged-revision CI jobs before closing this documentation ticket.

## Product specification boundary

This change updates documentation and backlog routing only. It introduces no product behavior, runtime package, contract, service, installation or device operation, so no new OpenSpec capability or change is warranted. Future behavior changes need their own refined issue, OpenSpec artifacts and executable validation under `docs/sdlc.md`.

## Dependencies and delivery

No unfinished implementation prerequisite blocks this documentation work. Follow `AGENTS.md` and `docs/sdlc.md`; preserve all existing local Codex priorities and other worktrees. Future implementation issues remain open when this ticket completes. Hardware and installed-client evidence remain separate from documentation/source CI.


## Created skeleton issues

- [Qualify Corsair RAM and H150i lighting through iCUE](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/51)
- [Qualify Lian Li Strimer control while preserving L-Connect 3](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/52)
- [Implement the PC lighting controller with a qualified Corsair adapter](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/53)
- [Add the qualified Strimer adapter to the PC lighting controller](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/54)
- [Add shared automatic agent status to qualified PC lighting targets](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/55)
- [Expose qualified PC lighting controls through shared UI and MCP services](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/56)
- [Install and verify Corsair PC lighting status and restoration](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/57)
- [Install and verify Strimer lighting handoff and restoration](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/58)

- [Qualify Varmilo VA108M-RGB lighting through supported interfaces](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/60)
- [Add a qualified Varmilo keyboard adapter to PC lighting](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/61)
- [Install and verify Varmilo keyboard status without affecting typing](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/62)

Shared status #55 and controls #56 conditionally require #61 for keyboard participation. Their required source prerequisites do not depend on keyboard support.

## Delivery receipt — verified September 23, 2026

[PR #59](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/59) merged on September 10, 2026 as `f2b37b6c8db29411e34e8bcf1e73c50c47ff7fe7`. The merge is an ancestor of remote `main`, verified at `ff9d8c6b695aa668f1a54afaace57692da39eec5`. The four-file merge delivered the controller guide, architecture, roadmap and root discovery link. Later documentation maintenance in #170 replaced copied roadmap/dependency tables with canonical GitHub links; it does not undo this delivery.

The original receipt records independent read-only Standards and Specification reviews with no findings against base `a7b1aa0476c2f3e0561b5d53dbc8395353180d60` and candidate `baf2b0bc2eb2b7839afe98175d8f3c686e5860c4`. Both reviews used that same comparison. No new source change or review was needed for this tracker reconciliation. GitHub has no review submissions, inline comments or review threads on this PR. The historical merge command and its expected-head guard are not exposed by the current readback; this receipt verifies the resulting merge rather than claiming to have replayed that operation.

The original local evidence records Node 24.20.0 workflow checks and all 10 workflow tests passing, dependency setup with `npm ci`, unchanged manifests/lockfile, and two OpenSpec capabilities, zero active changes and two archived changes. No product delta required a new OpenSpec change. The closeout additionally checked whitespace and all 30 local Markdown file targets in the four delivered files at the merge revision.

All 13 configured jobs at the exact merge revision succeeded, with job and step readbacks:

- [Checks run 34537753088](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/34537753088): 12 successful jobs, covering workflow checks on Linux/Windows, controller contracts on Python 3.12/3.14 on both systems, MCP on both systems, and lifecycle contracts on Python 3.12/3.14 on both systems.
- [Work guide run 34537752995](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/34537752995): successful generation, output consistency, maintenance tests and browser checks.

These are the GitHub Actions workflows configured at the September 10 merge revision, before Depot adoption. They establish historical merged-revision validation; they are not substitute Depot evidence for a new candidate. The original billing-blocked attempts remain historical failures. The [PR run](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/34176141304) subsequently passed on attempt 2. No rerun or account-setting change was needed during this closeout.

All eleven skeleton issues #51-#58 and #60-#62 exist and remain linked from this issue and future-work guide #35. Fresh native-relationship reads verified all 52 edges of the 29-issue transitive prerequisite graph in both directions, with no cycles. Ten skeletons remain open with `status:backlog` and `deferred`; #54 had already been closed separately on September 10. Its existing state was preserved and is not evidence of installed or physical Strimer support. No linked issue or dependency was changed during closeout.

This completes the documentation/backlog ticket. Qualification, runtime implementation, installation and physical acceptance remain separate work. No service, personal configuration or device was changed. No public guide was published or claimed current by this closeout.

title: Implement Work, Free and Quiet desk preset coordination
body:
## Outcome

Apply Work, Free or Quiet to explicitly configured Nanoleaf and Pixoo participants through the existing hub and owning controller services. Keep this personal-project feature small: fixed mode mappings, one active preset request, no saved restoration baseline and no background enforcement.

Owner-approved scope reduction, September 24, 2026. This replaces the earlier broad coordination investigation and rapid-replacement requirements. It changes the planned behavior, not delivery status.

## Fixed preset behavior

| Desk preset | Nanoleaf | Pixoo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Work | Request native Work mode. | Request native Monitor mode. |
| Free | Request native Free mode. | Request native Media mode. |
| Quiet | Request native Quiet mode. | Request native Monitor mode; issue no additional brightness or animation commands. |

Use each controller's supported native API and exact wire values. The table names device behavior, not a new common controller mode enum. Native mode policies own brightness, presentation and any scene/media handoff. Quiet does not promise a subdued Pixoo presentation in this release.

Free delegates to native Free/Media behavior. The hub does not capture pre-Work settings, choose a saved scene or playlist, or guarantee restoration of arbitrary previous content. Manual device-app changes persist until the next explicit preset request and its supported ownership handoff; the service cannot bypass an external owner.

## Implementation boundary

- Add one small module inside the existing hub process. Expose the same operation through `POST /api/hub/v1/desk-preset` with `{preset: "Work" | "Free" | "Quiet"}` and an MCP `desk_preset_set` tool. Follow the host's existing authentication, request-validation and authorization conventions.
- Configure participation as an explicit list of existing registered device aliases in hub configuration. No discovery, new device destinations, participation editor or custom preset editor. Reject invalid participant configuration; do not invent failed rows for unknown devices.
- Require control authority for every configured participant before sending any device command. A caller lacking that authority receives a rejection with no device writes. Empty participation produces an explicit unavailable result, not successful application.
- Read each participant's current snapshot and capabilities, then submit its one native mode command with the owning API's request identity, revision and generation guards. Resolve exact API compatibility in the issue-linked specification before coding. Use existing controller clients and queues; introduce no physical writer or shared controller-database access.
- Process devices independently with bounded snapshot/command waits. Unsupported capabilities, an unavailable controller or a failed device request produce a per-device result without preventing supported participants from running. A capability declaration alone does not establish preset compatibility.
- Admit one preset invocation at a time across HTTP and MCP. Keep a process-local busy flag until that invocation's bounded per-device calls have settled; release it on all exit paths. Reject overlapping invocations as busy without queuing, cancelling or replacing them. Existing controller queues still own commands already admitted downstream. Do not promise atomic desk changes or last-request-wins behavior.
- Return per-device receipts or typed failures using their existing queued, sent, failed, partially-applied, uncertain and cancelled meanings. Do not collapse them to `ok/error`, claim all devices reached the requested state, or treat a timeout as proof that no command took effect. No new result taxonomy or operation-history service is needed.
- Retain no durable selected preset, restoration baseline or request history. No automatic retries, rollback, startup commands, reconnect replay, polling to enforce a preset or restart recovery of pending writes. New explicit requests read fresh state and respect controller conflicts or uncertainty holds.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Bounded specification.** Create issue-linked OpenSpec artifacts for the fixed matrix, participant configuration, native API mapping, shared HTTP/MCP operation, busy behavior and result contract. Record native Free/Media limitations. Update affected architecture/development documentation within implementation scope; the broad investigation backlog is superseded by these bounded decisions.
- [ ] **AC2 — Shared implementation.** HTTP and MCP call the same hub operation, use configured participants and existing authentication/guards/queues, and preserve independent device failures. No dashboard UI or additional device family is required.
- [ ] **AC3 — Focused fake-controller validation.** Cover the three mappings; both entry points; invalid input, empty participation and unauthorized requests with zero writes; unsupported and slow/offline participants; overlap returning busy and releasing the flag after failure; stale/manual-change conflicts without automatic overwrite; preservation of queued/partial/uncertain receipts; and restart/reconnect producing no commands. Exercise the new composition without duplicating the full downstream controller test suites.
- [ ] **AC4 — Delivery evidence.** Pass applicable repository checks, independent Standards and Specification reviews, current-head hosted CI and merged-revision checks. Reviews cover the small module's authentication, ownership and concurrency behavior. Report source and transport outcomes separately from installation and physical observations.

All verification above is planned, not executed. Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [SDLC](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md), [controller contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/controller-contract.md) and [ADR 0005](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/decisions/0005-general-device-controls.md).

## Scope and follow-up boundaries

- No dashboard buttons in this issue. HTTP/MCP provide explicit preset selection; physical binding and on-screen feedback remain in [#68](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/68).
- This issue does not supply #68's currently specified authoritative cycle selection/revision state. Reconcile that requirement before implementing the binding. Do not infer a desk-wide current preset from one Nanoleaf device or add an independent client counter implicitly. #68 is not changed by this scope update.
- Installation, binding verification, manual handoff and visible restoration remain in [#69](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/69). Do not fold or close that issue based on source tests or a three-mode smoke test. Device work requires its existing explicit target and operation authorization.
- Tidbyt, LIFX and PC lighting participation remain future work requiring their own supported hub integration and defined preset mapping. Existing controller availability does not automatically enroll a device family.
- Desktop-input decisions, including the exclusion of keyboard A/B and attached Super Buttons from preset bindings, remain in [desktop-controls.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/desktop-controls.md). This feature does not block independent Codex mouse delivery.
- Source delivery does not install software, alter personal configuration, launch agent sessions or contact physical devices. Keep credentials and private runtime state outside Git.

## Readiness and assessment

All six recorded source prerequisites were verified closed on September 24, 2026:

- [Hub #63](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/63)
- [Hub #32](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/32)
- [Hub #31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31)
- [Hub #5](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/5)
- [Nanoleaf #49](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/49)
- [Pixoo #33](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/33)

The earlier dependency-blocked wording is superseded. Labels and native dependency relationships are unchanged by this tracker-only revision. The bounded specification and exact native API verification precede implementation; this update claims no source, installation or physical completion.

Reassessment: complexity medium, uncertainty low-to-medium, impact medium. Fixed one-command mappings and no persistent coordination reduce the work substantially; authorization, snapshot-to-command conflicts and partial results still require focused validation. Hub owns implementation and API notes; existing device owners retain their writers and native behavior. Reassess if scope expands to compound actions, durable cycling, automatic recovery or additional device families.

title: Verify desk preset switching, manual handoff and restoration
body:
## Outcome

Verify the delivered configured preset-binding path across an explicitly identified set of supported devices after source delivery and separately authorized installation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Record participating devices, configured target identities/endpoints, supported operations, baseline presentation and installed versions. Authorize the exact sequence before physical changes.
- [ ] **AC2.** Verify Work, Free and Quiet visibly on each selected target, including status from authorized real agent sessions when testing the full lifecycle.
- [ ] **AC3.** Make a manual change in a vendor app. Confirm it remains until the next explicit configured preset request, then verify supported handoff and restoration.
- [ ] **AC4.** Verify one offline/slow device, mixed native modes, unknown/unsupported capabilities, rapid presses of the selected preset binding, concurrent frontend control, sleep/reconnect and restart. The display must show actual partial/uncertain outcomes.
- [ ] **AC5.** Confirm reconnect does not replay historical presses and source/transport success is not presented as optical confirmation.
- [ ] **AC6.** Confirm unrelated mouse input, normal typing, keyboard-owned A/B mappings and cooling controls remain untouched; no Wispr trial is required. Restore baseline presentation and record the result.
- [ ] **AC7.** Publish separate source, installation, real-client, transport and per-device visible/restoration evidence. Mark missing targets as unverified.

The source prerequisite on #8 supplies the shared producer setup for full installed agent-status acceptance. Additional device qualification/install gates remain conditional on the selected target set. Future PC/keyboard lighting participates only after its own capability and physical-acceptance work; it does not block the existing supported devices. Missing permissions or hardware are future acceptance gaps, not authority granted by this ticket.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, September 7, 2026. Source baseline: [hub main a7b1aa0](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/tree/a7b1aa0476c2f3e0561b5d53dbc8395353180d60), live prerequisite issues, and the user-confirmed decisions below. Uses the canonical [work-assessment contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-skills/blob/22588b494cac646bd6eaa5e2f01b8d439ab6a60e/skills/deliver-work/references/work-assessment.md).

- **Complexity: high.** Several installed controllers and agent lifecycle sources must be observed through failures and manual changes.
- **Uncertainty: medium.** The runbook can be bounded after source delivery, but actual target capabilities and physical outcomes remain unverified.
- **Impact: medium.** The sequence changes personal device presentation; each target needs a known restoration path.

**Evidence limits and unknowns:** Selected installed devices, current app/firmware versions, user-authorized sequence and per-target visible results.

**Readiness:** Blocked by preset-binding delivery and shared producer setup. Physical execution additionally needs the selected devices, their applicable qualification/install gates, a named operator and explicit authorization.

### Planned acceptance evidence

All checks below are planned and unexecuted. Proposed paths and commands are not delivery receipts.

| Criterion | Planned verification and limitation |
| --- | --- |
| AC1 | Preflight the named operator, configured target inventory, qualified modes and baseline/rollback record before any authorized physical writes. |
| AC2 | User-observed Work/Free/Quiet sequence with authorized real agent activity verifies each target; keep optical outcomes distinct from producer and transport receipts. |
| AC3 | Change a scene/mode in the native app, wait to confirm it persists, then explicitly request the next preset and observe qualified handoff/restoration. |
| AC4 | Execute the approved failure/lifecycle matrix and compare visible behavior with per-device feedback. Record partial outcomes rather than treating the desk as atomic. |
| AC5 | Reconnect after an interrupted request and inspect fresh state; confirm no missed press is replayed and no sent receipt is labeled optical proof. |
| AC6 | Observe ordinary input and unaffected cooling controls, then restore the baseline. Do not record typed or dictated content. |

- [ ] **AC2.** Let users assign registered app/hub actions and custom keyboard shortcuts with explicit application scope. Include save, named-profile selection and restoration of defaults; settle profile lifecycle details during refinement.
- [ ] **AC3.** Switching a control profile alone changes no lights or displays. A binding may explicitly invoke a desk preset when its service is available.
- [ ] **AC4.** Allow useful local profile actions when the hub is unavailable. Identify unavailable integrations and shortcut collisions before activation; do not silently redirect a binding to another action.
- [ ] **AC5.** Preserve normal input outside the configured scope. Validate profile changes while controls/modifiers are held, action removal, disconnect, restart, invalid configuration and rollback without replaying old presses.
- [ ] **AC6.** Keep arbitrary scripts, shell execution, raw device commands and multi-step macros outside this first editor. Existing vendor configuration must not compete with the selected mapping owner.
- [ ] **AC7.** Define the editor's UI host, versioned configuration format, migration, atomic save and personal-data storage before implementation. Obtain actual UI approval and separate physical acceptance from fake tests.

title: Fix diagram connectors hidden behind boxes in the work guide
body: ## Failure and reproduction In the work guide's "Where we're going" section, connector lines and arrowheads disappear behind boxes. Readers cannot reliably follow a connection from its source to its intended destination. Hovering or focusing a node highlights its connections, but portions remain obscured. The user's screenshot shows this around **Shared Codex integration**, with several highlighted connections crossing intermediate rows of boxes. The affected routes include its connections to **Automatic status**, **Corsair controller + status**, and **PC / container hosting**. 1. Open `docs/work-guide/outputs/agent-device-work-guides.html` in a browser. 2. Expand "Delivery history and ordered roadmap" and scroll to "Where we're going". 3. Hover over or keyboard-focus "Shared Codex integration". 4. Follow its highlighted connections into the lower tracks. Portions disappear beneath intermediate boxes, making the destination difficult to identify. 5. Check the default, unhighlighted state and other nodes with connections between tracks for the same obstruction. Browser version and viewport for the original capture were not supplied. Source pointers: - [Generated guide](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/7464b9e669c7150f780b334a3429c5f30a89b438/docs/work-guide/outputs/agent-device-work-guides.html), section `#timeline`, SVG `.roadmap`. - [Roadmap generator](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/7464b9e669c7150f780b334a3429c5f30a89b438/docs/work-guide/work/timeline.py#L167), `roadmap_map()`. It emits connector elements before node rectangles and draws connections between tracks as curves without checking intervening boxes. This is consistent with the reported obstruction; the implementation should verify routing, layering and marker clearance. - Inspected main HTML SHA-256: `8385675bb5dc6801de4c5f99e377caea2d281a2102ab6ce75b265bbac4cea6b3`. ## Expected behavior and acceptance criteria - [ ] Every roadmap connection can be followed continuously to the intended destination. Intermediate boxes do not conceal the line or arrowhead. - [ ] Arrowheads remain visible at their intended destination boundaries. Connections do not cross unrelated box text or imply a connection to an intermediate box. - [ ] Fix all occurrences of this defect on the page. Audit the full roadmap, history chart, overview sequence and all eight inline architecture/sequence diagrams. Record the sections checked and any additional occurrences corrected. Check corresponding companion viewers when they share an affected diagram. - [ ] Connections remain clear in the default view, during mouse hover and keyboard focus, and with repository filters applied. Preserve the meaning of solid versus dashed connections and the underlying dependencies. - [ ] Verify desktop and narrow layouts, browser zoom, diagram zoom/panning where supported, and print output. Preserve node links, tooltips, search, navigation and expand/collapse behavior. - [ ] Correct the owning generator or diagram inputs and regenerate affected outputs so rebuilding the guide retains the fix. - [ ] Include before/after visual evidence and obtain human approval of the current visual candidate before delivery. ## Dependencies, verification and delivery target The hub owns this guide under `docs/work-guide`, adopted in https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/72. This defect concerns the guide's presentation; its repair does not depend on implementing the product milestones shown in the diagrams. Current authorization is **ticket creation only**. No implementation, document changes, regeneration, deployment or device operations are requested in this task. Additional affected sections beyond the reported roadmap remain an explicit audit requirement; this ticket does not claim they are defect-free. ## Evidence Example: file://wsl$/Ubuntu/tmp/hub-work-guide-sdlc/docs/work-guide/outputs/agent-device-work-guides.html#timeline

title: Restyle the guide and atlas in the Neon skin
body:
Owner: Hub guide and atlas source.

## Outcome

Restyle the public work guide and the atlas in the Neon Geometry Wars skin, readable on a phone. Build it so a later skin is a new set of token values, not new templates or generator changes.

V1 ships one skin. The alternate skin and a skin picker with a saved preference are deferred to a separate issue.

## Scope

- **Tokens.** Guide and atlas styles use CSS custom properties named for their roles (surfaces, text, borders, selection, pending, status, diagram edges, radius, type scale, spacing). The Neon skin supplies their values for dark and light. Fixed-meaning colors (cyan Hub, magenta Nanoleaf, lime Pixoo, status colors) live in a separate token set that skins don't override.
- **Decoration.** Neon's artwork, glow, opening and streak are scoped to the skin. CSS animations only, with no JavaScript render loop or timers. Decoration sits on borders and artwork, never on text or dependency edges, and never signals live agent or device activity. Starting values: a ~2 s opening and a ~1 s streak every 25 s; tune by eye.
- **Motion off.** A pause control and `prefers-reduced-motion` stop all decorative motion. Print shows no decoration.
- Change the generators and assets (`docs/work-guide/work/build_guide.py`, `docs/system-design/build.py`), not generated output. Bundle artwork; add no remote requests.
- If [#196](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/196)'s brief dialog or [#197](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/197)'s status line has merged, style it too. Neither blocks this issue.

## Acceptance

1. At 390 and 1440 px, in dark and light, the guide (header, navigation, cards, issue badges, status, inline diagrams) and the atlas use the Neon skin. The owner approves the atlas candidate, as `docs/sdlc.md` requires; the guide needs no approval.
2. Colors in guide and atlas styles come from tokens. A check fails on color literals outside the token files.
3. Pause and reduced motion stop all decorative motion. Every page stays readable and usable with motion off. Decoration stays out of the tab order and never covers controls.
4. The guide README has a short section listing the tokens and how to add a skin.
5. Existing checks pass, plus the checks in AC2 and AC3.

Evidence: before/after screenshots at 390 and 1440 px in the PR, and these runs:
- guide: `python3 docs/work-guide/work/build_guide.py`, `python3 docs/work-guide/work/test_maintenance.py`, `node docs/work-guide/work/check_guide.cjs`
- atlas: `python3 docs/system-design/build.py` and its `--check` mode, `python3 docs/system-design/check.py`, `node docs/system-design/check.cjs`

## Delivery

Follow [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md). The atlas lives outside `docs/work-guide/`, so normal CI applies. No product contract changes, so no OpenSpec change. [#87](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/87) publishes the result.

This issue absorbs #86. [#181](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/181) is not a prerequisite; it can adopt these token names for the apps later.

Out of scope: the nine Archify architecture viewers (they keep Archify's styling), the alternate skin and picker, composition comparisons, the finish-kit fingerprint, frame-rate budgets and phone measurements, the [#73](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/73) connector fix, React adoption ([#182](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/182)) and publication (#87).

Assessment: complexity medium (two generators, token conversion, motion), uncertainty low, impact low (reversible styling). Ready.

title: Apply the Neon skin to the guide and atlas
body:
Owner: Hub guide and atlas source.

Outcome: the work guide and the atlas use the Neon Geometry Wars design selected in [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85), and read well on a phone.

Required inputs: [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85)'s selected design (composition, colors, type, artwork and motion values) and [#181](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/181)'s semantic roles.

## Scope

- Apply #85's design to the guide (header, navigation, cards, issue badges, status and inline diagrams) and to the atlas. Change the generators and assets (`docs/work-guide/work/build_guide.py`, `docs/system-design/build.py`), not generated output.
- Define the skin as CSS custom properties named after #181's semantic roles, so a later skin is a new set of values rather than new templates.
- Keep dark/light behavior, the repository colors (cyan Hub, magenta Nanoleaf, lime Pixoo) and status meanings. Decorative light never signals live agent or device activity.
- Build the opening and the occasional streak with CSS animations only: no JavaScript rendering loop or timers. A pause control and `prefers-reduced-motion` stop them. Start from #85's values; the historical targets are a roughly two-second opening and a one-second streak every 25 seconds.
- Bundle the artwork; add no remote art requests.
- If [#196](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/196)'s brief dialog or [#197](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/197)'s status line has merged, style it too. Neither blocks this issue.

## Acceptance

1. At 390 and 1440 px, in dark and light, the guide and atlas match #85's selected design. The owner approves the atlas candidate, as `docs/sdlc.md` requires for atlas UI; the guide needs no approval.
2. Pause and reduced motion stop all decorative motion, and every page stays readable and usable with motion off. Decoration stays out of the tab order and never covers controls.
3. The existing guide and atlas checks pass, plus one check that pause and reduced motion stop the animations.

Evidence: before/after screenshots at 390 and 1440 px in the PR, and these runs:
- guide: `python3 docs/work-guide/work/build_guide.py`, `python3 docs/work-guide/work/test_maintenance.py`, `node docs/work-guide/work/check_guide.cjs`
- atlas: `python3 docs/system-design/build.py` and its `--check` mode, `python3 docs/system-design/check.py`, `node docs/system-design/check.cjs`

## Delivery

Follow [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md). The atlas lives outside `docs/work-guide/`, so normal CI applies rather than the guide-only exception. No product contract changes, so no OpenSpec change. [#87](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/87) publishes the result.

Deferred: the alternate skin and a skin picker with a saved preference. Their look isn't chosen yet; open a separate issue once #85 or #181 settles it. The nine Archify architecture viewers keep Archify's own styling and themes.

Out of scope: frame-rate budgets and phone performance measurements, controlled-clock motion tests, bundle-size and provenance reports, the [#73](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/73) connector fix, React adoption ([#182](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/182)) and publication (#87).

Assessment: complexity medium (two generators plus motion), uncertainty low once #85 is done, impact low (reversible styling). Blocked by #85 and #181.

title: Publish and verify the first mobile guide workspace and atlas
body:
Owner: Hub guide publication.

Outcome: the public guide and atlas at their existing URLs include the Neon/Prism presentation, task briefs and live GitHub status, and they work on a phone without signing in.

Required inputs, all merged first: [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85) presentation, [#196](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/196) task briefs and [#197](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/197) live status. This issue publishes them and adds no features.

## Steps

Follow [Publish the public edition](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/work-guide/README.md#publish-the-public-edition): export from the merged Hub revision, open the public-repository PR, merge it and check the Pages deployment. Keep the current `/`, `/architecture/` and `/atlas/` paths.

The hub repository is now public (checked September 23, 2026). Re-check it, then correct the wording that calls it private in the public README and in `docs/work-guide/README.md`.

## Acceptance

1. Over unauthenticated HTTPS, the landing page, the nine architecture viewers and every exported atlas file match the hashes from the merged Hub revision.
2. On a real phone, open an issue, copy one brief into a Codex or Claude app, see the live GitHub status line, pause the motion, open the atlas and return.

One closing comment records the Hub revision, public PR, Pages run, hash result, and the phone and browser used.

## Delivery

The procedure's gates apply to the public PR: independent Standards and Specification reviews, a guarded merge and no `--admin`. Human approval of atlas UI belongs to #85's source PR; guide UI needs none. To roll back, revert the public PR.

Out of scope: refreshing local copies of the guide outside the repositories; separate evidence reports for each stage; outage or recovery demonstrations; print, offline and reduced-motion checks on the phone, which the guide and atlas checks in #85, #196 and #197 cover; new hosts, visibility changes and schedules.

Assessment: complexity low (one export and one public PR), uncertainty low, impact low (the previous edition stays one revert away). Blocked by #85, #196 and #197.

title: Reduce CI minutes while preserving all test coverage
body:
## Outcome and scope

Reduce GitHub Actions minutes for agent-device-hub while retaining every existing test, package-consumer check, and supported OS/Python combination on PRs and main. The accepted approach removes duplicate runs and compilation before considering any coverage reduction.

Planning baseline, refreshed September 10, 2026: main `396c36aed74cf1d016564536eca13bb16f89834b` still triggers Checks on every push and pull request. It has 12 jobs and 32 full-build invocations per workflow. [Successful core run 34426914343](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/34426914343) used approximately 13 raw runner-minutes, or 18 minutes after rounding each job upward. This is one observation, not monthly billing evidence. [PR #82](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/82) adds a guide browser workflow with the same duplicate triggers.

Authoritative delivery and validation policy: [SDLC](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md), [development](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/development.md), and [work-guide maintenance](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/work-guide/README.md). This is CI/tooling work with no product behavior or wire-contract delta; record that reason rather than inventing product OpenSpec scenarios.

## Planned implementation

Deliver two sequential PRs linked to this issue, keeping it open until both are verified.

1. Restrict push validation to `main`, preserve existing PR events, add workflow-level cancellation of superseded PR runs, and set ten-minute core job timeouts. Preserve matrix entries, job names, action pins, permissions, commands, and `fail-fast: false`. Apply equivalent scheduling to the guide workflow in coordination with PR #82. Use concurrency group `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true`; main runs remain independent, and matrix siblings must not cancel one another.
2. Build once per product job, retain its typecheck, and call build-free test variants. Add `:built` variants for `test:contracts`, `test:package`, `test:mcp`, `test:mcp:protocol`, `test:mcp:package`, `test:lifecycle`, and `test:lifecycle:package`. Each original command continues to build before invoking its variant, preserving clean-checkout developer behavior. Retain isolated archive installation, manifest/hash verification, full consumer tests, and consumer typechecking. Add setup-python pip download caching with `requirements-contracts.txt` as the dependency key; keep dependency installation, `npm ci`, and existing npm caching.

Do not remove tests, introduce path-based skipping, reduce platform/version coverage, defer coverage to scheduled runs, share compiled output or installed dependencies between jobs, change runner/billing/privacy settings, weaken merge gates, install software on personal devices, or operate devices. Browser caching, job consolidation, and artifact-retention changes are outside this item.

## Acceptance criteria and verification

- [x] An ordinary update to an open PR runs each applicable workflow once through `pull_request`, with no duplicate branch-push run. A merge to main still runs every configured validation job. Verify workflow configuration and hosted run event/head associations during normal delivery.
- [x] A superseded PR workflow can be cancelled without cancelling another PR, a main run, another workflow, or matrix siblings. Add focused configuration regression coverage and inspect natural overlapping hosted PR updates. If no overlap occurs, explicitly record runtime cancellation as unobserved; static checks alone do not prove scheduler behavior.
- [x] Every core job has a ten-minute timeout; the guide job retains its existing ten-minute timeout. Verify configuration without deliberately running a hung hosted job.
- [x] All 12 core job identities and the Ubuntu/Windows, Python 3.12/3.14, Node 24 coverage remain. Retain the guide job when introduced. Require successful current-head and merged-revision hosted jobs under existing delivery policy.
- [x] The core workflow performs 10 full builds rather than 32, with one build before each product job's tests and one typecheck per product job. Verify script expansion and build-before-test ordering. Compare test inventories/results between original standalone commands and the optimized sequence; a failed build must prevent downstream tests from running against stale output.
- [x] Existing standalone test commands work from a clean build state. All archive-consumer, tamper/hash, TypeScript, Python, and MCP protocol checks retain their behavior. Build-free variants consume only output freshly produced in the same job; do not reuse another run's output.
- [x] Python cache misses still install dependencies and pass tests; cache keys distinguish supported runtimes/platforms and dependency changes. No credentials, private state, or compiled artifacts enter new caches. Inspect setup-python cache configuration and normal hosted cold/warm evidence where available.
- [x] Report before/after job and step durations, raw runner-minutes, and rounded minutes by OS from comparable successful runs. Exclude billing-blocked runs from performance comparisons. Removing duplicate events should halve validation copies for an open-PR update; a one-update PR plus merge drops from three copies to two. These are scheduling estimates, not a guaranteed invoice reduction. Report additional build savings as measured, without a speculative target.
- [x] Update development documentation for equivalent CI commands and complete the work-guide maintenance record and affected inputs/output under delivery authority. Preserve guide browser checks and review-artifact retention.

Planned checks, not executed as part of issue publication: Node 24 `npm ci`, `npm run check:workflow`, `npm run test:workflow`, `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, all existing controller-contract, lifecycle, MCP and isolated-package commands, plus focused CI regression checks. Use Python 3.12 and 3.14 in the hosted matrix. Follow the work-guide procedure for generator, maintenance and browser verification where applicable, and report the actual specification inventory.

## Dependencies and coordination

No incoming implementation prerequisite was identified. [PR #82](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/82) owns the proposed guide workflow; coordinate its scheduling changes without taking over its branch or requiring unrelated guide/UI delivery first. The core optimization can proceed independently. Reconcile the guide workflow before claiming this issue's full scheduling scope complete. The second PR follows the first as the selected measurement and review sequence, not as a separate cross-issue dependency.

Use one coordinating writer for root scripts, manifests and CI. Refresh main, open PRs and affected instructions before editing. Preserve concurrent ownership and use isolated worktrees.

## Assessment and readiness

Planning assessment at the baseline above:

- Complexity: medium. Workflow concurrency, npm command composition, and cross-platform archive tests interact, but product state and APIs do not change.
- Uncertainty: low. Coverage preferences are settled and repeated triggers/builds are visible in source and hosted evidence. Remaining bounded questions are actual savings, cache effectiveness, and observable cancellation; resolve through configuration checks and normal hosted delivery evidence.
- Impact: medium. Incorrect scheduling or script ordering could undermine repository-wide validation. Preserve full coverage, fail on unsuccessful builds, and retain all existing review/merge gates.
- Readiness: ready for implementation planning and assignment; no unresolved product decision. Publication does not authorize implementation. Session reasoning setting: unknown.
- Reassess if main changes workflows/scripts, guide ownership changes, a test-equivalence check fails, or reviews reveal a coverage or cancellation gap.

Independent Standards and Specification reviewers must inspect the same committed base/head. Include concurrency and package-consumer compatibility in review scope. No new UI behavior is planned; any scope expansion into UI retains the repository's human approval gate. Close only after both PRs and their merged-revision CI satisfy acceptance. Recover regressions through a reviewed revert of the affected workflow/script change, preserving tests and coordinating shared files; do not bypass CI to recover.

## Publication boundary and guide checkpoint

The current request authorizes creation and readback of this issue only. No implementation, PR, guide-source edit, public publication, or live operation is authorized by this planning publication. Guide synchronization remains pending with the Hub planning/delivery coordinator: add this saved issue to the canonical backlog inputs, regenerate through the existing procedure, and record the result in `docs/work-guide/updates.md` when document edits are authorized. Public-site publication is separate and is not started by this issue.

title: Skip automatic CI for guide-only changes
body:
## Outcome and scope

Skip automatic Hub CI when every changed file is under `docs/work-guide/`, including guide generators, tests, snapshots, documentation and generated assets. Any change outside that directory retains normal CI. This scope was explicitly selected during planning.

The inspected main revision is `1fd353215532a5d0220b99d9b35b6da0436221cc`. The `Checks` and `Work guide` workflows currently have no guide-only path exclusion. Preserve the scheduling, timeouts, concurrency and build optimizations delivered under https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/91. That closed issue explicitly excluded path-based skipping; this is separate maintenance work.

Authoritative policy: [repository instructions](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [SDLC](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md), [development](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/development.md), and [guide maintenance and publication](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/work-guide/README.md).

## Planned implementation

- Add `paths-ignore: ['docs/work-guide/**']` to both `push` and `pull_request` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `.github/workflows/work-guide.yml`. Preserve main-only pushes, existing PR events, permissions, action pins, job identities, platform/version matrices, commands, concurrency and timeouts.
- Update AGENTS.md and the SDLC/development/guide procedures to permit intentionally filtered workflows only for verified guide-only changes. Cover PR merge, merged-revision readback, issue closure and the source-validation prerequisite for later public publication. An absent workflow is not automatically proof that filtering worked. Record the exact revision, complete changed-file scope and local guide validation evidence. Mixed changes retain every existing CI gate.
- Retain local generation, generated-output consistency, maintenance tests, browser verification and review artifacts for guide-only candidates. Independent Standards and Specification reviews, guarded merges and applicable current-candidate human UI approval remain required.
- Extend existing workflow regression coverage for the two filters while preserving the assertions for scheduling and all configured jobs.
- Update affected guide inputs/output and its maintenance record during authorized delivery. Treat proposed behavior as planned until delivered.

No product API, wire contract or runtime behavior changes. No dependency changes, new scheduler, custom path-classifier service, dummy success workflow, device operation, installation, public deployment or changes to another repository's workflows. Public publishing jobs remain unchanged. This is CI/tooling maintenance with no product capability delta; record that reason rather than inventing product OpenSpec scenarios.

## Acceptance criteria and planned verification

- [ ] Both workflows declare the exact guide-folder exclusion for PRs and main pushes. Parse their YAML in regression tests and confirm the existing scheduling, permissions, job identities, matrices, pins and commands remain intact.
- [ ] Guide-only changes skip both automatic workflows. Cover additions, edits and deletions in guide content, generators/tests and output; verify event/head associations on the subsequent normal guide-only reconciliation PR and its main merge. Record the compared revisions and changed paths. Absence of a run alone is insufficient evidence. Native GitHub path-filter limits remain applicable and must be documented rather than promising zero runs for every possible large diff.
- [ ] Mixed changes still run all configured jobs. Cover guide plus source, root documentation, dependency and workflow changes, including movement of files out of the guide folder. Verify normal hosted PR and main checks on the implementation delivery, which itself changes files outside the excluded folder.
- [ ] Guide-only merges retain successful local generation, maintenance and browser checks, generated-output consistency, review evidence and UI approval where required. Update all applicable instructions so intentional filtering is distinguished from missing, pending, failed or cancelled required CI. Mixed changes receive no exception.
- [ ] Confirm required-check compatibility before merge. Prior branch-protection and ruleset reads returned HTTP 403 and do not establish effective settings. Refresh those reads and inspect the candidate's authoritative merge/check state. If a required check blocks guide-only merging, stop that delivery gate and report the owner/action needed; do not use `--admin`, weaken protection, change account settings or substitute dummy success checks. GitHub documents that path-filtered required workflows can remain pending: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax .
- [ ] The implementation PR and merged revision pass every configured job under the existing policy. Record successful local workflow checks and the actual specification inventory. Reconcile guide history/status only from verified results, and report source synchronization, public publication and live verification separately.

Planned commands, not executed as part of issue publication: use Node 24, run `npm ci`, `npm run check:workflow`, `npm run test:workflow`, `python3 docs/work-guide/work/build_guide.py`, `git diff --exit-code -- docs/work-guide/outputs`, `python3 docs/work-guide/work/test_maintenance.py`, and `node docs/work-guide/work/check_guide.cjs`. Run generated-output consistency after intended output has been committed. Retain the current guide workflow's browser setup and preserve review artifacts outside Git. Delivery must run all other checks required by current repository policy and changed scope.

## Dependencies, coordination and recovery

No incoming implementation dependency was identified. #91 is delivered background, not an open blocker. One coordinating writer owns the shared CI and instruction changes in an isolated worktree based on refreshed main. Coordinate with concurrent guide work, including https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/99, without taking over its branch or making its merge an unnecessary prerequisite.

Independent read-only Standards and Specification reviewers inspect the same committed base/head, including filter semantics and the narrow delivery-policy exception. Recheck issue scope, base/head and all applicable checks before guarded squash merge. Observe normal hosted PR/main behavior; do not open disposable PRs merely to generate CI events. title: Re-evaluate Linux performance budgets and reduce hub memory use
body:
## Outcome
Re-evaluate the Linux/WSL performance budgets and reduce standalone hub memory use with reproducible measurements.

## Context and owner decision
During [Hub #5](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/5), the synthetic host workload completed 9,000 ingest/read pairs but reached 164.82 MiB peak RSS against the original 128 MiB service constraint. Four further diagnostic variants also exceeded that constraint. The receipts are retained in [PR #121](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/121), under `apps/hub/evidence/`.

The owner explicitly requested doubling the service RSS limit to **256 MiB** and creating this backlog item. This is a deliberate budget revision, not evidence that memory use improved. Preserve the original receipts and their failed results against 128 MiB. This follow-up is not a prerequisite for #5; that issue still requires its remaining functional acceptance and validation against the revised budget. Hook latency/CPU/child-RSS limits, queue/body limits and deadlines are unchanged by this decision.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Audit the scope and rationale of the existing budgets: service RSS versus JavaScript heap and native allocations, full-hook latency/CPU versus API timings, startup versus steady state, and isolated versus combined service memory.
- [ ] Define representative Linux/WSL workloads, including 1/10/50 sessions, longer-running steady state, bounded journal growth, SSE clients, replay retention and controller outages. Record versions, load, sampling and measurement boundaries.
- [ ] Profile allocations and retention to identify the causes of the observed memory use. Distinguish startup/JIT overhead, transient allocation, native SQLite/network allocations and leaks using evidence.
- [ ] Implement measured memory improvements without weakening durability, ownership, privacy, fail-open deadlines, retention or failure isolation. Retain before/after receipts and every failed trial.
- [ ] Propose justified service and end-to-end budgets with explicit headroom and regression checks. Retain 256 MiB until a separately reviewed change replaces it; do not silently rewrite historical results.
- [ ] Align the budget artifact, documentation and qualification checks with [integrated performance #30](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/30). Distinguish partial API measurements from full integrated qualification.

## Scope and verification
Linux in WSL is primary. Native Windows qualification, installation, live state migration and physical-device testing are outside this source follow-up. Use disposable state and fake controllers. Require independent review and applicable CI for future implementation.

Related: [Pixoo performance hardening #61](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/61). Coordinate shared measurement boundaries without absorbing that separately owned work.

## Planning
Backlog only; this issue does not start its implementation. Before implementation, prepare an issue-linked OpenSpec change if required by `docs/sdlc.md`.

title: Support best-effort Codex current status across successive turns
body:
## Outcome
Make ordinary successive Codex Desktop turns in Ubuntu WSL show Working, Finished and Working again through the shared monitor. V1 uses explicitly best-effort current status; reliable event history is a separate future capability.

## Evidence and accepted policy
The installed provider emits unknown ordering; the reducer intentionally makes successive unordered turns ambiguous. The source reproduction start(turn-one), stop(turn-one), start(turn-two) leaves activity unknown and the previous notice uncleared. Synthetic qualified ordering makes the same sequence pass. See [Pixoo #34 diagnosis](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/34#issuecomment-5769993937).

The owner accepted receipt order as a best-effort choice for a previously unseen valid turn start. This is a deliberate revision of the current conservative policy, not authoritative provider order. A delayed unseen start can temporarily select the wrong turn or prematurely clear a notice. Native turn IDs remain opaque. Do not fabricate provider sequence numbers or imply reliable history.

## Scope and acceptance criteria
- [x] A valid start with usable session/turn identity for a previously unseen turn selects that turn and sets activity active. A matching stop completes it and retains a completion notice without claiming success or readership.
- [x] A new selected turn clears only previous completion notices covered by each consumer's clearOnNewTurn policy. Manual dismissal remains notice/consumer-scoped; unresolved approval/input attention remains independent.
- [x] Known superseded-turn events and unchanged duplicates cannot overwrite current activity or restore cleared notices. Bound remembered identities; specify behavior when that bound is exhausted, including limits on rejecting very old events.
- [x] Missing identity or contradictory evidence remains visibly unknown. Preserve freshness timeout, restart uncertainty and session separation. Document the limitation for previously unseen delayed starts.
- [x] Existing sessions stuck in ambiguity recover through a valid fresh start under the new policy without deleting the database, labels, unrelated notices or attention. Provide a supported compatibility path if persisted format changes are needed.
- [x] Preserve available event/session/turn identity and genuine ordering evidence. Clearly separate observations, best-effort current-state calculation and the bounded diagnostic journal. No claim of complete durable event history or retroactive reliability.
- [x] Both Pixoo and Nanoleaf consume the shared result with their existing independent policies. Hooks remain silent, private, bounded, fail-open and independent of devices; preserve existing CLI/Claude compatibility through regression checks without expanding live-client qualification.
- [x] Package the fix reproducibly with version/hash/source receipt and concise installed-update instructions. No new installer, runtime-owner relocation or live database reset.

## Verification
Map the criteria to provider-to-reducer and packaged-hook regressions covering start/stop/next-start, delayed starts and stops, duplicate delivery, two sessions, bounded identity retention, restart, recovery from existing ambiguity, acknowledgment isolation and differing consumer policies. Retain privacy, authentication and hook-deadline checks. Use real consumer code with fake device transports. Synthetic ordering alone cannot satisfy the ordinary provider-path regression. Installation and the short real Desktop/Pixoo retest remain in Pixoo #34.

## Dependencies and coordination
Delivered Hub #2/#3/#8 contracts/state/setup are inputs; this is a focused follow-up, not a reopening of those deliveries. [Pixoo #34](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/divoom-app-upgrade/issues/34) consumes this fix and an installed update before resuming its lifecycle acceptance. Manual task reset and reliable history do not block #34.

Coordinate shared tests, packages and guide inputs with [Hub PR #135](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/135). Shared files are coordination, not a dependency on performance qualification. No required input from future history work.

## Exclusions
Reliable event capture/history/replay, new client/platform certification, frontend redesign, device rendering changes and an extended performance programme. Per-task manual reset is a separate follow-up.

## Assessment and readiness
Planning baseline: Hub main 25590e9c95ce334a516d2de0494584d67ea15a26 and observed installed failure, September 22, 2026. Complexity high: cross-process events, persisted state and two consumers. Uncertainty medium: bounded retention and compatibility details require design, while product tradeoff and reproduction are established. Impact medium: shared displayed status and notices; permission boundaries unchanged. Ready for implementation planning. Review transition/concurrency and persistence behavior within independent reviews. Reassess if required client identity is absent, a storage migration is necessary, or scope/base changes.

## Delivery and planning
Source-only delivery. Publication does not start implementation, installation, agent sessions or device operations. Use the assigned issue number for a new OpenSpec change under `openspec/changes/`; revise affected specifications and document consequential policy decisions before implementation. Preserve the archived earlier changes. Follow current AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md: isolated work, relevant tests, independent Standards and Specification reviews, applicable CI, guarded merge and merged-main verification. Publish new versioned artifacts rather than replacing released bytes. Synchronize the maintained Hub work guide during delivery; public publication remains separate.

Planning reasoning setting: unknown. No agents were dispatched for this planning publication.

Source delivery completed in [PR #144](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/144), merged as `013b829a851277cd0cfbaeaba6d6d0dfc32727c7`. Its tree matches reviewed head `b1eff926ed56a8264881023c814291da8d92b7c0`. Both independent reviews passed after the documented corrections; all six PR and all six merged-main jobs passed. Main receipts: [Checks](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/35682328106) and [Work guide](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/actions/runs/35682328098). GitHub recorded closure at merge time; this completion update follows verified main CI and artifact publication.

Published [agent-state 2.0.0](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/releases/tag/agent-state-v2.0.0) and [Hub 0.2.0](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/releases/tag/hub-v0.2.0), each with archive, checksum and merged-source receipt. title: Add reliable shared agent-event history as a separate capability
body:
## Outcome
Provide an evidenced agent-event timeline independently of the best-effort current-status display. This is a deferred feature capability, not a v1 delivery requirement or a ready implementation story.

## Refinement required before implementation
- [ ] Define what reliability guarantees for the chosen provider: capture completeness, event identity, ordering, delivery gaps and supported client paths. Record unsupported guarantees rather than promising exactly-once or total order without evidence.
- [ ] Decide retention duration, storage limits, pruning/deletion behavior and the minimum history inspection interface.

title: Add Pixoo general controls to the BUNNY component view
body:
## Outcome

Add Pixoo general controls to the existing Pixoo component view in BUNNY: screen power, brightness, saved-playlist selection and the six playback actions, usable without an active agent session.

## Scope and accepted definition

Implements the first slice of [#31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31), recorded in [ADR 0005](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/decisions/0005-general-device-controls.md). Pixoo already declares these capabilities in controller v1 through Pixoo #37: power maps to screen power (off pauses, on does not resume), brightness is 0 to 100, media selection uses up to 100 discovered playlist IDs and the actions pause, resume, stop, next, previous and clear.

Controls live in the existing component view under `apps/dashboard`, next to the delivered Monitor/Media mode and settings controls. Navigation is unchanged and no page issues commands to more than one device. Every action submits one guarded controller v1 command through the existing hub route with request identity, configuration revision and generation guards. The frontend creates no writer and no restoration state.

## Accepted rules

- Controls appear only when the Pixoo snapshot declares the capability and the credential has control scope. A disabled control names the missing capability or scope.
- Power and brightness are available in Monitor and Media.
- Playlist selection and playback actions are disabled while Pixoo is in Monitor, with the reason and a one-click explicit switch to Media using the existing mode control. No user action changes the mode as a side effect of another command.
- Nothing restores automatically. Returning to Monitor is the existing mode control.
- Playlists are listed by ID until the Pixoo naming extension is consumed; that extension is separate and non-blocking.
- Uncertain results stay locked and are never retried automatically. Transport success is not a physical result.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1.** Each control submits exactly one valid v1 command with the snapshot's request ID, revision and generation, and the receipt or typed failure is shown with pending, conflict and uncertain states.
- [x] **AC2.** Availability follows declared capability, control scope and mode per the rules above; every disabled control shows its reason; the Monitor gating switch is explicit.
- [x] **AC3.** The view is usable with no observed sessions and with a read-only credential, which sees disabled controls with explanations.
- [x] **AC4.** Reconnect, resync, concurrent edits and stale revisions preserve drafts and focus and replay no commands.
- [x] **AC5.** Keyboard access, contrast, reduced motion and narrow layouts pass the existing accessibility checks.
- [x] **AC6.** The exact issue-linked OpenSpec change records the `unified-dashboard` delta; browser fixtures with the fake Pixoo controller cover every rule; `npm run test:dashboard` and `npm run test:dashboard:browser` pass with the shared checks.
- [x] **AC7.** Explicit human approval of the actual UI candidate is recorded in the PR, renewed after changes, under the SDLC UI approval scope.

Physical acceptance on the display is the separate hardware issue created by #31's decomposition.

body:
## Outcome

Add Nanoleaf general controls to the existing Nanoleaf component view in BUNNY: power, brightness and saved-scene activation, usable without an active agent session.

## Scope and accepted definition

Implements the Nanoleaf slice of [#31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31), recorded in [ADR 0005](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/decisions/0005-general-device-controls.md). Nanoleaf's controller v1 currently declares only Work/Quiet/Free mode; the native capabilities come from [Nanoleaf #64](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/64), which is a required input. The Pixoo slice in #151 establishes the shared control components and does not wait for this issue.

Controls live in the existing component view under `apps/dashboard`, next to the delivered mode and settings controls. Every action submits one guarded controller v1 command through the existing hub route. The frontend creates no writer and no restoration state.

## Accepted rules

- Controls appear only when the Nanoleaf snapshot declares the capability and the credential has control scope. A disabled control names the missing capability or scope.
- Power and brightness are available in Work, Quiet and Free. The view shows the desired brightness as an override that persists until the next explicit mode command, matching the controller's policy from Nanoleaf #64.
- Scene activation is disabled while the wall is in Work or Quiet, with the reason and a one-click explicit switch to Free using the existing mode control. No user action changes the mode as a side effect of another command.
- The scene list comes from the controller snapshot only, never from browser or hub configuration. Scene names appear only when the integration extension supplies user-chosen names; IDs otherwise.
- Nothing restores automatically. Returning to Work or Quiet is the existing mode control. Uncertain results stay locked.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1.** Each control submits exactly one valid v1 command with the snapshot's request ID, revision and generation, and the receipt or typed failure is shown with pending, conflict and uncertain states.
- [x] **AC2.** Availability follows declared capability, control scope and mode per the rules above; every disabled control shows its reason; the Free gating switch is explicit.
- [x] **AC3.** The view is usable with no observed sessions and with a read-only credential.
- [x] **AC4.** Reconnect, resync, concurrent edits and stale revisions preserve drafts and focus and replay no commands. Nanoleaf's unknown observation stays unknown in the view.

Physical acceptance on the installed wall is the separate hardware issue created by #31's decomposition.

- [#31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31): general-control definition, accepted 2026-09-22.
