title: Install and verify Pixoo general controls on the physical display
body:
## Outcome

Make the delivered Pixoo general controls usable in the existing BUNNY installation, then verify them in one short, owner-observed session on the named Pixoo. Check installed versions first and update only what is needed through the existing supported installation procedure.

Owner-approved simplification, September 24, 2026: retain the functional checks and safe installation/restoration steps; replace separate evidence packages with one issue checklist. This is a scope revision, not an installation or acceptance result.

## Acceptance checklist

- [x] **Prepare and update.** Name the installation owner and exact target, including its explicitly authorized IP in private setup records. Obtain permission for the update, display-content replacement and test sequence. Record installed hub/dashboard and Pixoo versions with corresponding source revisions. Follow the Pixoo owner's supported update and rollback procedure only where an update is needed. Keep credentials and runtime data private.
- [x] **Choose the final state.** Note current mode, playlist, screen power and brightness where known, plus the intended final state. Mark unavailable starting values unknown instead of guessing.
- [x] **Check Monitor controls.** In Monitor, confirm playlist/playback controls are disabled with a reason. Try screen power and brightness and observe the display response.
- [x] **Check Media controls.** Explicitly switch to Media, select one existing playlist and try pause, resume, stop, next, previous and clear once each. Use suitable existing media and explicitly restart playback as needed between checks. During playback, confirm screen-off pauses and screen-on does not resume; explicit Resume remains necessary. Check the device's response as well as the command result.
- [x] **Return and finish.** Explicitly return to Monitor and observe agent-status presentation. Confirm there was no automatic return during the Media checks. Leave the display in the chosen final state and record it.
- [x] **Record acceptance.** Complete this checklist with owner-observed results and any failures or unverified steps. Close only after the required installation and functional checks pass. Missing permission, an unavailable target or an unverified behavior remains explicit.

## Evidence and limits

Use one issue update/checklist for installed versions, command results, visible behavior, failures and final state. Keep transport acceptance distinct from what the owner actually saw, without a separate report or screenshot for every successful click. Retain detailed logs only for failures or ambiguity; add troubleshooting notes only when the session reveals something useful.

This is a single-target functional check. No endurance run, repeated hardware matrix or new automated hardware-test framework is required. Existing installation and restoration rules still apply. This issue alone grants no permission to install software, start agent sessions or operate devices.

title: Qualify iPhone Apple Music now-playing sources through the apartment speakers
body:
## Current delivery direction (September 24, 2026)

The owner selected Linux/Docker-compatible music integration with Sony as the first source. [#175](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175) now delivers the shared playback and Sony modules together; [#228](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/228) was consolidated without claiming implementation, and [#36](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/36) is deferred Windows work. The Windows-first ordering and "second source" references below describe the completed September 23 planning baseline, not current prerequisites. This note changes no qualification result or completion evidence; installed adapter and Docker acceptance remain outstanding in their owning issues.

## Outcome

Decide how BUNNY sees, and where possible controls, Apple Music playing from the iPhone, and pick the source to build. The result feeds the hub playback service from [#36](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/36) as a second playback source. It does not change the Windows connector.

## What is already known (2026-09-22)

The phone plays Apple Music over AirPlay to apartment speakers. The user's preferred primary output is a Sony HT-A series soundbar (A3000, A5000, A7000 or A9; exact model to record), with Sonos as the fallback. The phone's own audio never passes through the PC, so a PC-hosted AirPlay or Bluetooth receiver is not in the audio path.

Sony's Audio Control API runs on the soundbar at `http://<ip>:10000/sony` as JSON-RPC over HTTP with WebSocket notifications. python-songpal (issues #96 and #107) and homebridge-sony-audio support the HT-A7000, HT-A5000 and HT-A9. Same-generation device descriptions in python-songpal expose `avContent.getPlayingContentInfo` (title, artist, albumName, durationMsec, positionMsec, applicationName, service, source, uri and a content thumbnailUrl), `notifyPlayingContentInfo` for push updates, and `pausePlayingContent`, `setPlayNextContent` and `setPlayPreviousContent`. None of those descriptions mention AirPlay, so whether an AirPlay stream fills the title and artist fields, and whether the transport methods reach the phone, is exactly what the spike must answer. Sony's manual and developer pages block automated fetches; the user has the manual.

Paths ruled out by the planning investigation: iCloud exposes no playback state. The Apple Music API only lists recently played items after a delay, has no now-playing or control endpoint, and needs the $99 a year Developer Program. Phone Link has no iPhone media support. Shortcuts has no song-change trigger. `MPNowPlayingInfoCenter` only publishes an app's own now-playing data. A custom app reading the system music player needs Xcode on a Mac.

## Spikes, in order

1. **Sony soundbar, Audio Control API.** Record the exact model and confirm network standby is on. With the phone streaming Apple Music to the soundbar, call `getPlayingContentInfo` and subscribe to `notifyPlayingContentInfo` (python-songpal is the quickest tool). Record which fields arrive for the AirPlay source (title, artist, album, thumbnail URL, position, duration), how fast a track change shows up, and whether pause, next and previous reach the phone. Note the network path: WSL sits behind NAT, so unicast HTTP to the soundbar IP works, but SSDP discovery and long-lived WebSocket notifications may need the Windows side or polling.
2. **Sonos local API.** Same check against a Sonos speaker with SoCo or equivalent, only if the Sony result is missing fields or control. Sonos discovery and event callbacks have the same NAT caveat.
3. **Fallbacks, only if 1 and 2 fail.** A Linux-hosted shairport-sync added as an extra AirPlay 2 output receives metadata and artwork without moving the sound; remote control of AirPlay 2 senders is still experimental there, it is Linux only, and mDNS does not cross WSL's NAT. The Last.fm relay (free scrobbler app plus the Last.fm "now playing" flag) is read-only and only near-live while the scrobbler stays active.

[#11](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/11) evaluates Home Assistant, which has songpal (Sony) and Sonos integrations. Record whether it would be cheaper than a direct integration, without making it a prerequisite.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1.** One recorded check per spike actually run: fields received, artwork, measured delay between a track change on the phone and the observed change, and whether pause and next reach the phone. Read-only against the speakers; no install on the phone or PC without the user's ok. Keep speaker IPs and any API keys out of Git.
- [x] **AC2.** A recommendation: which source becomes the second playback source, or none, and what the #36 snapshot contract needs for it (at least a source id and per-source availability, plus a source-selection rule when the phone and the Windows app play at once).
- [x] **AC3.** If a source is chosen, its implementation issue is filed with the same fake-source test shape as #36.

## Dependencies

The spikes are independent. Integration needs the #36 playback contract. #37 and #38 consume a second source if one is adopted.

## Assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-22, against hub `main` f11334d.

- **Complexity: low.** Read-only checks against speakers on the LAN.
- **Uncertainty: high by design.** The spikes resolve it. Unknowns: whether AirPlay content fills the Sony playing-content fields, transport control forwarding to the phone, the exact soundbar model.
- **Impact: low.** Reversible. Personal accounts and speaker addresses only.

**Readiness:** ready. Speaker types and spike order were settled with the user on 2026-09-22. **Review:** none beyond the coordinator's readback for the record; source reviews apply to the follow-up implementation issue.

Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. This planning record authorizes no installation, personal settings change or device operation beyond the read-only speaker checks named above.

Part of the [future-work guide](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/35); follows [ADR 0004](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/decisions/0004-local-first-personal-assistant.md).



## Delivery evidence (2026-09-23)

[PR #176](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/176) merged as `5db67a0944f017d655331ab410c639570c876108`; all six applicable Depot jobs passed on that main revision. The [qualification record](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/5db67a0944f017d655331ab410c639570c876108/docs/iphone-apple-music-qualification.md) covers the Sony HT-A9 and conditional Sonos Move checks, the Sony recommendation, the #36 contract needs, and the Home Assistant comparison. The owner separately authorized pause/next/previous calls to each receiver during this delivery and confirmed their effects on the iPhone. [Implementation #175](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175) is filed and blocked by #36. No adapter was installed, and no receiver address or track metadata was committed.

title: Make the BUNNY atlas start with a system map and agent walkthrough
body:
## Outcome

Make the BUNNY atlas useful on arrival: a system map and one short agent-to-device walkthrough, with details available when selected. Keep this proportional to a personal project by using the existing HTML generators and Archify.

The September 23 audit found that the overview leads with prose and a 26-document catalog, while its diagrams are elsewhere. Main at planning is `a76b22db3497bcc1c92f6445add1356f8eb1820e`. The September 19 atlas remains useful as a clearly dated reference.

## Scope and acceptance

- [ ] **Start with the map.** At 1440×1000, the first screen contains the system map. A reader can identify the applications, embedded libraries, private stores and device owners without opening the complete reference. Keep explanatory prose brief and move detail behind selection or expansion. Evidence: before/after desktop capture and a short reading walkthrough.
- [ ] **Represent the actual boundaries.** Show where the hub, shared state core, MCP module and controller writers run. Distinguish lifecycle observations from deliberate UI/MCP commands. Label future music/automation behavior separately. Record source revisions and distinguish source implementation from installed or physical acceptance. Evidence: trace the displayed facts to owning code, contracts and application guides.
- [ ] **Follow one complete scenario.** Explain agent observation → committed shared state → consumer/controller projection → designated device writer. Keep the shared core's state publication distinct from device command execution. Show one concise interruption/reconnect alternative and link its existing behavior/runbook. Evidence: source-backed sequence and browser walkthrough; no live device experiment.
- [ ] **Reveal useful details.** Mouse and keyboard selection expose a brief responsibility description and links to the owning code, API/contract or storage documentation. Current hub routes and storage ownership must be discoverable. Keep existing source-pinned API/schema references visibly dated; do not infer current schemas from the older atlas. Evidence: navigation and keyboard checks plus source/link inspection.
- [ ] **Reuse the diagrams.** The atlas and work guide consume the same editable definitions for the system map and lifecycle walkthrough, rather than maintaining competing models. Preserve the historical component documents, combined reading view and existing deep links with clear dates. Evidence: generator/input inspection and reproducible output checks.
- [ ] **Qualify the candidate.** Labels and controls are readable at desktop and narrow widths; mobile does not simply shrink the whole map into unreadable text. Offline browsing, search, themes and print remain usable. Obtain approval of the current atlas UI candidate under the repository UI rule. title: Deliver shared Linux playback with a separate Sony HT-A9 source
body:
## Outcome

Deliver the Linux-native shared playback module and the first Sony HT-A9 source module together, in one issue and PR. The iPhone continues playing Apple Music to the HT-A9 over AirPlay; BUNNY reads metadata and sends qualified controls. No Windows helper or audio routing through the hub is needed.

Owner decision, September 24, 2026: consolidate [#228](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/228) here while preserving separate modules and an architecture that supports future music sources. This combines delivery, not the two responsibilities. [#36](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/36) remains deferred Windows integration.

## Architecture to preserve

- **Shared playback module:** owns the normalized snapshot, observation freshness, authenticated snapshot/command routes and command results. It accepts source observations and delegates commands through a small typed interface. It must not import Sony protocol code or interpret Sony response fields.
- **Sony source module:** owns the configured receiver endpoint, polling, Sony field normalization and supported command calls. Endpoint details and raw Sony responses stay inside this module. The hub composes and stops both modules.
- **Future sources:** retain stable neutral source ids, source-scoped observations, optional metadata and declared controls. Bind commands to the requested source id; consumers must not depend on Sony fields or receiver URLs. The design must show how another adapter can keep its own snapshot/freshness and how one explicit selection controls presentation and routing. When multiple sources arrive, a newer observation or unavailable selected source must never silently select another source. Adding an adapter must not require rewriting the shared service or consumer contract.
- **First implementation:** one configured Sony source, selected explicitly by configuration. Keep the interface small and the snapshot in memory. No plugin discovery, generic source manager, dynamic switching UI, separate daemon or playback database. A second real adapter and multi-source runtime/selection behavior are deferred; the architecture must leave room for them.

## Initial behavior

- Poll `getPlayingContentInfo` around every two seconds, with a documented timeout and no overlapping reads. Normalize title, artist, optional album, playback status and supported controls. A successful unchanged read refreshes observation time; failures do not. Use documented available/stale/unavailable rules and start unavailable until the first successful observation.
- Expose authenticated `GET /api/playback/v1/snapshot` and `POST /api/playback/v1/commands` through existing hub read/control and request-validation boundaries. The snapshot includes its source id and observation time/age. Preserve current controller-registration restrictions; the privately configured Sony endpoint is not a client-supplied URL proxy. Playback remains separate from agent lifecycle/state exports.
- Implement qualified pause, next and previous. Play/resume stays unsupported until separately qualified. Preserve sent/failed/uncertain outcomes, unsupported/unavailable failures, request correlation, small bounded duplicate suppression and one command at a time. No automatic write retries or pending-command replay after restart.
- Start with text metadata and snapshot polling. [#39](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/39) owns song-transition detection, track comparison/identity and lighting effects. [playback artwork story](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/229) owns artwork acquisition. Neither feature blocks this delivery. Subscriptions, SSE, precise progress and repeat detection are outside this first version.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **AC1.** Source and the issue-linked design preserve the module boundary above. Document a concrete future two-source flow: independent freshness, explicit selection, source-bound commands and no silent fallback. A simple non-Sony fake can use the same interface without changing the shared module; no second production integration is required.
- [x] **AC2.** One focused suite using a fake Sony endpoint covers metadata/status, missing fields, unchanged observations, unavailable/non-AirPlay input, timeout and reconnect. Use controlled-clock checks for freshness; avoid duplicating the same scenarios in separate service and adapter suites.
- [x] **AC3.** Verify authentication, the configured source target, unsupported controls, duplicate next, concurrent commands and uncertain outcomes. No command is redirected or automatically resent.
- [x] **AC4.** Add proportionate playback validation to docs/development.md and CI and pass the required hub/shared checks. Document configuration, the API and module extension points; correct Windows-first architecture wording, including ADR 0004. Preserve historical qualification facts. Atlas regeneration and work-guide publication are not completion gates for this feature.
- [x] **AC5.** After separate installation/control authorization, verify a real iPhone AirPlay track change reaches the hub within a few seconds and pause reaches the phone. Record actual effects and timing separately from fake/HTTP evidence.

## Evidence, dependencies and follow-ups

Completed input: [#158](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/158) and the [HT-A9 qualification record](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/5db67a0944f017d655331ab410c639570c876108/docs/iphone-apple-music-qualification.md). It established WSL HTTP/WebSocket access, metadata, optional artwork and phone-confirmed pause/next/previous. Previous restarted the current song; selecting the preceding song, play/resume and Docker behavior were not established. Position/duration were absent. This covers the tested AirPlay path, not other receiver inputs or arbitrary Windows playback.

No open source prerequisite; [#228](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/228) is consolidated here, not a separate dependency. [#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/37) owns UI/MCP, [#38](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/38) display cards, [#39](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/39) transitions/lighting and [playback artwork story](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/229) shared artwork. [#42](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/42) retains Docker packaging and actual container-to-receiver/client verification; Linux source or installed-WSL checks do not establish container acceptance. [#178](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/178) owns catalog/chosen-item research. No Windows, Sonos, Music Assistant, account setup, audio capture or new physical-device writer is included.

## Assessment and delivery

Complexity low-to-medium: two small modules delivered together. Uncertainty low-to-medium: the receiver protocol was qualified; implementation and installed behavior remain to verify. Impact low for source work; real transport controls can interrupt music. Ready for specification/implementation when selected. Docker deployment and UI approval remain with their owning work.

Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md), the owning hub/development guides and the issue-linked OpenSpec change. Retain independent Standards/Specification review and applicable local, PR and merged-revision CI. Tracker changes do not authorize implementation or installation. Live checks require a named owner, explicit private target and sequence authorization; keep credentials, receiver addresses and private listening data out of Git.

title: Qualify Apple Music catalog search and chosen-item playback requests
body:
## Outcome

Decide how BUNNY can find Apple Music content and request a specific song, album or playlist for playback through an agent tool or authenticated API. Qualify the actual player and output path before promising "play this" on the owner's iPhone or Windows PC. Return a recommended capability boundary and implementation issues; this investigation does not build or install a music connector.

## Delivery preference (September 24, 2026)

Prefer Linux/Docker-compatible paths and preserve the existing iPhone-to-HT-A9 output where possible. Basic now-playing and transport will come from the separate shared playback and Sony modules in [#175](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175); those APIs do not select a catalog item. Windows-specific delivery [#36](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/36) is deferred. Music Assistant and MusicKit/browser alternatives remain research candidates, not adopted players or new prerequisites. Distinguish a server-owned queue/output from controlling the existing iPhone session.

## Questions to resolve

1. **Find music.** Compare Apple Music catalog search, charts and related content with personal-library search and recommendations. Record result IDs, storefront and availability, pagination, developer-token requirements, user authorization, subscription requirements where applicable, and any account or program cost. Separate public catalog results from personal data. Use Apple's current documentation and a bounded real query only when authorized credentials are available.
2. **Request a chosen item.** Compare (a) opening an Apple Music result for a user tap, (b) a Windows playback path, (c) MusicKit on the Web, and (d) an iPhone MusicKit companion using `SystemMusicPlayer`. For each, determine whether a selected catalog item can be queued and started, where audio originates, whether the owner's preferred iPhone-to-HT-A9 AirPlay route survives, and what happens when the app is backgrounded or absent. Check whether a request can reach the iPhone reliably; continuing audio after backgrounding alone does not prove remote command delivery. Record documented, live-tested, unsupported and unknown separately.
3. **Choose the command boundary.** Compare MCP tools, a scoped authenticated HTTP API, and provider hooks as entry points. In the accepted hub architecture, hooks are bounded observational emitters; deliberate music requests belong to an owning service reached through MCP or API. Define candidate `search_music`, `recommend_music` and `request_playback` inputs/outputs, read versus control scope, explicit target/source selection, request identity and sent/failed/uncertain outcomes. A dispatched request is not proof that the selected track played. Do not silently switch from the chosen output or retry an ambiguous play request.
4. **Recommend delivery.** Select the smallest supported search/discovery and playback-request paths, or recommend a link-and-tap handoff if direct playback is not qualified. State the needed implementation issues, fake-service tests, account setup and installed/physical acceptance gates.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** A source-backed capability matrix distinguishes catalog search, personal-library search, recommendations, result links, queue/start, transport controls and now-playing observation. It records exact authentication and cost prerequisites, output target and confidence level for each candidate.
- [ ] **AC2.** A concrete "find this album and play it on my iPhone through the HT-A9" trace identifies the catalog item, chosen player, authorization, request delivery, playback receipt and observation that would confirm the intended item and output. A Windows-target trace is optional while Windows integration is deferred; the chosen Linux-compatible approach must state where audio originates and how it reaches the selected output.
- [ ] **AC3.** MCP, authenticated HTTP and hooks are compared against the hub's current ownership and permission rules. The proposed tool/API contract distinguishes read from control, bounds result data, uses an explicit target and request ID, and reports unsupported/unavailable/uncertain without claiming playback success.
- [ ] **AC4.** Perform a bounded real catalog search and chosen-item playback trial on the intended target if the required developer account, credentials, build/install path and separate device authorization are available. Record the tested app, output, account conditions and observed result without committing tokens, addresses or listening history. If a gate is unavailable, name it and leave that behavior unqualified; documentation or a fake does not establish a live playback result.
- [ ] **AC5.** Record a recommendation and file only the implementation issues justified by the result, with dependencies and fake-source tests. If direct selected-item playback remains unqualified, specify the manual handoff and the next live trial needed before implementation.

## Relationship to existing work

- [#158](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/158) qualified now-playing and basic transport through the HT-A9 and Sonos Move; it did not select a catalog item.
- [#175](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175) delivers separate shared observation/transport and Sony source modules together. [#36](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/36) is deferred optional Windows integration. None is a prerequisite for this investigation; a later integrated command path should reuse the shared service. These basic transport adapters do not supply search, library or queue selection.
- [#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/37) plans now-playing and basic UI/Codex controls. [#152](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/152) forwards saved device-playlist controls. This issue does not expand either into Apple Music catalog access.
- Part of the future music work in [#35](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/35). Source delivery, Apple account connection, companion installation, real-client qualification and speaker acceptance remain separate.

## Assessment and authority

**Complexity: medium.** Several distinct catalog and playback paths must be compared. **Uncertainty: high.** Apple documents catalog access and MusicKit playback, but remote request delivery to the owner's iPhone and preservation of its AirPlay output need a real trial. **Impact: low for document-only work; medium for an authorized playback trial.** The trial could replace the current queue or change the audible song. **Readiness:** documentation and interface investigation can start now. Live API and device checks are conditional on named credentials, installation authority and an explicit target/sequence; do not infer those permissions from this issue.

Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. This issue authorizes investigation and qualification planning, not account setup, installing an app, changing personal settings or sending music commands. Keep credentials, device addresses, private track data and listening history out of Git.

body:
## Outcome

Define one reusable B.U.N.N.Y. UI foundation and a skin template for applications, the work guide, and the system-design atlas. Keep shared interaction patterns and state meanings consistent while skins can change colors, typography, surfaces, artwork, and decorative effects. Preserve Neon Geometry Wars (the existing Neon HUD/Prism direction) as the initial/default skin. This issue delivers the design and adoption plan; implementation follows in the owning issues.

## Scope and design input

- Own the canonical shared application guide in this repository, for example `docs/application-ui-style-guide.md`, and link it from the B.U.N.N.Y. dashboard README. The existing Nanoleaf wall-map ADR remains authoritative for its own UI. Recheck current source revisions before finalizing the guide.
- Use the owner-selected Nanoleaf Neon HUD wall map as the reference for the Neon Geometry Wars skin. Its quieter dashboard variant remains deliberate. Cyan selection, magenta pending, 2 px corners, grids, glow and faceted materials are skin choices, not universal values required of every future skin. Preserve current approved screens until their owning UI candidates are reviewed.
- Resolve the recommendations in the complete user-provided draft below: semantic color roles and variants, type, shape, spacing, components, state cues, accessibility, motion, responsive layout, brand, and future-page handoff. Mark observed source facts, approved shared rules, and device-specific exceptions separately.
- Define shared semantic roles and the reusable skin template here. [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85) defines the guide/atlas tokens on its own schedule; align role names with it rather than blocking it. Nanoleaf retains wall geometry, truthful device/task rendering and physical effects; Pixoo retains media, player and display rendering. Do not turn crystal tubes, connectors, wall animation or the `◈` glyph into mandatory generic components. Source migration remains separate.
- Record the owner-selected name **B.U.N.N.Y.** in `docs/decisions/0004-local-first-personal-assistant.md`. Replace its stale undecided/future-naming statements while preserving the broader accepted direction. The draft below predates this naming decision, so its `BUNNY` spelling is historical input. Do not invent an expansion of the initials or a new logo. Keep package names, paths and machine identifiers stable.

## Acceptance criteria and planned evidence

- [ ] **AC1 — Source and precedence.** Compare the draft against current Hub `apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx`, `style.css`, README and architecture, plus Nanoleaf `bridge/wall.html` and accepted ADR 0004. Record verified source revisions and correct any stale claims. Evidence: source citations or revision links for observed values; a clear precedence rule for future agents. The draft's Hub `a76b22d` and Nanoleaf `2558df5` snapshots are inputs, not a claim of current source.
- [ ] **AC2 — Approved visual rules.** Present a concrete candidate covering color roles, dense-page variants, typography, grid strength, skin-specific shape language, navigation, buttons, forms, panels, status, pending and empty states. Record the owner's decision on the current candidate and its revision. Evidence: the reviewed guide plus representative wide and narrow examples, including focus, selected, pending, unavailable, stale and error states. The draft's recommendations become binding only when approved.
- [ ] **AC3 — Accessibility and meaning.** Specify text or another non-color cue for status, visible keyboard focus, readable contrast on rendered/translucent surfaces, reduced-motion behavior, and responsive checks. Keep device/task status, selection and pending intent distinct in every skin; cyan selection and magenta pending remain the Neon mapping. Evidence: checked color calculations where applicable, rendered examples and an inspection checklist; do not present opaque-pair calculations as proof for every state.
- [ ] **AC4 — Ownership and reuse.** Name the Hub token layer as the future shared application seam while keeping wall-rendering and device-specific tokens in the Nanoleaf domain. Document which dashboard shell and component patterns new pages reuse, the dense-page variant rule, and when a new design decision is required. Preserve capability/permission gating and the distinction between inspection, pending commands and observed physical results. Evidence: a usable new-page checklist and source-linked examples. Use B.U.N.N.Y. as the shared application display name.
- [ ] **AC5 — Naming decision.** ADR 0004 records B.U.N.N.Y. as the selected AI assistant name and no longer calls naming undecided or future work. The style guide uses that spelling for the shared application and explains the older draft spelling. Evidence: owner decision in this planning request, ADR diff and guide review. This decides user-facing spelling only; no acronym expansion, new logo, path rename or machine-identifier change is approved.
- [ ] **AC6 — Durable delivery.** Commit the guide and its owning links through the repository SDLC, with independent Standards and Specification reviews, applicable CI and merged-main readback. Treat this as design/documentation with no product behavior delta; record that disposition rather than inventing an OpenSpec product capability. The PR must identify any visual examples that count as UI changes and record any required current-candidate approval under `docs/sdlc.md`.

## Dependencies and assessment

No unfinished source prerequisite. [Nanoleaf ADR 0004](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/docs/decisions/0004-wall-map-visual-direction.md), [Nanoleaf #23](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/23), and [Hub #6](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/6) are accepted source inputs, not new blockers. The guide/atlas in [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85) does not depend on this issue. [#182](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/182) requires this accepted foundation. [#87](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/87) retains publication ownership.

Planning assessment, 2026-09-23; Hub remote `main` `5db67a0944f017d655331ab410c639570c876108`, Nanoleaf remote `main` `cbb948516eb161d551d817c7ee2870b2b74dc9cb`; session reasoning setting: unknown.

- Complexity: **medium-to-high** — one foundation must cover applications, generated documentation and domain-specific views while keeping adoption bounded.
- Uncertainty: **medium** — the draft is source-backed, while the shared recommendations and examples still need owner approval.
- Impact: **medium** — an incorrect guide could steer several future UI changes, but the document is reversible.
- Readiness: **ready for design/documentation work**. The visual reference and source owners are known; selecting the final shared rules is this issue's outcome. Reassess if source, ADR, UI policy or intended scope changes.

## Authority and exclusions

This issue defines future documentation and design work, including the ADR 0004 naming update. Current authorization updates the UI tracker plan only. It does not approve the recommendations, implement tokens, restyle either UI, publish a public site, migrate source, install services or operate devices. Future application UI changes need approval of their own current candidate.

## Skin template — planning extension, 2026-09-23 (trimmed)

V1 ships Neon Geometry Wars only. The alternate skin, a skin picker with saved preference, and Nanoleaf/Pixoo adoption are deferred to a later issue once the alternate's look is chosen.

- [ ] **AC7 — Extensible single-skin template.** Define three layers: shared component/interaction rules; named semantic roles; and skin values/assets/decorative effects. Supply Neon Geometry Wars as the only skin, plus short instructions for adding a skin as new values without copying screens or forking logic. Skins cannot change capability gating, state definitions, task/project identity or physical-device colors. Reuse [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85)'s guide/atlas token names where the meaning is the same.

<details>
<summary>Complete source-backed draft supplied by the owner on 2026-09-23</summary>

# Agent Device Hub UI style guide

**Status:** Source-backed draft for design approval  
**Prepared:** 2026-09-23  
**Scope:** The BUNNY application dashboard in `agent-device-hub` and the Nanoleaf wall-map UI currently in `codex-nanoleaf`. This guide is for application screens and their reusable UI. The work guide and system-design documentation have separate presentation and are outside this guide.  
**Source snapshots:** Hub `a76b22db3497bcc1c92f6445add1356f8eb1820e`; Nanoleaf `2558df5a2fc543247b0c75898ef0260ba3ea264b`.

**User-selected visual reference:** The Nanoleaf wall map. New shared application pages should take their visual foundation from it. The Hub dashboard remains the existing shared shell and an example of how that foundation is adapted to dense information and forms.

This document records the current visual language, then makes explicit recommendations for keeping new pages consistent. A value marked **current** comes from source. A rule marked **recommended** is a proposed shared convention and needs design approval before it becomes binding. Repository instructions, accepted ADRs, and current UI approvals take precedence if the implementation context changes.

## 1. Visual direction

**Current:** The accepted Nanoleaf wall-map direction is a compact Neon HUD: near-black surfaces, a faint cyan grid, cyan selection, magenta pending changes, system fonts, narrow borders, mostly square corners, and restrained glow. The Hub dashboard explicitly carries this language into its central BUNNY interface. The Hub uses a quieter version of the grid and less decorative motion so data and controls stay readable.

**Recommended shared rule:** Use the Nanoleaf wall map as the visual anchor. A screen should read as a calm control surface first. Use the grid as texture, cyan to show an available primary action or current selection, and magenta to show a pending edit or attention that needs resolution. Reserve vivid physical-light colors for actual device or task status. Do not use a glow on every card, button, or heading.

The Nanoleaf crystal tubes, hexagonal connectors, two-second status flow, and opening assembly belong to the wall visualization. They are **not** generic dashboard components.

## 2. Sources of truth and precedence

| Concern | Current source | Rule for an implementation agent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shared application shell and component pages | `agent-device-hub/apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx`, `style.css`, and `README.md` | Extend the existing dashboard navigation and component views. Keep the BUNNY shell consistent across pages. |
| Nanoleaf-specific wall map | `codex-nanoleaf/bridge/wall.html` and `docs/decisions/0004-wall-map-visual-direction.md` | Preserve the wall-map material, status meaning, and interaction distinctions. |
| Cross-project UI ownership | `agent-device-hub/docs/architecture.md` | The shared frontend uses Nanoleaf's approved visual language; a device's capability and permission determine available controls. |
| Behavior and validation | Each repository's `AGENTS.md`, app README, and development guide | Follow the current repository rules and tests for the page being changed. This guide grants no migration or device-operation authority. |

**Recommended:** Keep the common foundation in one named token layer when the applications can share it. Device-specific colors and wall-rendering tokens stay in the Nanoleaf domain. Until source migration is delivered, the Nanoleaf repository remains the wall-map source of truth; do not treat this guide as a source-migration instruction.

## 3. Color

Use role names in new code. The hex values below are the current CSS values; a shared-token refactor is a separate implementation decision.

| Role | Current value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page background | `#05070d` | Main canvas and the darkest surface in both apps. |
| Solid panel | `#080c16` | Sidebar, opaque cards, menus, and the wall-map panel fallback. |
| Primary text | `#d7e3ff` | Body text and major headings. |
| Cyan accent | `#22d3ee` | Primary action, selected item, active mark, and key readout. |
| Dark text on cyan | `#04121a` on the wall map; `#101724` on dashboard primary buttons | Use only when cyan fills the control. |
| Pending / emphasis | `#e879f9` | Pending wall edits, pending control cues, and restrained emphasis. Do not imply a successful physical result. |
| White focus | `#ffffff` | Visible keyboard focus on both current UIs. |
| Muted text, wall map | `#7f93bd` | Secondary wall-map labels. |
| Muted text, dashboard | `#a6b4ca` | Secondary dashboard text. |
| Dashboard border | `#34415a` | Quiet panel dividers and card edges. |
| Wall-map border | `rgba(34, 211, 238, .2)` | Cyan-tinted divisions and surfaces. |
| Dashboard input surface | `#0d1420` | Form controls. |

**Current:** The dashboard and wall map use different muted-text and border values. **Recommended:** For a new page, start with the Nanoleaf muted-text and cyan-tinted edge tokens. The dashboard's lighter muted text and quieter slate borders are established variants for dense information and forms. If a new Hub page uses those variants, apply them consistently and document why. Do not silently replace values across an already approved screen.

**Recommended semantic token starter:** These names are proposed for new shared code; the values come from the Nanoleaf source. Keep the dense-information variants explicit instead of scattering raw colors through new pages.

```css
:root {
  --ui-bg: #05070d;
  --ui-panel: #080c16;
  --ui-panel-translucent: rgba(8, 12, 22, .82);
  --ui-text: #d7e3ff;
  --ui-muted: #7f93bd;
  --ui-edge: rgba(34, 211, 238, .2);
  --ui-edge-strong: rgba(34, 211, 238, .5);
  --ui-accent: #22d3ee;
  --ui-accent-ink: #04121a;
  --ui-pending: #e879f9;
  --ui-focus: #ffffff;
  --ui-radius: 2px;
  --ui-grid-size: 32px;
  --ui-font: Bahnschrift, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif;
  --ui-font-mono: "Cascadia Mono", Consolas, ui-monospace, monospace;
  --ui-muted-dense: #a6b4ca;
  --ui-edge-dense: #34415a;
}
```

**Current background texture:** Both use a 32 px cyan grid. The dashboard uses `rgba(34,211,238,.025)` lines in its main region; the wall map uses `rgba(34,211,238,.055)` lines, plus a light vignette and scanline treatment on its canvas. **Recommended:** Keep dashboard texture at or below its current strength; reserve the fuller treatment for the wall canvas.

### Status colors

**Current Nanoleaf wall and task palette:** working `#00ff00`, question `#ffff00`, blocked `#ff0000`, unread `#193cff`. The UI lifts these to legible chip colors: working `#2bff63`, question `#ffe600`, blocked `#ff4a4a`, unread `#5b9bff`.

**Recommended:** Treat these as semantic device/task statuses, not general decoration. Include a text label or other non-color cue. Do not reuse green to mean that a command reached the physical lights unless that result has actually been observed. Keep pending magenta distinct from task status and from selection cyan.

### Contrast check on current opaque pairs

Calculated from the source hex values: primary text on page background `15.65:1`; wall muted text on page background `6.53:1`; dashboard muted text on page background `9.59:1`; cyan on page background `11.14:1`; wall dark text on cyan `10.50:1`. These calculations do **not** validate every translucent panel, hover state, image overlay, or user-selected project color. Check those in the rendered page. For ordinary text, the WCAG 2.2 AA minimum is [4.5:1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html); for large text it is 3:1.

## 4. Typography and visual hierarchy

| Role | Current treatment |
| --- | --- |
| Body and headings | `Bahnschrift, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif` in both apps. |
| Technical labels and readouts | `"Cascadia Mono", Consolas, ui-monospace, monospace` on the wall map; Cascadia Mono/Consolas for dashboard eyebrow, topbar, and navigation labels. |
| Wall-map body | `14px / 1.45`; compact controls and details. |
| Wall-map labels | `10.5px`, uppercase, `0.14em` letter spacing; wall-map brand uses `0.18em`. |
| Dashboard page heading | `clamp(2rem, 3.8vw, 3.2rem)`, weight `550`, line-height `1.12`, letter spacing `-.045em`. |
| Dashboard section heading | `1.7rem`, letter spacing `-.025em`; compact card headings are `1rem`. |
| Dashboard paragraphs | Line-height `1.6`. |

**Recommended hierarchy for new dashboard pages:** one clear page title and a short explanation; section headings for groups; compact card headings; then subdued labels and metadata. Use the mono face for short system labels, device IDs, timestamps, and numbers. Keep prose in the UI face. Do not set long paragraphs in uppercase or mono.

**Current font constraint:** The Nanoleaf wall-map content security policy prevents remote and data-URI fonts. Use the listed local fallbacks there. The Hub already uses the same system family, so a remote font is unnecessary for visual consistency.

## 5. Shape, space, and composition

- **Current shape:** Buttons, fields, cards, and badges use a `2px` radius. Most surfaces are flat, separated by a one-pixel border. The wall map uses translucent cards and cyan corner brackets for selected cards.
- **Current dashboard shell:** `232px` sidebar with a bounded main column (`max-width: 1500px`), 42 px desktop main padding, 24 px session-card padding, and 20 px session spacing. At 900 px the sidebar narrows to 180 px; at 680 px navigation becomes a top row and dense forms become one column.
- **Current wall map:** On wide screens, a 264 px projects rail, flexible canvas, and 320 px inspector. Below about 1050 px, the inspector moves below the canvas. At 680 px, the three regions stack. The wall-map card uses 14 px padding and 12 px gap.
- **Recommended composition:** Keep a stable page shell, consistent left alignment, clear groups, and room around the main content. Use the dashboard's quieter spacing for forms and data; retain the map's denser composition where the live wall needs the screen area. Do not force one page's column widths onto the other.

## 6. Component rules

| Component | Current pattern | Recommended reuse rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary button | Cyan fill, dark text, 2 px radius in the dashboard; the wall map's main Assign action has the same role. | One clear primary action per local decision group. Give it a text label that names the action. |
| Secondary button | Dark or transparent surface, pale text, border. | Use for inspection, cancellation, alternate actions, and low-priority controls. |
| Selected navigation or item | Cyan line/border and a distinct filled background. | Mark the current location with `aria-current` where applicable. Selection must remain visible without animation. |
| Pending action | Magenta cue with explicit text. The wall map uses a dashed pending outline; the dashboard uses status text and a magenta pending cue. | State what is pending. Do not use the same cue for success, failure, or keyboard focus. |
| Card or panel | Dark surface, thin border, compact heading, supporting text. | Place related facts and controls together. Use glow only when it communicates an active selection. |
| Form field | Dark input, pale text, visible label and white focus outline. | Keep labels visible, show the current or unknown value honestly, and preserve draft/selection on refresh. |
| Badge or status | Text plus small colored cue. | Use status text, not color alone. Distinguish attention, stale observation, and pending commands. |
| Empty or unavailable state | Written explanation; dashboard empty state uses dashed border. | Explain what is absent or why a control is unavailable. Do not imply a device or integration is broken from missing data alone. |

**Current Hub behavior:** A control may be unavailable because of capability, scope, mode, stale evidence, or another owner. The UI explains why. A submitted control keeps or restores focus, uncertain actions remain locked until explicit reload, and reads do not issue device commands. Preserve these behaviors when restyling. The wall map likewise keeps selection, Work/Quiet/Free meaning, and pending edits distinct.

## 7. Motion and responsiveness

**Current shared behavior:** Both UIs respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. The dashboard removes animations and transitions under that preference. The wall map keeps static visual distinctions between Work, Quiet, and Free when motion stops.

**Current Nanoleaf-specific motion:** The wall renderer uses a two-second indicative status flow in Work, steadier and dimmer rendering in Quiet, and a desaturated dim view in Free. Its opening assembly is decorative and separate from actual device effects. It is not an exact preview of physical controller frames.

**Recommended:** Use small, short transitions only where they clarify state. Keep the dashboard still by default. Never make color or motion the only way to learn a state. Check the page at wide desktop, intermediate widths near its layout changes, and narrow mobile; test keyboard order and visible focus at each.

## 8. Brand and imagery

**Current:** The Hub shell uses a text `BUNNY` wordmark with a `◈` glyph and a `LOCAL INTEGRATION` sublabel. The Nanoleaf page uses `Codex × Nanoleaf` plus `Wall map` in text. The wall visualization and its local Prism SVG assets are the distinctive Nanoleaf imagery. No shared finished logo asset is established by these sources.

**Recommended:** Keep `BUNNY` in the shared Hub shell and identify Nanoleaf within its component view or advanced editor. Preserve the current Nanoleaf wall-map title while it remains in its own application. A future logo or migration-specific brand treatment needs an explicit design decision; do not invent one by copying the `◈` glyph into every device screen.

## 9. Agent implementation handoff

Use this guide with a specific UI task. The implementation agent should:

1. Read the current `AGENTS.md`, relevant app README, and source files listed in section 2. Confirm their revisions and identify any newer UI decision or human approval.
2. Use the Nanoleaf wall map as the visual reference. Keep **current** source facts distinct from **recommended** shared conventions. A proposed departure from the selected direction needs a new design decision.
3. Inventory the page's colors, type, spacing, and components. Map repeated raw values to semantic names without changing domain status meaning. Keep Nanoleaf wall-rendering tokens local.
4. Implement the page in its owning application. Extend the Hub's component navigation and existing control patterns; do not migrate the Nanoleaf source or alter controller behavior as part of a styling task.
5. Compare wide and narrow screenshots with the selected reference. Inspect normal, hover, focus, selected, pending, disabled, stale, error, and empty states. Include long labels and small screens.
6. Run the owning repository's UI checks. For Hub dashboard changes, use its dashboard and browser checks; for Nanoleaf wall-map changes, use its Python and browser checks. Record which checks ran and whether any visual or physical acceptance remains outstanding.
7. Obtain the current candidate's required human UI approval under the repository rules before merging UI changes. A prior approval of another page or revision does not cover a changed candidate.

### Acceptance checklist for each new or restyled page

- [ ] Uses the correct shell and local identity; no invented shared logo.
- [ ] Uses the role colors, font stacks, and 2 px shape language consistently.
- [ ] Has a clear title, section hierarchy, readable body text, and visible field labels.
- [ ] Looks coherent at desktop, intermediate, and mobile widths without clipped controls or horizontal overflow.
- [ ] Shows keyboard focus and distinguishes selected, pending, unavailable, stale, and error states in text as well as color.
- [ ] Supports reduced motion while preserving the meaning of modes and statuses.
- [ ] Keeps inspection separate from commands and preserves existing device/control semantics.
- [ ] Includes a current-candidate screenshot or browser evidence and the required human UI approval before merge.

## 10. Future change triggers

- The Nanoleaf values are the default for new pages. The dashboard's muted text and slate borders remain its documented dense-information variant. Restyling the existing dashboard to align them exactly requires a reviewed UI candidate.
- Treat the current `BUNNY` text and `◈` glyph as the interim Hub mark. A dedicated shared logo, if desired, needs a separate asset and design decision.
- If the Nanoleaf source moves into the Hub, review the resulting page in its new shell. The migration does not by itself approve changes to the wall visualization or its status meaning.

</details>

title: Apply the Neon skin foundation and B.U.N.N.Y. display name to the dashboard
body:
## Outcome

Implement the approved B.U.N.N.Y. UI foundation in the existing dashboard. Deliver reusable shell/component patterns and Neon Geometry Wars as the only skin, structured so a later skin is a new set of token values, with visual, accessibility and behavior evidence.

## Required input

**Blocked by [Hub #181](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/181).** Its owner-approved guide revision must settle the single-skin template, semantic roles, dense-information variants, component/state rules and source precedence before this UI candidate adopts them. Recheck the accepted revision and current dashboard source at delivery; an open planning issue is not an approved design input.

## Scope

- Work in `apps/dashboard` and its owning README/tests. Add an application-local semantic token layer and one Neon skin file that supplies its values and any decoration. Keep dense-page muted text and border variants named and deliberate. Do not create a cross-repository CSS package or move Nanoleaf wall-rendering tokens into the Hub.
- Apply the approved roles to the shared application shell, navigation, buttons, panels, forms, badges and status/pending/empty treatments where repeated raw values or divergent patterns exist. Keep the established dashboard layout and component views unless a specific approved guide rule calls for a visual change. Record before/after dispositions for existing variants.
- Use the same foundation for activity, component and connection views, including the read-only/unknown component case. Change user-facing dashboard text from `BUNNY` to `B.U.N.N.Y.` in the shell, login, footer and application documentation, consistent with the ADR 0004 decision planned in #181. Keep package names, paths, API identifiers and other machine-facing names stable. Preserve capability and permission explanations, command guards, selection and drafts, focus recovery, pending/uncertain outcomes, stale evidence and no-write inspection. This is presentation work, not new device behavior.
- Keep the Nanoleaf wall map in its owning repository; its geometry, status animation, Prism material and physical-light palette remain device-specific. The work guide and atlas consume the same shared vocabulary through their own [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85) delivery; they do not depend on this React implementation. Nanoleaf and Pixoo editor adoption is deferred with the alternate skin.

## Acceptance criteria and planned evidence

- [ ] **AC1 — Approved mapping.** Every new shared token and dense variant maps to a specific approved #181 rule. Repeated dashboard colors, font stacks, grid and shape values use the named roles where they represent the same meaning; device/task status colors keep their semantics. Evidence: a compact token/usage map and CSS review against the accepted guide. No blanket replacement of an approved screen merely to make hex values identical.
- [ ] **AC2 — Coherent components.** The shell and current views use the same approved treatment for primary/secondary actions, selected navigation, panels, forms, badges and written empty/unavailable states. Pending intent, selection, status and keyboard focus remain visually and semantically distinct. Magenta pending and cyan selection are the Neon mapping. Evidence: before/after browser screenshots for activity, component and connection views and a disposition for any retained dense-page variant.
- [ ] **AC3 — State and accessibility coverage.** Normal, hover, focus, selected, pending, disabled/read-only, stale, error, unknown and empty states remain legible and identifiable without color or motion alone. Check rendered contrast, keyboard order and focus, long labels, reduced motion and no horizontal overflow at desktop, around the 900/680 px layout changes, and narrow mobile. Evidence: browser screenshots and accessibility/contrast results on the actual rendered surfaces; source hex calculations alone do not qualify translucent states.
- [ ] **AC4 — Behavior preservation.** Selection, filtering, reconnect and snapshot reads issue no commands; form drafts and focus survive refresh; guarded command, conflict and uncertain-result behavior remains as before. Evidence: existing dashboard unit/browser scenarios plus focused regression assertions for any changed component markup or interaction. Fake controllers and synthetic state prove source behavior only; no physical-device claim.
- [ ] **AC5 — Display name.** The visible application name reads `B.U.N.N.Y.` in the dashboard shell, login and footer, and the owning dashboard documentation uses the approved spelling. Inspect current rendered pages and search current user-facing source text for the old display spelling. Internal paths, package/API names and the dated system-design atlas are unchanged. No new acronym expansion or logo is introduced. Evidence: source search and screenshots of logged-out and logged-in states.
- [ ] **AC6 — Delivery gates.** Follow the repository SDLC on an isolated branch/worktree. For dashboard changes, run Node 24 setup and the dashboard checks in `docs/development.md`, plus shared build/type/contract/workflow checks from the assigned root. Obtain independent Standards and Specification reviews, all applicable current-head CI, and explicit human approval of this exact UI candidate, renewed after subsequent UI changes. Read back merged-main checks before closure. With no skin selection or persistence this is presentation only: record the no-product-contract-change rationale instead of an OpenSpec change. Installation and physical acceptance remain separate.

## Assessment and readiness

Planning assessment, 2026-09-23; Hub remote `main` `5db67a0944f017d655331ab410c639570c876108`.

- Complexity: **medium** — one token layer and several shared dashboard views/components must stay coherent.
- Uncertainty: **medium** — the approved token names, variants and examples are pending #181; the owner has already selected B.U.N.N.Y. for user-facing text. Current CSS and validation paths are known.
- Impact: **medium** — a styling error can hide control state or make forms inaccessible; the source change is reversible.
- Readiness: **blocked** on #181's approved guide revision and ADR 0004 naming record. Reassess when that input lands, when the dashboard source changes, or if the adopted rules affect behavior or product contracts.

## Authority and coordination

Current authorization updates this planning issue and dependency only. Future delivery owns the UI candidate and its approval; this issue does not implement it or approve a later revision. Coordinate with any active `apps/dashboard` owner before editing shared files. [Hub #6](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/6), [#151](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/151) and [#153](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/153) are delivered behavior inputs, not prerequisites to redo. No service installation, device command, wall-map rewrite, source migration, public-site publication or new shared logo is included.

## Skin structure — planning extension, 2026-09-23 (trimmed)

- [ ] **AC7 — Extensible single skin.** Views use semantic roles only; the Neon skin file supplies their values and decoration. Adding a skin later needs a new skin file, not copies of views or edits to command/state logic. Document how to add one in the dashboard README. Reduced motion (AC3) disables decoration without removing state information.

Deferred to a later issue once its look is chosen: the alternate skin, a skin selector with saved preference, a decoration-off control, and skin-switching lifecycle behavior. Readiness remains blocked by [#181](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/181). Device contracts, services, installations and physical effects remain outside scope.

title: Add explicit recovery for uncertain approval attention
body:
## Outcome
Give a user a protected, explicit way to retire one uncorrelated, uncertain approval indicator in shared agent state. This unblocks [Nanoleaf #72](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/72) without claiming that Codex granted or denied the underlying permission.

## Evidence and boundary
The qualified Codex producer maps `PermissionRequest` to `attention.approval` with an unknown attention ID and currently emits no correlated `attention.resolved` event. The reducer intentionally cannot clear unknown attention by guessing. The two Nanoleaf #72 records have old approval attention and uncertain freshness while the shared feed remains connected. Official Codex hook documentation lists `turn_id` and `tool_name` for `PermissionRequest` but no `tool_use_id`; `PostToolUse` has a tool-call ID. A general automatic match is therefore unproven. See [Codex hooks](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks#permissionrequest).

Hub #138 resets activity and explicitly retains unresolved attention; this issue is a separate, narrow attention recovery operation.

## Scope and acceptance criteria
- [x] Add a protected, revision-guarded operation that targets exactly one session and one currently uncertain approval attention item. Require an explicit user action; no timeout or automatic clearing. Reject stale revision, absent/ambiguous target, and unauthorized requests without modifying state.
- [x] Retire only that shared monitor attention marker. Preserve other attention, activity, notices, labels, preferences, other sessions, and diagnostic evidence. The action does not approve/deny a Codex permission, invoke Codex, acknowledge a notice, or write a device.
- [x] Return an auditable result that a consumer can distinguish from ordinary stale snapshots. Preserve replay and restart behavior. Fresh later approval evidence can create a new indicator.
- [x] Document the limited meaning and privacy boundary. Keep unknown provider correlation explicit; do not infer resolution from `Stop`, elapsed time, or a same-name tool call.
- [x] Regression tests cover exact targeting, authorization, revision/replay, persistence, concurrent/other attention, no agent/device action, and consumer recovery from an uncertain snapshot.

## Verification and delivery
Source-only, including a linked Nanoleaf consumer update under #72. Use isolated state and fake transports. Follow Hub and Nanoleaf review, CI, guarded merge, and guide synchronization gates. Installation and physical acceptance require separate authorization.

title: Report Codex Desktop read state to the shared owner
body:
## Outcome

When you read a finished Codex Desktop task in Codex, consumers that honor read evidence stop showing it as unread. Legacy Nanoleaf did this, and shared mode lost it. The owner reports the state as `read.observed`. Notices and acknowledgments do not change.

## Why

[Nanoleaf #74](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/74) traced the wall's growing unread count to this gap. #195 expires sessions after 24 hours without activity, which stops the growth. But a task you have already read in Codex still shows unread until you acknowledge it or it expires.

## Source (checked September 23, 2026)

- Codex Desktop uses the Windows Codex home, `C:\Users\<user>\.codex` (`/mnt/c/Users/<user>/.codex` from WSL), not WSL `~/.codex`.
- In `.codex-global-state.json`, `electron-thread-read-state-v1.unreadByIdentity` holds one list of unread thread IDs, nested under a host key and a `local:` key. The IDs match Desktop session IDs.
- The list names only unread sessions. Nothing lists read ones.
- The older key that legacy Nanoleaf reads, `electron-persisted-atom-state.unread-thread-ids-by-host-v1`, no longer exists. The format can change again.
- No hook reports reads, and a Linux file watcher on `/mnt/c` receives no events. The poller therefore checks the file's modification time and size every few seconds and parses the file (about 3 MB) only when they change.

## Scope

- [ ] Add a read-only poller to the owner for Codex Desktop sessions (`provider: codex`, `client: desktop`) and a configured file path.
- [ ] A listed session is `unread`. A session missing from a successfully parsed list is `read` if it was listed earlier or its latest turn ended at least 5 seconds ago. Desktop sets the flag shortly after Stop, and legacy Nanoleaf used the same 5-second wait.
- [ ] A missing, unreadable or unexpectedly shaped file produces no events. If the format changes again, the poller goes quiet instead of guessing.
- [ ] Emit only when a session's state changes. This keeps the journal small and does not keep sessions alive under #195.
- [ ] Never touch sessions from other clients or providers. Only `read` or `unread` for known sessions leaves the poller.
- [ ] Record the source and the read rule in [docs/provider-qualification.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/provider-qualification.md).

The owner already stores `read.observed` ([reducer.ts](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/4efab3b4586e32bdedb5415c35a28af31bf78ec8/packages/agent-state/src/reducer.ts#L160)). After a new completion, Desktop lists the session again and it returns to unread, so no reducer change is expected.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Fixture tests cover:
  - a listed session
  - an unlisted session after the wait
  - an unlisted session within the wait that was never listed
  - a missing or malformed file
  - an unchanged file
  - a new completion after read
  - a non-Desktop session
- [ ] Live: read a finished task in Codex Desktop and see Nanoleaf's unread indicator clear. One closing comment records it.

## Dependencies

None. Nanoleaf already hides its unread indicator for `read: read`. #218 uses the same configured Codex home.

## Not included

Changes to notice retention, clearing notices by age (#195 covers expiry), bulk acknowledgment, Claude read evidence, consumer-side provider logic and writing Codex state.

## Readiness

Complexity small. Uncertainty low. Delivery follows docs/sdlc.md.

title: Expire monitoring sessions after 24 hours without activity
body:
## Outcome

The shared owner forgets any session that has had no new agent evidence for 24 hours. That frees owner capacity, which fixes the capacity failure blocking [Tidbyt #21](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/21). It also clears stale rows from the wall, Tidbyt, Pixoo and the dashboard. New activity later creates a fresh entry.

Removing archived Codex tasks sooner is split out to #218.

## Owner policy (September 23, 2026)

- The full session identity stays the monitoring key. Subagents remain separate records.
- Expiry forgets monitoring state. It does not acknowledge, mark read, complete or cancel anything. It applies to sessions with open notices or attention too.
- Expiry may drop task labels, manual task-project associations, Line placement and animation state. Global projects, colors, reservations, scenes, device settings and agent conversations stay.
- New activity after expiry creates a record with defaults. Old effects are not replayed.
- The 128-record limit stays. It counts children.

## Design

The owner already has most of what this needs:

- **Clock.** Use each session's `lastEvidenceAtMs`. It is saved with the session and set only when an event is applied ([reducer.ts](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/4efab3b4586e32bdedb5415c35a28af31bf78ec8/packages/agent-state/src/reducer.ts#L172)). Duplicates, labels and acknowledgments do not change it, and a restart does not reset it.
- **Timing.** Expire alongside the existing 24-hour journal pruning ([index.ts](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/4efab3b4586e32bdedb5415c35a28af31bf78ec8/packages/agent-state/src/index.ts#L59)), at startup, and before rejecting a new identity at capacity. Real rejections still count as loss.
- **Late events.** `runtime.ended` never creates a record, and the owner drops events observed before the 24-hour cutoff. Old events therefore cannot refill freed slots.
- **Children.** Each record expires on its own clock, with no cascade. Child counts are derived from the records present ([children.ts](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/4efab3b4586e32bdedb5415c35a28af31bf78ec8/packages/agent-state/src/children.ts)), so a missing parent or child does not break the snapshot.
- **Consumers.** The snapshot format does not change; expired sessions just disappear. Nanoleaf deletes a missing task's rows, which this policy accepts. The existing resync resets of animations are also accepted.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fake-clock test fills the owner to 128, expires old records, admits new identities and continues past 128 lifetime identities.
- [ ] Tests cover:
  - just before and at 24 hours
  - renewal by a new event
  - no renewal from labels or acknowledgments
  - a restart that keeps the window
- [ ] `runtime.ended` for an unknown identity creates nothing. Events older than the cutoff are dropped. A new start after expiry creates a fresh record.
- [ ] Expired notices and attention disappear without an acknowledgment. Other sessions and global settings are unchanged.
- [ ] Nanoleaf and the dashboard handle a child whose parent expired.
- [ ] Installed: back up the owner database, update the service, and confirm that old sessions leave and `lossCount` stops rising. Then finish the #21 display checks. One comment records this.

## Related work

#191 (read evidence) and #218 (archive removal) are independent follow-ups. [Nanoleaf #80](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/80) groups children for display but frees no capacity. The UI work in Nanoleaf [#75](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/75), [#76](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/76) and [#77](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/77) can proceed on its own. #123, #138 and #139 keep their separate scopes.

## Not included

Archive removal, changes to the per-session notice limit, a cleanup UI, restoring expired tasks, synthetic lifecycle events and a live database reset.

## Readiness

Complexity small to medium: an owner change plus tests. Uncertainty low. Delivery follows docs/sdlc.md.

title: Prepare Codex and Claude task briefs from the mobile work guide
body:
Owner: Hub guide source.

Outcome: open any issue in the guide on a phone or desktop, pick an action and copy a short prompt that starts that work in an existing Codex or Claude app. Plan starts the `plan-work` skill; Implement starts `deliver-work`.

## Scope

- Selecting an issue badge (`a.issue[data-issue]`) opens one native `<dialog>` with the repository, number, title, a GitHub link and four actions: Explain, Plan, Implement and Review. Each action shows its prompt in a read-only textarea with a Copy button. Update the search hint that says issue links open GitHub.
- Build prompts in the browser from the badge's existing key, URL and title. Reference the full issue URL and embed no snapshot context: the agent reads the live issue and the repository's AGENTS.md.
- Prompt templates. Delivery may tune the wording but keeps the skill names and scope limits:
  - Explain: `Explain <issue URL> ("<title>"). Read the issue and the repository's AGENTS.md first. Read-only: don't change files, branches or GitHub.`
  - Plan: `Use the plan-work skill for <issue URL>. Planning only: return proposals and don't change the tracker until I approve. If plan-work isn't available here, say so and stop.`
  - Implement: `Use the deliver-work skill to deliver <issue URL>. If deliver-work isn't available here, say so and stop.`
  - Review: `Review the open pull request for <issue URL>. If there isn't exactly one, ask me which revision to review. Read-only: report findings without changing files or GitHub.`
- Expose `openBrief(key)` so [#201](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/201) can open the same dialog.

Implement uses the deliver-work default finish line (merged PR and closed issue). Edit the pasted prompt to set a narrower limit.

## Acceptance

1. Selecting a Hub, Nanoleaf or Pixoo badge opens the dialog with the correct repository, number, title and URL, and the GitHub link still works. Escape and Close dismiss the dialog and return focus to the badge. At 390 px the page does not overflow.
2. Each prompt uses the full issue URL. Explain and Review state read-only scope; Plan names `plan-work` and planning-only scope; Implement names `deliver-work`. Titles render as text, not markup.
3. Copy writes the prompt to the clipboard. If the Clipboard API is denied or unavailable, including when the guide is opened from `file://`, the textarea text is selected for manual copying.

Evidence: one new `check_guide.cjs` case covering these criteria at 390 px, plus the existing `build_guide.py`, `test_maintenance.py` and `check_guide.cjs` runs. No live agent or device test.

## Delivery

Follow [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md) and the [guide procedure](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/work-guide/README.md). This issue does not verify that a given app session can load `plan-work` or `deliver-work`; that depends on the user's agent setup.

Assessment: complexity low, uncertainty low, impact low (client-side copy only). Ready for source delivery.

title: Show current public GitHub status in the dated guide
body:
Owner: Hub guide source.

Outcome: when the guide opens, its issue badges show current status read directly from GitHub, with one line saying when that status was read. If GitHub can't be reached, the guide keeps its snapshot status and says so.

## Scope

- On page load, send anonymous GitHub REST requests for `agent-device-hub`, `codex-nanoleaf` and `divoom-app-upgrade`:
  - open issues: `/repos/jimmie-potts/<repo>/issues?state=open&per_page=100`
  - issues closed since the snapshot: `/repos/jimmie-potts/<repo>/issues?state=closed&since=<snapshot refreshedAt>&per_page=100`

  Follow `Link` pagination and skip pull requests. All three repositories are public, and the API allows browser requests without sign-in (`access-control-allow-origin: *`, 60 requests an hour per IP). Checked on September 23, 2026.
- Port the `guide_status.py` rules to the page:
  - closed with `state_reason` `completed` → Completed; other closures → Closed
  - `status:review` → In review; `status:in-progress` → In progress
  - `blocked` label or `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0` → Blocked. `blocked_by` counts open blockers only; `total_blocked_by` also counts closed ones.

  Update each badge's symbol, status text, `data-state`, `data-status`, `title` and `aria-label`.
- Add one freshness line, for example "Status from GitHub at 14:32. Guide text and counts from the 23 Sep snapshot." or "GitHub unavailable; showing 23 Sep snapshot status."
- Update the guide intro sentence that says the guide loads nothing remote.
- No refresh button: reloading the page refreshes status.

## Acceptance

1. When every read succeeds, each badge shows the status the ported rules give for the live data, and the freshness line shows the read time. Guide prose, counts and "Waiting for" text keep their snapshot values, and the page labels them as snapshot values.
2. Missing data never changes a status. If any read for a repository fails, including 403 or 429 rate limiting, that repository's badges keep snapshot status and the freshness line names the repository. An issue absent from both reads keeps its snapshot status.
3. The page renders completely without the requests. Offline and `file://` use fall back to snapshot status without console errors. Values from GitHub are written as text, not markup.

Evidence: `check_guide.cjs` cases with routed fake API responses covering a closed issue, a newly blocked issue, an issue in review, a second results page and one failed repository, plus the existing `build_guide.py`, `test_maintenance.py` and `check_guide.cjs` runs. Update the check's external-request expectation to allow only GET requests to `api.github.com`.

## Delivery

Follow [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md) and the [guide procedure](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/work-guide/README.md). body:
