Owner: Hub collector source and public guide operations.

Outcome: public status stays useful without a visitor login or repeated manual whole-guide rebuilds.

Required inputs: [#197](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/197)'s accepted projection/reader and [#87](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/87)'s verified deployment path. Implement only after those exact artifacts are reviewed.

Acceptance and planned evidence:

1. Document a narrow data-only publishing policy before enabling automation. The existing rule forbids refreshing data in the public copy; any exception must name the source-owned generator/version, exact allowed status files, validation, actor, and permitted publication path. Human-authored HTML/JS/diagram changes keep normal PR/review gates. Policy and workflow changes cannot waive their own review/CI.
2. Propose a 30-minute refresh target plus owner-triggered refresh, with visible last-success time and no exact scheduling guarantee. Serialize runs, coalesce duplicates, respect GitHub retry/rate-limit signals, and produce no change when inputs are unchanged. Verify scheduling configuration and concurrent-run/failure fixtures; tune cadence from measured workload before activation.
3. Run the pinned collector with the narrowest required credential and repository access, outside browser assets. Choose the supported existing execution provider during delivery and record why. Validate the full projection before publishing, retain the last-good generation on error, and report failures to the owner through an explicitly selected operational route.
4. Demonstrate a changed public issue flowing into the published feed without rewriting the atlas baseline or unrelated guide HTML. Verify source/public provenance, live feed bytes, changed UI state, a no-change run, and a failed-run stale state. Use disposable fixtures until an operational trial is separately authorized.
5. Document enable/disable, credential revocation, recovery from partial publication, and restoration of the prior generation. Initial activation requires the named installation/publication owner. Source tests do not claim an active schedule.

Locations: source collector, owning development/CI/publishing procedure, and narrowly scoped public deployment integration. Keep one coordinating writer across repositories.

Assessment: complexity medium (scheduled collection/deployment); uncertainty medium (provider/credential/publishing exception must be selected); impact high (automated public writes). Blocked by [#197](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/197)/#87 and the reviewed operational policy. Source work and activation have separate evidence. Excludes unattended HTML/code deployment, issue mutation, repo visibility changes, and an always-on agent runner.

## Delivery and evidence boundary

Planning baseline: September 23, 2026; Hub `600d9055dacaa242cc188cf5cbca19c04f08f484`, public guide `6f2289cf3ca743abe2f13add88be2d58446953e7`. Reasoning setting: unknown. All implementation, browser, performance, deployment, and installed-client checks described here are planned, not executed.

title: Navigate development through an interactive mission map
body:
Owner: Hub guide UI.

Outcome: select meaningful next work through a map that opens the same task brief as the list view.

Required inputs: [#196](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/196) `openBrief(key)` function and [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85) Neon tokens and decoration layer. [#197](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/197) status integration is optional: use its qualified generation when available, otherwise label the snapshot. No silent live claim.

Acceptance and planned evidence:

1. Reuse existing guide/timeline issue and dependency semantics. Show repository sectors, selected prerequisites, downstream consequences, and issue links. A map/list switch retains the same selection and counts. Fixture checks establish stable issue identity and no duplicate ownership.
2. Show ready, blocked, deferred, active, and unknown conditions with text/shape as well as color. Existing conservative readiness rules remain authoritative. Missing dependencies and stale evidence withhold confident availability. Test all conditions and cross-repository paths.
3. Selecting an objective opens [#196](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/196). Touch targets, pan/zoom/fit, keyboard navigation, focus, and a complete list alternative work at phone widths. Decorative particles never intercept input. Browser journeys cover selection during refresh and deep-link navigation.
4. Use brief selection/route pulses with pause/reduced-motion and hidden/offscreen suspension. Do not animate structural geometry continuously while reading. Check on a real phone that pulses don't stall scrolling.

Locations: `timeline.py`, guide generator/styles/JS and browser tests; reuse existing graph inputs. Inspect whether [#73](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/73) affects the chosen routes; coordinate its owner rather than claiming its repair or adding a blanket dependency from the issue title alone.

Assessment: complexity medium; uncertainty medium (dense mobile graph layout); impact low (read-only navigation). Blocked by [#196](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/196)/#85. title: Follow a signal through the atlas with controlled playback
body:
Owner: Hub atlas and shared diagram definitions.

Outcome: readers can play, pause, step, and replay the existing source-pinned agent observation walkthrough, with the active segment explained beside the diagram.

Required input: [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85) Neon tokens and decoration layer. Existing [#172](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/172) implementation is the foundation, not new feature scope to duplicate.

Acceptance and planned evidence:

1. Add Play/Pause, previous/next step, and replay to the existing phase selection. A pulse follows only the documented active edge; participants, segment IDs, source revisions, and alternative paths retain their meanings. Test phase/edge correspondence and first/last/alternative boundaries.
2. Selecting a phase directly cancels or repositions playback deterministically. Theme, resize, hide/show, and repeated initialization cannot create duplicate clocks or surprise replays. Controlled-clock browser tests cover these paths.
3. Each phase remains readable without motion. Keyboard/touch controls, reduced motion, pause, labels, and print/export preserve the information. Clearly label the animation as a walkthrough of documented behavior, not live agent/device telemetry.
4. Include approved current atlas candidate, desktop/narrow/mobile browser evidence, and actual-phone playback acceptance after publication. Changes to shared diagram definitions require fresh render/spec receipts and both guide and atlas checks.

Assessment: complexity medium; uncertainty low-to-medium (extending observed phase controls); impact low (read-only explanation). Blocked by [#85](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/85). Excludes scenario fault injection, device calls, broad diagram redrawing, and fabricated runtime traffic.

title: Define the owner workspace, sign-in, and outbound connector boundary
body:
Owner: Hub architecture, with public-site integration as a consumer.

Outcome: an accepted design for optional private coordination from the public guide, using the qualified app capabilities from [#199](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/199).

Required input: [#199](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/199)'s capability/authentication evidence for the intended app path. The output must settle implementation-changing decisions before [#204](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/204)/[#205](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/205) are called ready.

Acceptance and planned evidence:

1. Compare a private-network-only route with a small authenticated HTTPS service and outbound PC connector for the actual phone workflow. Select hosting, reachability, operational owner, account/provider, and expected costs with the user. No hosting purchase or service setup occurs in this design task.
2. Recommend GitHub sign-in with one allowed owner account and a secure server session; define the final mechanism, expiration/revocation, CSRF/origin handling, and narrowly scoped GitHub access. Authentication and operation authorization remain separate. Public HTML/assets must never contain private records or long-lived credentials.
3. Define a private task record keyed to repository/issue, with explicit user-chosen label, agent/session reference, worktree reference, decisions, questions, handoff, PR, evidence, and next action. GitHub remains status authority. Preserve one active writer per deliverable. Keep these records and message contents out of the existing shared monitoring feed and public export.
4. Define API/adapter boundaries for drafts, queued/sent/delivered/answered/uncertain outcomes, offline PCs, duplicate submissions, cancellation, reconnect, expiration, account revocation, and ownership changes. Do not conflate notice dismissal, message delivery, agent receipt, and successful implementation.
5. Locate responsibilities in existing apps/hub and apps/dashboard where appropriate. If internet reachability requires a separate small relay, name its narrow ownership and justify it. Do not expose the loopback device-control listener or create a second agent-state owner.
6. Record the decision through the repository's ADR/OpenSpec conventions and refine [#204](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/204)/[#205](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/205) into exact contracts and checks. Security/concurrency review inspects the boundary before implementation. Public reads continue when the private service is unavailable.

Assessment: complexity high; uncertainty high (hosting, app access, and authentication require decisions); impact high (remote authenticated commands and private data). Blocked by [#199](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/199) and future owner choices, not part of the anonymous release. No new general-purpose orchestrator, organization role system, device remote-control scope, or embedded chat replacement.

title: Deliver the first qualified native-app handoff from the phone workspace
body:
Owner: Hub work service and the selected native-app connector.

Outcome: send a prepared task or follow-up from the phone to one verified native-app path and observe its actual delivery state. The other app retains manual handoff until independently qualified.

Required inputs: [#199](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/199) selected supported adapter/version, [#203](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/203) command/ownership contract, and [#204](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/204) owner inbox. Choose the first app from the qualification result and user workflow; do not promise arbitrary existing-session access. If no supported path qualifies, keep this blocked and retain the manual workflow.

Acceptance and planned evidence:

1. The paired connector uses an outbound authenticated connection and an explicitly selected machine/project/session target. It cannot accept anonymous commands or route to arbitrary executables. The app's actual sandbox/approval boundaries remain effective. Test revoked pairing, wrong owner/target, and unavailable capability.
2. Request identity prevents duplicate starts/deliveries across repeated taps, retries, and reconnects. Offline requests remain visibly queued; expired/cancelled requests do not replay unexpectedly. Uncertain outcomes require reconciliation rather than automatic resubmission. Verify with failure/concurrency fixtures.
3. Show only evidenced queued, delivered, waiting-for-input, answered, failed, or uncertain states. Never infer task completion from process exit, transport acknowledgment, or lifecycle stop. Copy/manual handoff remains available without creating duplicate execution.
4. Route a supported question/reply flow if the chosen client supplies it; unsupported cells stay disabled with explanations. Correlate replies to the right request/turn and reject stale replies according to the accepted contract.
5. Before live activation, record the named owner, actual phone/browser, PC/WSL/client versions, account/authentication path, allowed workspace, and recovery procedure. Separately authorized end-to-end acceptance demonstrates one request, one follow-up, disconnect/reconnect, offline queue, revocation, and return to the native app. Synthetic tests do not qualify these behaviors.
6. Source and installed rollout receipts stay separate. A second app adapter is its own subsequent bounded item derived from [#199](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/199); do not expand this pilot into an unverified multi-provider framework.

Assessment: complexity high; uncertainty high until installed capabilities are proven; impact high (remote instructions can initiate development). Blocked, not implementation-ready today. Excludes device control, unattended merge authority, app-database manipulation, and replacing the Codex/Claude UI.

It does not start implementation, modify repository visibility, install credentials/hooks/services, launch agents, activate schedules, contact devices, or publish a website. Guide-source synchronization, public publication, and real-phone/installed acceptance remain separate future effects. Private task records and conversations never enter the public feed or the existing metadata-only monitoring service.

title: Clean up delivered worktrees and scratch after merge
body:
## Outcome

Deliveries clean up after themselves. After a PR merges and main CI passes, the coordinator removes its own worktree and scratch files, so finished work stops piling up on the host.

On 2026-09-23 the WSL host's `/tmp` (a 7.6 GB RAM-backed tmpfs shared by all agent sessions) filled completely. Most of it was finished per-issue checkouts, each with its own `node_modules`, left behind after their PRs merged. There were also 48 stale worktree registrations across four repositories. No repository rule said when a delivery should clean up, and the shared deliver-work skill keeps artifacts when no retention rule exists. Host-level storage guidance (large work goes under `.local/`, not `/tmp`) now lives in the global agent instructions; this issue adds the repository-level retention rule.

## Scope

- `docs/sdlc.md`: add a cleanup step after the main-CI readback. The coordinator removes its own clean worktree with `git worktree remove` (never forced) and deletes its own `.local/scratch/<task>` folder, after confirming that required evidence is in the PR, the issue or the main checkout's `.local/evidence/`. Because this repository squash-merges, delivery is judged by the PR's merged state, not commit ancestry. Failed or abandoned work is kept until the user decides. Other sessions' worktrees, branches and scratch stay untouched.
- `docs/development.md`: when the default `node` is not 24, run commands through `fnm exec --using=.nvmrc --` and reuse one shared Node 24 installation instead of installing Node per task.

Out of scope: host-level storage rules, removing existing worktrees under `.local/worktrees`, and CI changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- `docs/sdlc.md` contains the cleanup step with the conditions above.
- `docs/development.md` contains the fnm note.
- `npm run check:workflow` and `npm run test:workflow` exit zero, and every configured Depot job succeeds on the PR head and the merged main revision.

## Dependencies

None. The same retention rule is proposed for codex-nanoleaf and divoom-app-upgrade in linked issues.

## Verification

Local workflow checks, Depot CI, and independent Standards and Specification reviews.

## Delivery target

Merged to `main`.

title: Make the work guide clipboard-fallback check pass in Depot CI
body:
## Outcome

The work guide's browser check passes in Depot CI again, so main's Work guide job is green and deliveries blocked on merged-main evidence can close.

## Problem

`docs/work-guide/work/check_guide.cjs:214` asserts that a denied clipboard makes the task brief select its prompt for manual copying (`A denied clipboard selects the prompt`). The test gets its "denied" case by calling `clearPermissions()` and relying on headless Chromium to reject `navigator.clipboard.writeText`. Main's Work guide job on `a19a62eb673fd17a5aecdb1db6b5575947e2feb7` failed on this assertion twice: check runs 107425147844 and 107426083706, Depot attempts `4z0gb8j2xf` and `cbcfp3cqdr`. The assertion arrived in #209 (Refs #196). That was a guide-only change, so Depot never ran it before merge.

## Scope

- Reproduce the failure with CI's browser (Playwright 1.63.0 and its headless Chromium shell).
- Make the denied and missing clipboard cases deterministic, so they no longer depend on the browser's default permission. Keep the real granted-clipboard copy check.
- Change the guide's copy behavior only if the reproduction shows a product defect rather than a test-environment assumption.

Out of scope: guide content or snapshot refreshes, and other guide checks.

## Acceptance criteria

- The Work guide job passes on Depot for the candidate: a `depot ci run` of `.depot/workflows/work-guide.yml` with the change, plus main's Work guide job after merge (the next non-guide merge runs it).
- Locally: `build_guide.py`, `test_maintenance.py` and `check_guide.cjs` pass, and `git diff --exit-code -- docs/work-guide/outputs` shows no drift.

## Dependencies

Regression from #196 (#209). Blocks closure of #207.

## Verification

A red/green reproduction with CI's browser, a Depot run of the Work guide workflow, local guide checks, and independent Standards and Specification reviews.

## Delivery target

Merged to `main`, with main's Work guide job green.

title: Clear Codex Desktop tasks and Line assignments when sessions end
body:
## Outcome

Retire an ended Codex Desktop session and its known descendants from the shared owner in one durable update. Existing consumers remove the task: Nanoleaf releases its Line assignments, Tidbyt and Pixoo update their monitoring displays, and the dashboard removes its row.

The owner retires within seconds of accepting `runtime.ended`. Displays follow their existing polling, write cadence and transport availability; this is not a promise that all physical devices clear simultaneously.

Scope simplified with the user on September 24, 2026. The agreed retirement behavior and safeguards remain.

## Policy

The [Codex hook reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks#sessionend) documents `SessionEnd` for archive/delete of an open conversation, normal shutdown, and a conversation idle and unopened in any connected client for 30 minutes. The existing normalizer maps these to the same `runtime.ended` event; its reason is currently `"other"`. No new idle timer or cause detection is needed.

- Apply retirement to `provider: codex`, `client: desktop`. Keep other provider/client policies unchanged in this delivery; [Hub #241](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/241) extends the same owner rule to Codex CLI and Claude Code afterward.
- Remove the parent and descendants linked by known parent identities together. Do not guess relationships or terminate agents.
- Use [#195's forgetting policy](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/195): notices, attention, task labels, task-project overrides, Line placement and animation state may be discarded. This is not acknowledgment, readership, success or cancellation. Preserve unrelated sessions, global projects, colors, reservations, scenes, settings and conversations.
- Ordinary turn completion, waiting for input, read/acknowledgment changes and five-minute freshness uncertainty do not retire sessions. A turn exceeding 30 minutes does not trigger cleanup just because of its duration.
- Keep the 24-hour evidence expiry as the fallback for absent/lost ends, with each record's existing expiry clock.
- Eligible new work after resume or unarchive creates a fresh monitoring record with defaults, without old-effect replay. Retain protection against recognizable delayed events and document unknown-ordering limits.

## Bounded implementation

1. Extend the owner's existing atomic session-removal path from #195 and publish the normal snapshot revision. No new cleanup service, per-device cleanup command or physical writer.
2. Reuse consumer reconciliation. Add focused checks for Nanoleaf, Tidbyt, Pixoo and the dashboard; change a consumer only where a check demonstrates a gap. Retain device queues, native modes, scene restoration, cadence and resynchronization behavior. Report unrelated existing animation limitations separately.
3. Keep archive lookup out of retirement. Cleanup works without Codex-home configuration or a readable archive folder. Retain read-only archive evidence solely as an admission safeguard against archived tasks returning through delayed events, using [#191's configuration](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/191). Missing/unreadable files supply no evidence; never write or move Codex files.
4. Keep retirement/resume handling bounded and durable across restart. Resolve the case where a consumer misses retirement and sees the same conversation identity recreated at its next read. Preserve fresh-record semantics without assuming every intermediate snapshot was observed.
5. Update the issue-linked OpenSpec change, affected lifecycle/state contract and guide, compatibility assessment and required checks. Use the smallest change demonstrated necessary by the focused scenarios below.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] One normalized `runtime.ended` scenario verifies atomic parent/known-descendant retirement, capacity release and one published revision. Retain provider-mapping coverage; do not duplicate identical unit tests for the four documented end causes.
- [x] Unknown/repeated ends create nothing. Unrelated sessions and global settings survive.
- [x] Ordinary completion, waiting, read/acknowledgment changes, freshness uncertainty and a turn lasting over 30 minutes retain the session; fake-clock coverage preserves the separate 24-hour fallback.
- [x] Archive admission tests cover available archive evidence, absent configuration, missing/unreadable folders, delayed events and new work after unarchive.
- [x] Focused tests cover recognizable delayed events, same-identity resume, a recognizable old end after resume, owner restart and a consumer missing the entire retirement between reads. New monitoring records start fresh and old effects do not replay.
- [x] Cover child events after parent retirement and state the admission rule and limits of missing identity/order evidence.
- [x] Existing-consumer checks verify Nanoleaf assignment release, Tidbyt/Pixoo monitoring updates and dashboard removal, including reconnect. If nothing remains to display, preserve each consumer's existing idle behavior. Fix change-caused regressions without redesigning unrelated effects.
- [ ] Existing installed/live acceptance remains: with separate installation and named-device authorization, use throwaway conversations for an archive end, a non-archive end and resume. Observe dashboard removal, visible Nanoleaf Line release and fresh monitoring. Record timing and distinguish source, installed-client and visible-device evidence. Other consumer checks do not require repeating complete hardware qualification.
- [ ] Reopen-to-read: as part of the separately authorized installed resume trial, reopen a retired throwaway conversation that is not archived, without submitting a prompt. Record whether Desktop emits `SessionStart` or other lifecycle hooks and whether the owner recreates a monitoring record; read evidence alone must not recreate one. Document the consequence for [Nanoleaf #110](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/110): a recreated record would count toward Work when automation is enabled; otherwise reopening adds no session presence. Distinguish observed hook/owner behavior from the expected future automation behavior; implementing #110 is not a prerequisite for this check.

## Dependencies and boundaries

[#195](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/195) is complete. [#191](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/191) supplies the archive safeguard's Codex-home context, not a prerequisite for receiving ends.

[Hub #241](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/241) follows this delivery and generalizes accepted-end retirement across the supported providers. It is not a blocker for #218 and does not expand #218's active PRs or acceptance scope.

[Nanoleaf #110](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/110) is a downstream consumer of authoritative session presence/removal, with #241 as an additional prerequisite for consistent provider behavior. It owns automatic Work/Free switching and manual override; this issue issues no mode commands. An unavailable feed must not be represented as a healthy empty snapshot.

No archive polling, App Server client, Windows watcher, archive browser, restoration history, new dashboard feature, Claude/CLI policy change or future LIFX/PC-lighting integration. Those future consumers do not block delivery. This issue does not block completed [Tidbyt #21](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/21).

## Readiness

Ready for source work under docs/sdlc.md, with the bounded retirement/admission design and focused checks before delivery. Complexity remains medium because resume/order handling needs care; existing removal and consumer paths keep the implementation contained. This tracker revision authorizes no implementation, installation or device operation.

title: Refresh work-guide priorities, new issues and defects, and reorganize topic guides
body:
## Outcome

Make the work guide useful for choosing current work. Replace stale milestone-led opening cards with current work, newly added issues, all open defects, useful next steps, blockers and decisions, and later work. Reorganize the twelve historical guides into eleven topic guides plus a completed-milestones archive.

## Accepted design

The owner approved this design in the planning conversation and requested definition and implementation.

- Opening order: Current work → Newly added → Open defects → Useful next steps → Blockers and decisions → Later.
- Newly added: the latest eight open issues across all three repositories, sorted by creation date, with an expandable view of all open issues created in the last seven days. Creation date is distinct from edits and priority. Keep deferred and blocked qualifiers visible.
- Open defects: every open issue labeled `bug`, including blocked and deferred defects. Show the issue, affected feature/problem, status, owning guide, and a recorded workaround where available. Order by explicit priority where recorded, then newest first; do not infer severity or invent workarounds. Closed defects leave this view.
- Useful next steps explain the benefit, next action and gate. An issue without a recorded blocker is not automatically a recommendation. Pixoo embedded-host performance #61 is later by owner choice, even if its tracker lacks a deferred label.
- Eleven guides: Monitoring accuracy and recovery; B.U.N.N.Y. interface and device controls; Nanoleaf wall map and effects; Adding devices (separate Panels, Tidbyt, LIFX and deferred PC lighting tracks); Pixoo media and playlists; Music playback and presentation; Shortcuts and desk presets; Work guide and system atlas; Automation and remote access; Hosting and migrations; Engineering maintenance.
- Preserve completed evidence in an expandable archive. Each open issue has exactly one primary guide. Overview lists are references and do not inflate counts. Preserve old deep links, search, expand/collapse, print, task briefs, architecture viewers and live status behavior.
- Surface snapshot/freshness boundaries honestly. New/current/defect membership must agree with the data source named by each view; failed live refresh retains a clearly dated snapshot. Unknown or newly discovered issues remain reachable rather than silently disappearing.

## Implementation and acceptance

- [x] Refresh all three saved backlog inputs and reconcile issue coverage, current next steps and stale sequences (including Panels trial before map selector). Preserve separately dated architecture/history receipts; no new architecture behavior or invented delivery milestones.
- [x] Implement the opening sections and eleven-guide organization, including all open bugs, creation-date ordering, deferred visibility and the performance choice.
- [x] Preserve unique primary ownership, old anchors and existing guide interactions; document selection/freshness rules in the guide README.

## Scope and coordination

One coordinator owns the Hub guide source PR. Inputs cover Hub, Nanoleaf and Pixoo; implementation is confined to `docs/work-guide/`. This is generated documentation/navigation tooling with no product API, state, provider, device or runtime behavior change, so no product OpenSpec capability is introduced. Existing issue scopes and dependencies remain authoritative. No product implementation, installation or device actions are included.

The owner explicitly authorized merge and public publication. After source merge, publish the exact reviewed artifacts through a companion public-repository PR, verify its deployment and unauthenticated served hashes, and record source and public revisions separately. Do not close other roadmap issues merely because this guide links or summarizes them. Existing UI/style/mission-map issues retain their own scope.

Completed in [Hub PR #221](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/221), merged as `ddeecd8a4da9d6fc57c9f0506ff36157389bbfd6`. Both exact-candidate Depot filters, PR/main comparisons and empty check/status/run readbacks satisfy the documented guide-only CI exception; no hosted source CI success is claimed. Architecture/viewer bytes and separately dated history were preserved.

The live browser showed all six opening sections, eleven topic guides and all three current open defects, with current GitHub reads for all repositories and no page errors.

title: Push hub change notifications when state commits
body:
## Outcome

Readers of the hub's change stream learn about a new revision as soon as it commits, instead of up to a second later. The dashboard updates right after a hook event. Nanoleaf can later replace its once-a-second poll with this stream.

## Current behavior

`GET /api/monitor/v1/changes` is a Server-Sent Events stream. Each open stream runs its own 1-second timer. The timer reads the owner snapshot, compares a small fingerprint (revision, collector, loss count, rejected admissions, uncertain count) and writes a `state` event or a heartbeat ([server.ts](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/99ff4cc6a62b0407d452f4ac22718e22e754c3e9/apps/hub/src/server.ts#L245-L275)). A commit reaches readers 0 to 1 s later.

The agent-state core already signals every commit with `feeds.publish(revision)` ([index.ts](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/99ff4cc6a62b0407d452f4ac22718e22e754c3e9/packages/agent-state/src/index.ts#L113)), but the hub doesn't listen. `owner.subscribe` doesn't fit: it takes a configured consumer ID and allows one subscription per ID.

Commits come from more than the events route:

- hook ingest
- the Codex Desktop read-state reader from #219, which calls `owner.ingest` in-process
- label, acknowledge and recovery commands
- journal maintenance

## Scope

- [ ] Give the hub a commit notification from the owner that needs no consumer ID. One option is a listener on the owner API that the core calls where it calls `feeds.publish`. Hooking the core covers every commit source, including future ones, without wrapping each hub call.
- [ ] On each notification, run the existing publish step for every open stream. Coalesce a burst of commits into at most one write per stream.
- [ ] Keep the 1-second timer for heartbeats, the per-stream auth recheck and changes that don't commit (collector state, loss count, rejected admissions).
- [ ] Keep the wire format and limits as they are: event IDs, the 32-entry replay window, resync on an unknown cursor, the 16-stream cap and disconnecting a reader stalled for more than 5 s.
- [ ] A slow or paused reader must not delay ingest, commits or other readers. A listener error must not reach the commit path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A hub test shows a committed event reaching an open stream without waiting for the timer, for example by setting a long timer interval in the test.
- [ ] Tests cover a burst of commits, a commit from the in-process read-state reader and a paused reader that doesn't delay ingest.
- [ ] The existing feed tests pass unchanged: hub HTTP, dashboard matrix and the performance stalled-reader check.
- [ ] The agent-state and standalone hub checks listed in AGENTS.md pass.
- [ ] Live, after the installed monitor is updated separately: watch `/changes` with `curl -N`, submit a Codex prompt and confirm the `state` event arrives well under a second after the hook. One comment records it.

## Not included

- Nanoleaf reading the stream instead of polling. That is [codex-nanoleaf#90](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/90), which this issue blocks.
- Tidbyt's 30-second poll. Its writes are at least 15 s apart, so earlier notice doesn't help it.
- Session data in the stream, and any message broker.

## Readiness

Complexity small. Uncertainty low. No blockers. The owner API addition is a minor agent-state version. Delivery follows docs/sdlc.md.

title: Clear no-ID approval markers when their turn is retired
Check Tidbyt stale-status readability with night mode enabled
body:
## Problem

During #21 physical acceptance on 2026-09-24, the owner could read the dim `X-4F8C RUN` row only after it was pointed out. The owner also confirmed the `?` stale marker but described it as too dim to really see. The owner chose to record this as a separate follow-up rather than block #21.

The owner then clarified that Tidbyt night mode was enabled and device brightness was turned far down during these observations. The observations therefore do not isolate renderer dimming from the device-wide night-mode brightness reduction.

## Outcome

Keep stale status text and its uncertainty marker legible on the physical Tidbyt while preserving the distinction between current and uncertain evidence.

## Scope

Assess readability with the owner's intended night-mode settings before deciding whether a renderer change is needed. Record night mode and device brightness for each physical comparison. The renderer currently applies one-third brightness to uncertain rows in `controllers/tidbyt/src/status.ts`; this combines with device-wide brightness. If a presentation change is needed, preserve lifecycle interpretation, stale thresholds, status priority, rotation and publishing cadence. Do not change device brightness or night-mode settings without the owner's approval.

## Acceptance criteria

- Record whether the existing presentation is readable at the intended night-mode and brightness settings.
- If a renderer change is needed, the owner approves the revised normal and stale frame candidates.
- Any renderer change passes focused renderer checks and applicable repository checks.
- Separately authorized physical observation confirms that the label, state word and uncertainty marker are readable in the owner's usual viewing conditions.
- Missing or stale evidence remains visibly uncertain; it is not rendered as confirmed-current activity.

Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. Source delivery and physical acceptance are separate. This follow-up does not block #21.

title: Add optional shared playback artwork from the Sony source
body:
## Outcome

Add optional artwork to the shared playback service from [#175](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175), beginning with the Sony HT-A9 source. Acquire it once through the owning source/service so the BUNNY UI and display integrations can reuse it. Keep text-only now-playing and controls usable when artwork is missing.

## Scope and acceptance

- [ ] **AC1.** Define an optional source-scoped artwork reference/result in the shared contract. Sony-specific retrieval remains in the Sony module; shared consumers receive no private receiver URL. Keep the interface usable by future adapters and make unsupported/missing artwork explicit.
- [ ] **AC2.** Fetch only from the configured receiver under a documented size/time bound; validate the returned image bytes. The qualification observed JPEG bytes with `text/plain` and transient missing artwork, so do not require a correct MIME header or block metadata on artwork arrival.
- [ ] **AC3.** Keep only the current artwork or a small bounded cache. Do not attach delayed artwork from an earlier observation/source to the current track. Cover missing, delayed, invalid and oversized data and source/track changes with fake responses; no persistent artwork library is needed.

- [ ] **AC6.** Before closing this acquisition story, identify open work for visible artwork in the UI and on Pixoo/Tidbyt. Use [#37](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/37) and [#38](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/38) while they remain open; if their text-only deliveries have closed, create and link small rendering follow-ups. No web artwork search, Apple account/catalog access, unbounded downloads, playback history, discovery or new device writer.

Follow [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [docs/sdlc.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/sdlc.md), the owning hub/development guides and the issue-linked OpenSpec change. Retain independent Standards/Specification review and applicable local, PR and merged-revision CI. Tracker changes do not authorize implementation or installation. title: Document connecting device controllers for BUNNY in the hub setup guide
body:
## Outcome

An installation owner can enable BUNNY general controls on an installed hub by following the hub setup guide. They should not need to reconstruct the steps from source.

## Background

During [#154](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/154) and [#155](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/155) on September 24, 2026, the installed hub already contained the #151 and #153 UI. Its configuration had `"controllers": []`, so BUNNY could not command any device. [apps/hub/README.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/apps/hub/README.md) describes the controller fields. Neither [SETUP.md](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/apps/hub/SETUP.md) nor the [dashboard guide](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/apps/dashboard/README.md) explains how to wire a device in. The coordinator worked out the steps from source and the device repositories.

## Scope

Add a "Connect device controllers for BUNNY" section to `apps/hub/SETUP.md` covering:

- **Prerequisites.** The device controller must be running and expose `/controller/v1` on numeric loopback. For Pixoo that means device mode and `PIXOO_CONTROLLER_ENABLED=1`. For Nanoleaf it means the controller service.
- **A dedicated principal per device**, created with each owner's command, so the hub never reuses another client's credential:
  - Nanoleaf: `nanoleaf controller-token --principal <id>`.
  - Pixoo: `npm run mcp:credentials -- add <data-dir> <id> control`.
- **The controller entry:** `id`, `kind`, `controllerId`, `deviceId`, `endpoint` and `token`. Show how to read `controllerId` and `deviceId` from a native snapshot. Keep tokens only in the owner-only config, and never print them.
- **Back up, then restart the hub service,** and verify: health lists each device, native snapshots validate, and the launcher session shows the controls.
- **Rollback:** restore the config, revoke each principal, restart.
- **Troubleshooting:**
  - A registered device shows `unknown` health until its first request.
  - Pixoo Monitor presentation needs an explicit mode command after an app start.
  - A controller stopped mid-session reports unavailable until it returns.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] SETUP.md has the section above, with placeholders instead of private paths, IPs or tokens.
- [ ] The dashboard guide links to it from "Build and access".
- [ ] A reviewer can follow the section against a disposable hub and the fake controllers used by the existing tests. No installed service or device is touched.

## Planning and delivery

Documentation only, with no product behavior delta. Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. No work-guide refresh is needed.

title: Add the Sonos Move as a second playback source
body:
## Outcome

When the iPhone plays Apple Music to the Sonos Move over AirPlay, BUNNY shows what is playing and can send pause, next and previous, the same as for the Sony HT-A9 today. Today the hub sees nothing while the Move is playing; the HT-A9 reports AirPlay as `inactive`.

## Context

- [#158](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/158) qualified the Move through its local UPnP AVTransport API ([qualification record](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/iphone-apple-music-qualification.md#sonos-move-check)): title, artist, album, duration and position, plus phone-confirmed Pause, Next and Previous. Previous restarted the current song. UPnP event callbacks were not tested across WSL's NAT, so start with polling.
- [#175](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/175) delivered the shared playback module with one source. Its archived design describes the two-source flow this issue would implement: each source keeps its own freshness, one explicitly selected source drives the snapshot and commands, commands never go to another source, and an unavailable selected source is shown as unavailable instead of switching silently.

## Scope

- A Sonos source module that implements `PlaybackSource`, with a private numeric IPv4 endpoint and a neutral source ID.
- Multi-source support in the shared module and configuration: several sources, one explicit selection and per-source snapshots. A way to change the selection is part of this issue; choose between a config edit and an authenticated command when planning.
- Optional position and duration fields in the shared snapshot, since the Move supplies them.

Out of scope: grouped speakers, discovery, artwork (#229) and UI (#37).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Fake-endpoint tests for the Sonos source and for two sources with independent freshness, explicit selection and no silent fallback.
- [ ] Hub guide updated for configuration, selection and the new fields.
- [ ] Live check with the owner: a track change on the Move reaches the hub, and pause reaches the phone.

Only worth picking up if the owner plays to the Move regularly.

title: Qualify enforceable Hub merge gates and guide-only CI handling
body:
## Outcome

Define concrete, enforceable Hub merge gates that fit one maintainer and the existing guide-only CI exception. Finish with a reviewable configuration proposal and a clearly owned implementation step.

## Evidence and scope

On 2026-09-24, the effective-rules API for `main` returned no rules, classic protection reported an unprotected branch, and ruleset `23854742` had an empty branch inclusion list, no required checks and zero required approvals. The written SDLC gates remain procedural.

Inspect current GitHub/Depot capabilities and the repository's actual checks. This is a bounded design/qualification task for the Hub, not an organization-wide governance rollout.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Propose the exact branch target, allowed merge behavior, applicable check identities and trusted check producers. Retain guarded merges, deletion/force-push protection and required current-revision evidence. Name what GitHub can enforce and what remains procedural.
- [ ] Account for the shared GitHub identity used by the maintainer and agents. Do not assume an agent review appears as an independent native approving review or require an unavailable second human account. Identify a feasible review-evidence check and its trust limits; do not substitute a self-reported marker for independent review.
- [ ] Resolve guide-only compatibility. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/100 deliberately disabled automatic guide-only CI. Compare retaining that local-evidence exception with a small hosted guide validation path using existing generation, consistency, maintenance and browser checks. Explain cost, bookkeeping and failure tradeoffs. Keep the current policy until an explicit scope decision changes it; never emit dummy success for unexecuted validation.
- [ ] Walk through a normal source change, failed/missing/stale checks, a guide-only change, a mixed change and changed review scope/head. Identify cases the proposed rules permit or block and any capability that still needs a controlled trial. No disposable PRs or settings changes during this design task.
- [ ] Record the recommendation, unresolved owner decisions and recovery procedure in the issue. Before closing, link the accepted implementation/configuration work or record an explicit decision to retain procedural controls. A proposal is not enabled protection.

## Delivery and readiness

Ready for read-only qualification. Medium complexity and uncertainty from CI filtering and GitHub review identity; high impact if incorrect rules allow unsafe merges or block routine delivery. No incoming source dependency. Existing #100 is policy context, not unfinished work.

Tracker/design delivery only. Applying repository/account settings or replacing the guide policy requires the resulting concrete decision and an explicitly scoped follow-up. No product, installation or device work.

title: Retire ended monitoring sessions consistently across Codex and Claude
body:
## Outcome

Apply one shared-owner retirement rule to every currently supported provider/client: Codex Desktop (`codex`/`desktop`), Codex CLI (`codex`/`cli`) and Claude Code (`claude`/`code`). An accepted `runtime.ended` removes the known session and its known descendants in one durable update. Consumers reconcile the resulting snapshot.

User-approved planning, September 24, 2026. This extends [Hub #218](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/218), whose active delivery remains Codex Desktop only. It removes the policy exception that would otherwise let an ended Claude or CLI record hold [Nanoleaf #110](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/110) in Work until expiry.

## Owner policy

- Reuse #218's atomic retirement, bounded delayed-event guards, fresh record generations and known-descendant handling. The shared owner interprets provider lifecycle evidence once; devices do not add their own end filters or timers.
- An accepted end retires monitoring even when notices or attention remain. This may discard task labels, task-project overrides, Line placement and animation state, as already accepted in #218. It does not acknowledge, mark read, report success, cancel work or terminate agents. Preserve unrelated sessions, global settings and device reservations.
- Ordinary `Stop`/`turn.ended`, `SubagentStop`, interruption, waiting, completed/read status and five-minute freshness uncertainty do not become session ends. Completed and waiting records remain until an accepted runtime end or their existing evidence expiry.
- Preserve the 24-hour fallback for absent/lost ends, using each record's evidence clock. Turn duration alone does not imply an end; add no universal 30-minute timer. A real run with no accepted lifecycle evidence for 24 hours can still expire.
- Qualify the end/start mappings for each supported path, including provider-specific exit, clear/switch and resume behavior where applicable. Missing or unqualified end evidence is a coverage gap, not an invented end. Keep hooks bounded, metadata-only and fail-open.
- An eligible new start after retirement creates a fresh record without old-effect replay. Preserve known identity/order protections across restart and missed consumer snapshots, and document their existing limits. Read evidence alone cannot recreate a record. Keep the Codex Desktop archive admission safeguard specific to that client.

## Bounded implementation

Generalize the owner path delivered by #218 and reuse its fixtures and consumer checks. Change a consumer only for a demonstrated gap. No new service, policy registry, provider watcher, historical event replay, cleanup UI or per-device cleanup command. Do not add new provider families or change native modes here.

Assess compatibility and the upgrade behavior of already-retained records using stored evidence; never infer an old end from idle/unknown activity or scan transcripts. Records without sufficient end evidence retain the existing expiry fallback. Document this transition without resetting evidence clocks or live databases.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Parameterized owner/provider checks cover Codex Desktop, Codex CLI and Claude Code. An accepted known end atomically removes the record and known descendants, releases capacity and publishes one revision; unknown/repeated ends create nothing.
- [ ] Mixed-provider checks preserve unrelated records. Ending one provider's last session cannot remove another provider's session, and no ended record survives merely because it is Claude or CLI.
- [ ] Completion, waiting, interruption, read/acknowledgment, child turn completion, freshness uncertainty and turns over 30 minutes retain their existing semantics. Fake-clock checks preserve the separate 24-hour fallback.
- [ ] Reuse focused delayed-event, fresh resume, recognizable old-end, restart, child-admission and missed-retirement checks for the newly covered paths; preserve #218's unknown-ordering and bounded-history limits.
- [ ] Existing Nanoleaf, Tidbyt, Pixoo and dashboard checks confirm snapshot removal/fresh recreation without provider-specific cleanup. Preserve unavailable-feed handling, queues, native modes and each display's cadence.
- [ ] Record provider mapping evidence and remaining installed-path gaps. Update the issue-linked OpenSpec change, lifecycle/state requirements, affected package/provider/setup guidance, compatibility assessment and applicable validation during implementation.
- [ ] Document upgrade treatment of previously retained records and verify it with a legacy-state fixture; no fabricated end, acknowledgment, clock reset or old-effect replay.

## Verification and delivery target

Source-only. Extend existing fake-clock, provider, owner, persistence and consumer fixtures; run applicable repository checks. Synthetic events establish source behavior, not delivery from an installed client. Separately authorized installed qualification should observe a normal end and resume for each newly adopted CLI/Claude path, recording emitted events and owner removal/recreation. Named-device permission is required for any visible-light check; repeating every device's full hardware qualification is unnecessary.

#218 retains its installed Desktop acceptance, including reopen-to-read. This issue supplies owner removal to #110; it does not implement Work/Free automation or depend on #110.

## Dependencies and next action

- **Blocked by [Hub #218](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/218)**. Reuse its delivered retirement contract and consumer generation handling rather than expanding its active PRs.
- [Nanoleaf #110](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/110) must validate the consistent owner policy before claiming automatic Work/Free behavior across supported providers.

Backlog/blocked. After #218 is delivered, prepare the issue-linked OpenSpec change and focused provider qualification/tests. This planning update authorizes tracker changes only, not implementation, installation, settings changes, agent launches or device operations.

title: Qualify and add Sony HT-A9 play/resume when supported
body:

This tracker entry does not authorize installation or live device control.

title: Bound browser-session resources and centralize retirement cleanup
body:
## Outcome and real setup

Repeatedly opening and closing BUNNY on the single-operator Linux/WSL hub releases each retired browser session's resources. Existing launcher, dashboard, HTTP and MCP access continue to work.

Source inspection at main `28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17` found that monitor reads allocate a principal ledger, while browser expiry, eviction and logout remove credentials without retiring that ledger. The 16-session cap therefore does not bound ledger entries across launches. This is a source finding; retained bytes and real-world memory growth have not been measured. See [ledger creation](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17/apps/hub/src/server.ts#L100-L140) and [launch/logout](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17/apps/hub/src/server.ts#L218-L238).

## Smallest useful implementation

Keep the change inside the hub. Give browser-session resources one local lifecycle owner, using the existing maps where practical. Expiry, oldest-session eviction, logout, credential replacement and shutdown use one idempotent retirement path for credentials, streams and replay accounting. Retired sessions cannot admit new work; already admitted work stays tracked until settlement and is then released. Do not create a new service or persistent session store.

Required issue prerequisites: none open. The launcher from https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/179 is delivered. Coordinate overlapping stream/server edits with https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/222; that is shared-file coordination, not a blocker. General memory profiling remains https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/123.

Planning assessment, 2026-09-24: complexity **medium** (session, stream and replay lifetimes); uncertainty **low** for the retention path, with exact cleanup scheduling to establish in focused tests; impact **high** because authorization and replay must remain correct. **Ready for a separately requested delivery.** Refresh this assessment if authentication, admission or stream ownership changes.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Keep current browser scope/alias limits, configured machine credentials, Host/Origin checks, authentication before replay, request identities, restart epochs, byte/entry limits and the rule that pending work cannot be evicted to admit more work. Retiring a browser session does not undo a submitted command, retry it, quiesce agent state or change a device writer. No credentials or private state enter test receipts.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: **source-only**.

- [ ] A focused regression covers repeated launch -> monitor read -> logout, expiry and oldest-session eviction. Session/ledger counts and replay accounting return to a documented bound after cleanup; no public diagnostics endpoint is needed. The existing repeat-launch test alone is insufficient because it does not read monitor sessions.
- [ ] Retirement closes that browser principal's streams and rejects its token and cached requests. Another browser session and configured HTTP/MCP principal remain usable. Logging out of a dashboard opened with a manually entered configured credential must not revoke that credential or reset its replay identity: reconnecting with it cannot execute an old request again. Verify both credential kinds with disposable-host authentication, replay and stream tests.
- [ ] A controlled pending command survives retirement without another execution or false cancellation. Its accounting remains charged until settlement and is then released; repeated retirement cannot double-release it. Verify with a deferred fake operation, including rejection and timeout paths.
- [ ] Preserve launcher, replay/revocation and restart tests. On Node 24, run `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:hub`, `npm run test:hub:package`, `npm run test:hub:mcp` and `npm run test:dashboard:browser`, plus the shared suites required by AGENTS.md and docs/development.md. These are planned checks, not results.
- [ ] Prepare the issue-linked OpenSpec lifecycle/concurrency design at pickup. Follow docs/sdlc.md for independent Standards/Specification review, applicable CI and merged-revision readback. The PR walkthrough explains resource ownership, duplicate/restart behavior and the pending-retirement test; review explicitly covers authorization and replay.

## Meaningful deferrals

Process-wide profiling and performance-budget changes stay in #123; this issue proves bounded resource ownership, not an RSS improvement. Multi-operator or remote sessions are outside the selected setup and trigger reassessment if introduced. Installation and live-device trials require a separate request; source evidence does not update the installed hub.

title: Share the dashboard command lifecycle between forms and actions
body:
## Outcome and real setup

BUNNY's existing forms and one-click actions use one command lifecycle, so fixes to receipt handling, uncertainty and refresh ordering apply consistently. Preserve the current single-operator dashboard and its configured Pixoo/Nanoleaf controls, session labels and acknowledgments.

At main `28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17`, [useCommand and EditForm](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17/apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx#L47-L98) separately maintain submission, receipt tracking, busy/locked state and refresh ordering. Both changed in [PR #239](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/pull/239). This is maintenance work that preserves that delivered behavior.

## Smallest useful implementation

Use one dashboard-local hook or reducer for the shared lifecycle, reusing `resultMessage`, `failureMessage`, `observedResult` and the focus helper. Forms retain draft values and configuration-revision conflicts; action buttons retain command preparation. Keep device-specific request construction and availability rules with their callers. Remove the duplicated orchestration after both callers use the common implementation; moving functions to separate files alone does not satisfy the outcome.

Required issue prerequisites: none open. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/231 is delivered behavior to preserve. Coordinate `apps/dashboard` edits with https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/182; skin work is independent and is not a blocker. Prefer https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/244 before this work, then integration-contract consolidation; this is a preferred order, not a source dependency.

Planning assessment, 2026-09-24: complexity **medium** (two interaction models and asynchronous observations); uncertainty **low** (existing implementations and browser scenarios define the behavior); impact **high** because a lifecycle mistake could allow a duplicate or incorrectly guarded device command. **Ready for a separately requested delivery.** Reassess after command-policy or dashboard changes.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Preserve fresh guards immediately before device submission, configuration-revision draft conflicts, generation-only advances, one explicit submission, no automatic retry, accepted-ticket-only receipt tracking, editable rejected drafts, and locks for uncertain/partial results until explicit reload. Keep mode-specific controls, memory-only credentials, scope checks, focus restoration and no-write inspection. Transport acceptance never establishes physical output. Keep existing wording and layout unless an additional change is explicitly scoped.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: **source-only**.

- [ ] Both `useCommand` and `EditForm` delegate shared transitions to one implementation. Code review identifies the removed duplicate logic and confirms that draft rules and device commands remain explicit at their existing boundaries.
- [ ] Focused transition tests cover prepare-blocked, accepted/queued, definite rejection, uncertain/partial, matching terminal receipt and explicit reload. A rejected ticket cannot adopt another client's receipt; no transition resubmits a command. Exercise both form and action consumers.
- [ ] Cover a preparation failure before submission and a failed refresh after a command result. Preparation failure sends no write; refresh failure preserves the original receipt/effect evidence and does not imply that nothing was sent. Neither path leaves the control permanently busy or retries automatically. Recovery must obtain current guards before another explicit device submission. Use controlled rejected promises and stale-read responses for both consumers.
- [ ] Preserve the browser matrix for fresh guards, generation races, successive power/brightness changes, retained drafts, mode reapply, Start Monitor, terminal outcomes, reconnect, focus and accessibility. Confirm each deliberate activation sends at most one write and passive reads send none.
- [ ] On Node 24, run `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build:dashboard`, `npm run typecheck:dashboard`, `npm run test:dashboard` and `npm run test:dashboard:browser`, plus the shared hub/contract/workflow checks required by AGENTS.md and docs/development.md. Keep useful lower-level and browser tests. These are planned checks, not results.
- [ ] At pickup, record the issue-linked OpenSpec treatment under docs/sdlc.md; lifecycle/concurrency design must cover ordering and recovery even though intended behavior is unchanged. Preserve independent Standards/Specification review, applicable CI and merged-revision readback. Apply the existing human approval requirement to any changed UI candidate. The PR walkthrough traces one accepted command and one uncertain command through the shared lifecycle.

## Meaningful deferrals

Visual restyling belongs to #182; this issue provides no new skin or controls. A framework-wide form system and generic device action engine have no current requirement and are excluded; revisit only if another real caller cannot use the bounded helper. Installation and physical acceptance remain separately authorized; fake/browser checks establish source behavior only.

title: Consolidate duplicated Pixoo and Nanoleaf integration-contract definitions
body:
## Outcome and real setup

Reduce the places that must change when an existing Pixoo or Nanoleaf integration contract changes, while retaining both native protocols. The affected consumers are the single-operator hub's controller client, MCP tool definitions and dashboard. No new controller or wire version is requested.

At main `28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17`, protocol facts recur in [MCP schemas](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17/apps/hub/src/mcp.ts#L69-L83), hub validators, and [dashboard types/builders](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17/apps/dashboard/src/main.tsx#L8-L25). [The pinned Nanoleaf contract](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/28f759956eda24498d638392e1175b6d64c04d17/apps/hub/src/vendor/nanoleaf-integration.ts#L1-L13) already exports reusable types. Duplication is established; a current compatibility failure has not been demonstrated.

## Smallest useful implementation

Start with a short contract/caller map in this issue: list duplicated declarations, their authoritative owner, intentional transport projections and actual imports. Identify the declarations that can be removed and the checks that show callers still accept/reject the same inputs. Use that map to settle the smallest browser-safe local module arrangement before implementation.

Then reuse owner-supplied types and consolidate shared facts per extension for the hub validators, MCP schema projections and dashboard request builders. Keep protocol-specific projections explicit and preserve validation at each trust boundary. Use existing packaging and build facilities; do not add a plugin system, schema framework, new distributable package or cross-repository migration merely for this refactor. Preserve the reviewed vendor bytes and provenance rather than editing an upstream-owned copy in place.

Required issue prerequisites: none open. Coordinate overlapping dashboard command work and any owner-contract revision at pickup. https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/25 and https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/26 own deferred source migrations and do not block local reuse. Prefer https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/244, then https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/245, then this work to reduce overlapping edits; that order is not a dependency.

Planning assessment, 2026-09-24: complexity **medium** (three consumers and two protocols); uncertainty **medium** (the reusable declarations and browser/package boundary need the map above); impact **high** because validation or guard drift can change admitted device commands. **Backlog.** Next action: complete the bounded map and update this assessment to ready when it shows a concrete reduction without changing accepted contracts. If a candidate declaration must differ by boundary, retain it and explain why. Reassess on upstream pin, wire or packaging changes.

## Behavior and protections to preserve

Retain native API versions, different string/object request tickets, revision/generation meanings, configured target binding, strict unknown-field rejection, limits, mode semantics and configuration-versus-physical outcomes. Preserve HTTP/MCP authorization and ambiguous-write handling. Browser imports must not pull in Node transport, credential access or private configuration. Pixoo and Nanoleaf keep source and device-writer ownership.

## Observable acceptance and planned evidence

Delivery target: **source-only**; readiness mapping comes before implementation. If the map finds no worthwhile consolidation that preserves the native boundaries, record the evidence and recommend closing without implementation. Do not force an abstraction to satisfy this issue. The implementation criteria below apply only when the map establishes a useful change.

- [ ] The map names each shared declaration's owner, callers, removed duplicate and any intentional projection. Review shows fewer independently maintained protocol facts, with no new wire acceptance or capability claim.
- [ ] The selected local definitions serve the current hub, MCP and dashboard callers. Type/build checks cover browser compatibility and installed hub packaging; source inspection confirms no dependency on device-application internals or Node-only code in the browser.
- [ ] Preserve vendor checksums and native fixture coverage. Feed relevant valid and invalid native requests through the MCP projection and owning validator, accounting for documented projections. Cover tickets, bounds, unknown/private fields, target binding and differing native receipt semantics; keep semantic validation that a schema cannot express.
- [ ] Preserve dashboard request guards and HTTP/MCP outcomes. On Node 24, run `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:hub`, `npm run test:hub:mcp`, `npm run test:hub:package`, `npm run test:dashboard` and `npm run test:dashboard:browser`, plus shared contract/MCP/workflow checks required by AGENTS.md and docs/development.md. Use the documented pinned owning-service checks for affected native boundaries. These are planned checks, not results.
- [ ] At pickup, record the issue-linked OpenSpec treatment for this intended behavior-preserving refactor. Any necessary wire or capability change requires reassessment before implementation. Follow docs/sdlc.md for independent Standards/Specification review, applicable CI, conditional UI approval and merged-revision readback; review explicitly covers protocol compatibility and package contents.

## Meaningful deferrals

Source migrations remain in #25/#26; consumers continue using pinned owner contracts. A universal controller protocol and broad code generation have no demonstrated benefit here and are excluded; revisit only with a concrete new consumer requirement. No measured speed or memory improvement is claimed. Installation and device trials require a separate request.
